question.explanation: Age is a multiple of <math><mn>7</mn></math> and is <math><mn>1</mn></math> more than a multiple of <math><mtext>lcm</mtext><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>. Values: <math><mn>13</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>37</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>61</mn></math>; multiple of <math><mn>7</mn></math> is <math><mn>49</mn></math>.

question.question: Given the recursive function <math><mi>f</mi></math> on <math>{0,1,2,\dots}\times{0,1,2,3,4}</math> with <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn> </math> (mod <math>5</math>), and for <math><mi>i</mi>\ge1</math>: <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo></math> for <math>1\le j\le4</math>. Find <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2015</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Tabulation shows stabilization with <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> for all <math><mi>i</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></math>; hence <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2015</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: A point <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is chosen uniformly from <math><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>8</mn></math>, <math><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. What is <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>?
question.explanation: Feasible region is a right triangle of area <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> inside rectangle area <math><mn>32</mn></math>. Probability <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>32</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Two runners start at <math><mi>O</mi></math> on a straight track and run in the same direction; runner <math><mi>B</mi></math> is three times as fast as <math><mi>A</mi></math>. An observer at point <math><mi>P</mi></math> off the track so that <math><mover><mi>OP</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> is perpendicular to the track watches the angle <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi></math>. What is the maximum value (in degrees) of <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Let <math><mi>OP</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>OA</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></math>, <math><mi>OB</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></math>. Then <math><mo>tan</mo><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></math>, maximized when <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></math> is minimized by AM–GM at <math><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></math>, giving <math><mo>tan</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mfrac></math> so <math><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: The quadratic <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2.6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3.6</mn></math> can be written as <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo><sup>2</sup><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math>. What is <math><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Complete the square: <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1.3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1.91</mn></math>, so <math><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3.21</mn></math>.

question.question: The product of two consecutive positive even integers is <math><mn>288</mn></math>. What is the greater integer?
question.explanation: Let integers be <math><mi>n</mi></math> and <math><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math>; solve <math><mi>n</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>288</mn></math> to get <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>, greater is <math><mn>18</mn></math>.

question.question: What is the probability that a randomly selected integer from <math><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo>⋯<mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>}</mo></math> is divisible by <math><mn>2</mn></math> and not divisible by <math><mn>3</mn></math>?
question.explanation: There are 50 evens; 16 are multiples of 6, leaving 34 that are even and not multiples of 3. Probability <math><mfrac><mn>34</mn><mn>100</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>17</mn><mn>50</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: A bookcase has 3 shelves with 24 books: top 8 mystery, middle 10 math, bottom 6 science. Two books are removed from each shelf. What fraction of the remaining books are math?
question.explanation: Remaining books: <math><mn>24</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn></math>; math remaining: <math><mn>10</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>. Fraction <math><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>18</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: The volume of a cone is given by <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>B</mi><mi>h</mi></math>. If the base area is <math><mn>30</mn></math> square units and the height is <math><mn>6.5</mn></math> units, what is the volume?
question.explanation: Compute <math>\tfrac{1}{3}\cdot30\cdot6.5=10\cdot6.5=65</math> cubic units.

question.question: The curves <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></math> and <math><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>44</mn></math> intersect at four points. What is the product of the <math><mi>y</mi></math>-coordinates of all intersection points?
question.explanation: Setting <math><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> gives <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. The four <math><mi>y</mi></math>-values multiply to <math><mn>8</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1736</mn></math>.

question.question: Louis eats <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math> of a pie and Jack eats <math><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>. How much of the pie do they eat altogether?
question.explanation: Common denominator <math><mn>15</mn></math>: <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>15</mn></mfrac></math>, <math><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>10</mn><mn>15</mn></mfrac></math>; sum <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>13</mn><mn>15</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: In an arithmetic sequence, the 4th term is <math><mn>200</mn></math> and the 8th term is <math><mn>500</mn></math>. What is the 6th term?
question.explanation: The 6th term is the average of the 4th and 8th terms: <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>200</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>500</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>350</mn></math>.

question.question: Consider the geometric series <math><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mi>a</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>36</mn><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mo>⋯</mo></math> with positive integer <math><mi>a</mi></math>. If the sum is a perfect square, what is the smallest possible <math><mi>a</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Sum <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mi>a</mi></mfrac></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>. For a square, smallest working <math><mi>a</mi></math> is <math><mn>4</mn></math>: sum <math><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>.

question.question: How many <math><mi>y</mi></math>-intercepts does the parabola <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> have?
question.explanation: Set <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>: solve <math><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Discriminant <math><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> two real <math><mi>y</mi></math>-values.

question.question: If integers <math><mi>m</mi></math>, <math><mi>n</mi></math> satisfy <math><mn>3</mn><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></math>, what is the smallest possible value of <math>|m-n|</math>?
question.explanation: Seeking <math><mn>7</mn><mi>m</mi></math> closest to <math><mn>100</mn></math> under the constraint; solution <math><mo>(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>)</mo></math> gives <math><mo>|</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> (minimal).

question.question: Convert <math><mfrac><mn>21</mn><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>·</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>7</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></math> to a terminating decimal.
question.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by <math><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></math> to get denominator <math><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>7</mn></msup></math>: <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>21</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>7</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>672</mn><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>7</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0000672</mn></math>.

question.question: In the configuration of four mutually tangent unit circles inside triangle ABC with centers P, Q, R, S as shown, what is the degree measure of the smallest angle of triangle PQS?
question.explanation: Tangency gives <math><mi>QR</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>RS</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>PR</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>PS</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, so <math><mo>△</mo><mi>PRS</mi></math> is equilateral (<math><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math>). Then <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>PQR</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math> and <math><mo>△</mo><mi>PQS</mi></math> is <math><mn>30</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>90</mn></math>, so the smallest angle is <math><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: Find the equation of the plane through <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, and <math><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> in the form <math><mi>A</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> with integer coefficients and <math><mi>A</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Using <math><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">a</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>×</mo><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">c</mi><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="bold">a</mi><mo>)</mo></math> gives a normal proportional to <math><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>)</mo></math>; plugging in a point yields <math><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>11</mn><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Choice D is a non-primitive multiple.

question.question: How many two-digit positive integers are factors of both <math><mn>100</mn></math> and <math><mn>150</mn></math>?
question.explanation: Common divisors of 100 and 150 that are two-digit: <math><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn></math> — three numbers.

question.question: Simplify and rationalize: <math><msqrt><mroot><msqrt><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>729</mn></mfrac></msqrt><mn>3</mn></mroot></msqrt></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mn>729</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></math>. Inside-out: <math><msqrt><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>729</mn></mfrac></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>27</mn></mfrac></math>, cube root <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>, square root <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Two-thirds of the students at a school take music; that number is <math><mn>834</mn></math>. How many students are at the school?
question.explanation: Let total be <math><mi>S</mi></math>. <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>834</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>834</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1251</mn></math>.

question.question: Write <math><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></math> in the form <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><mi>c</mi></mfrac></math> with positive integers <math><mi>a</mi>,<mi>b</mi>,<mi>c</mi></math> and minimal <math><mi>c</mi></math>. Find <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Common denominator <math><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></math> gives <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></mfrac></math>; rationalize to <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math>, so <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>23</mn></math>.

question.question: For positive real numbers <math><mi>a</mi>,<mi>b</mi>,<mi>c</mi></math>, find the set of all possible values of <math><mfrac><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: By AM-GM, <math><mi>S</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≥</mo><mn>3</mn></math> with no equality (since <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mi>c</mi></mfrac><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></math>), so <math><mi>S</mi><mo>></mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Achievable arbitrarily close to 2 and unbounded above: set <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math>, vary <math><mi>b</mi></math>.

question.question: Find <math><mi>k</mi></math> if <math><msup><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></math>.
question.explanation: Left side is <math><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></math>; equate exponents: <math><mn>6</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: For how many integers <math><mi>n</mi></math> with <math><mi>n</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></math> is <math><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>24</mn></msup></math> a perfect <math><mi>n</mi></math>-th power?
question.explanation: <math><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>24</mn></msup></math> is an <math><mi>n</mi></math>-th power iff <math><mi>n</mi></math> divides 24. Divisors <math><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></math>: <math><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>24</mn></math> (7 values).

question.question: Hillary has eleven coins, all dimes and nickels. In total, the coins are worth 75 cents. How many nickels does she have?
question.explanation: Let dimes be <math><mi>d</mi></math> and nickels be <math><mi>n</mi></math>. Then <math><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></math> and <math><mn>10</mn><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>75</mn></math>. Divide the value equation by <math><mn>5</mn></math>: <math><mn>2</mn><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math>. Substitute <math><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi></math> to get <math><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math> so <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>.

question.question: Find the largest <math><mi>x</mi></math>-value where the graphs of <math><mi>f</mi>(<mi>x</mi>)</math> and <math><mi>g</mi>(<mi>x</mi>)</math> intersect, given that their difference simplifies to <math><mi>g</mi>(<mi>x</mi>)−<mi>f</mi>(<mi>x</mi>)<mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Intersections satisfy <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math> so <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Factor: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. The real roots are <math><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn></math>; largest is <math><mn>6</mn></math>.

question.question: Paul and Jesse each choose a number uniformly at random from the first six primes. What is the probability that their sum is even?
question.explanation: Sum is odd iff one picks <math><mn>2</mn></math> and the other an odd prime: <math><mn>10</mn></math> favorable of <math><mn>36</mn></math> total, probability <math><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>18</mn></mfrac></math>. Thus even-sum probability <math><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>18</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>13</mn><mn>18</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: The point <math><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></math> lies on <math><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>. When <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, what is <math><mi>b</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Substitute <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>: <math><mn>3</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math> so <math><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.

question.question: For a polynomial <math><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> with integer coefficients, how many different possible rational roots can it have?
question.explanation: By the Rational Root Theorem, possible roots are <math><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>±</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>: four possibilities.

question.question: Find the maximum value of <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> over all real numbers <math><mi>x</mi></math>, <math><mi>y</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Let <math><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></math> so numerator becomes <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi></math>. AM–GM: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></math>, <math><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>z</mi></math>, hence denominator <math><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></math>. So the expression <math><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>, with equality at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>p</mi>(<mi>x</mi>)</math> be a monic quartic with roots <math>1,2,3</math> and another real number <math><mi>r</mi></math>. Compute <math><mi>p</mi>(<mn>0</mn>)<mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi>(<mn>4</mn>)</math>.
question.explanation: Write <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></math>. Then <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>r</mi></math> and <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>r</mi></math>. Sum is <math><mn>24</mn></math>.

question.question: Evaluate <math><mn>441</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>)(</mo><mn>19</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>361</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Note <math><mn>441</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>21</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></math> and <math><mn>361</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>19</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. Expression equals <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>19</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>40</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1600</mn></math>.

question.question: If <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> is a positive factor of <math><mn>10</mn><mo>!</mo></math>, how many possible integer values of <math><mi>x</mi></math> are there?
question.explanation: Prime form: <math><mn>10</mn><mo>!</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mn>7</mn></math>. For <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>∣</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>!</mo></math>, exponents in <math><mi>x</mi></math> satisfy <math><mn>3</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, others zero. So <math><mi>a</mi><mo>∈</mo><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>}</mo></math> and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>}</mo></math>, giving <math><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> values.

question.question: In how many ways can 6 girls and 2 boys sit in a row if the 2 boys must sit next to each other?
question.explanation: Treat the boys as a block: <math><mn>7</mn><mo>!</mo></math> ways to arrange blocks, and <math><mn>2</mn><mo>!</mo></math> ways to order the boys: <math><mn>7</mn><mo>!</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>!</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>10080</mn></math>.

question.question: The arithmetic mean of <math><mn>7</mn></math>, <math><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mi>x</mi></math>, and <math><mn>10</mn></math> is <math><mn>9</mn></math>. Find <math><mi>x</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Sum must be <math><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn></math>.

question.question: If <math><mn>4</mn></math> daps <math><mo>=</mo></math> <math><mn>7</mn></math> yaps and <math><mn>5</mn></math> yaps <math><mo>=</mo></math> <math><mn>3</mn></math> baps, how many daps equal <math><mn>42</mn></math> baps?
question.explanation: <math><mn>5</mn></math> yaps <math><mo>=</mo></math> <math><mn>3</mn></math> baps <math><mo>→</mo></math> <math><mn>70</mn></math> yaps <math><mo>=</mo></math> <math><mn>42</mn></math> baps. Also <math><mn>4</mn></math> daps <math><mo>=</mo></math> <math><mn>7</mn></math> yaps <math><mo>→</mo></math> <math><mn>40</mn></math> daps <math><mo>=</mo></math> <math><mn>70</mn></math> yaps.

question.question: A group of <math><mi>N</mi></math> students (<math><mi>N</mi><mo><</mo><mn>50</mn></math>) leaves remainders 5 when grouped by 8 and 3 when grouped by 6. What is the sum of all possible values of <math><mi>N</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Solve <math><mi>N</mi><mo>≡</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mo>(</mo><mtext>mod</mtext><mo> </mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mi>N</mi><mo>≡</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mo>(</mo><mtext>mod</mtext><mo> </mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Solutions: <math><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>24</mn><mi>k</mi></math>. Under 50: <math><mn>21</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>45</mn></math>. Sum <math><mn>66</mn></math>.

question.question: Alice wins on heads on her turns; Bob wins on tails on his turns. Alice goes first; fair coin each flip. What is the probability Alice wins?
question.explanation: Sum geometric: <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>32</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mo>⋯</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Find the remainder when <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>611</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>11</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>11</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> is divided by <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Use Remainder Theorem at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math>: <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>611</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>11</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>.

question.question: Let distinct complex numbers <math><mi>a</mi>,<mi>b</mi>,<mi>c</mi>,<mi>d</mi></math> satisfy <math>|a|=|b|=|c|=|d|=1</math> and <math>a+b+c+d=0</math>. Find the maximum value of <math>|(a+b)(a+c)(a+d)(b+c)(b+d)(c+d)|</math>.
question.explanation: From <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mo>|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> one gets a reciprocal-symmetric quartic, implying some pair sums to zero; thus one factor vanishes and the product's absolute value is <math><mn>0</mn></math> (maximum is <math><mn>0</mn></math>).

question.question: Given a matrix <math><mi mathvariant="bold">A</mi></math> with <math><mi mathvariant="bold">A</mi><mfenced><mtable><mtr><mtd><mn>3</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mtable><mtr><mtd><mn>2</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>4</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced></math> and <math><mi mathvariant="bold">A</mi><mfenced><mtable><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>2</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>2</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mtable><mtr><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced></math>, find <math><mi mathvariant="bold">A</mi><mfenced><mtable><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>13</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>3</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>4</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced></math>.
question.explanation: Linearity: subtract to get <math><mi mathvariant="bold">A</mi><mfenced><mtable><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>2</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mtable><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced></math>, then add with the second relation to reach <math><mi mathvariant="bold">A</mi><mfenced><mtable><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>13</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>3</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>4</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mtable><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>14</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced></math>.

question.question: A line is parameterized by <math><mfenced><mtable><mtr><mtd><mi>x</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mi>y</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mtable><mtr><mtd><mn>8</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi><mfenced><mtable><mtr><mtd><mn>2</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>3</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced></math>. Write it as <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></math>. What is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></math>?
question.explanation: From <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>t</mi></math>, <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>13</mn></math>, so <math><mo>(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: Mikka wants to order a pizza with two different toppings. He has 8 different toppings to choose from. How many different pizzas could he order?
question.explanation: Choose 2 of 8 toppings: <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0"><mn>8</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>28</mn></math>.

question.question: How many of the first one hundred positive integers are divisible by <math><mn>3</mn></math>, <math><mn>4</mn></math>, and <math><mn>5</mn></math>?
question.explanation: Numbers divisible by all three are multiples of <math><mtext>lcm</mtext><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></math>. In <math><mo>[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>]</mo></math> only <math><mn>60</mn></math> qualifies, so the count is <math><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: Frank answered <math><mn>80</mn></math> questions on a 100-question test. Correct answers score <math><mn>5</mn></math>, incorrect score <math><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, blanks score <math><mn>0</mn></math>. If his total score is <math><mn>232</mn></math>, how many did he answer correctly?
question.explanation: Let correct <math><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math>, incorrect <math><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi></math>. Then <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn></math>, <math><mn>5</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>232</mn></math>. Substitute <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi></math>: <math><mn>5</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>80</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>232</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>56</mn></math>.

question.question: Compute <math><mrow><mo>∑</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>^</mo><mo>∞</mo></mrow><mfrac><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>·</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></math>, where <math><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>n</mn></msub></math> are Fibonacci numbers with <math><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, <math><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Since <math><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></math>, term <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mfrac></math>. Telescopes to <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: In a school of <math><mn>360</mn></math> students: <math><mn>180</mn></math> take calculus; twice as many take chemistry as physics; <math><mn>75</mn></math> take both calculus and chemistry; <math><mn>75</mn></math> take both physics and chemistry; <math><mn>30</mn></math> take both physics and calculus; <math><mn>15</mn></math> take all three; <math><mn>15</mn></math> take none. How many take physics?
question.explanation: Let physics be <math><mi>x</mi></math>, chemistry <math><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></math>. Using pairwise counts minus triple and summing disjoint regions to <math><mn>360</mn></math> yields <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>110</mn></math>.

question.question: If <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, compute <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.
question.explanation: From <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, then <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. So <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: In Ink: <math><mn>1</mn></math> Trinket <math><mo>=</mo></math> <math><mn>4</mn></math> Blinkets and <math><mn>3</mn></math> Blinkets <math><mo>=</mo></math> <math><mn>7</mn></math> Drinkets. In Trinkets, what is the value of <math><mn>56</mn></math> Drinkets?
question.explanation: From <math><mn>3</mn></math> Blinkets <math><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math> Drinkets, multiply by <math><mn>8</mn></math> to get <math><mn>24</mn></math> Blinkets <math><mo>=</mo><mn>56</mn></math> Drinkets. Since <math><mn>4</mn></math> Blinkets <math><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> Trinket, <math><mn>24</mn></math> Blinkets <math><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> Trinkets.

question.question: Find the midpoint of the line segment between <math><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Enter your answer as an ordered pair.
question.explanation: Midpoint formula: <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: What is the smallest positive multiple of 450 whose digits are all zeroes and ones?
question.explanation: Divisibility by <math><mn>50</mn></math> forces the number to end with <math><mn>00</mn></math>. Divisibility by <math><mn>9</mn></math> requires the digit sum to be a multiple of <math><mn>9</mn></math>, so we need at least nine 1s. The smallest such number is <math><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>00</mn></math> (i.e., <math><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>111</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn></math>), which is divisible by both <math><mn>9</mn></math> and <math><mn>50</mn></math>, hence by <math><mn>450</mn></math>.

question.question: A wheel is spun twice. The first result is reduced mod <math>4</math> to get a column (remainders <math>1,2,3</math>), and the second result is reduced mod <math>5</math> to get a row (remainders <math>1,2,3,4</math>) on a checkerboard with alternating shading. What is the probability the checker lands on a shaded square?
question.explanation: Parity of remainders is independent. First remainder even with probability <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>, odd with <math><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>; second even with <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>, odd with <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. Shaded when parities match: <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Sam carries a <math><mn>2</mn></math>-gallon bucket of milk for <math><mn>3</mn></math> miles. Each mile leaves <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> of the milk from the start of that mile. How many gallons are left when he gets home?
question.explanation: Amount left: <math><mn>2</mn><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>27</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>16</mn><mn>27</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: The product of <math>240</math> and <math>k</math> is a perfect cube. What is the smallest positive <math>k</math>?
question.explanation: Prime factorization: <math><mn>240</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. To make exponents multiples of <math><mn>3</mn></math>, multiply by <math><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>900</mn></math>.

question.question: In triangle <math><mi>ABC</mi></math>, with <math><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>∥</mo><mover><mi>DE</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> and <math><mi>BD</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>BC</mi></math>, if the area of <math><mo>△</mo><mi>ABC</mi></math> is <math><mn>6</mn></math> cm<math><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, find the area of <math><mo>△</mo><mi>CDE</mi></math>.
question.explanation: With <math><mi>AB</mi><mo>∥</mo><mi>DE</mi></math>, triangles are similar. Since <math><mi>BD</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>BC</mi></math>, we get <math><mi>CD</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>BC</mi></math> and the linear scale factor <math><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, so area scale is <math><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. Thus <math><mo>[</mo><mo>△</mo><mi>CDE</mi><mo>]</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>54</mn></math>.

question.question: What is the sum of the digits of <math><mfrac><mn>4321</mn><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></math> written as a terminating decimal?
question.explanation: Convert to denominator <math><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup></math>: multiply numerator by <math><mn>5</mn></math>. Decimal is <math><mn>0.00021605</mn></math>; digit sum <math><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></math>.

question.question: Compute <math><mi>sin</mi><mn>20</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>40</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>80</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>100</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>120</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>140</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>160</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Using symmetries <math><mi>sin</mi><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>120</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> and identities to pair terms yields value <math><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>256</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: For a constant <math><mi>c</mi></math>, in cylindrical coordinates <math><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></math>, find the shape described by the equation <math><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi></math>.
question.explanation: In cylindrical coordinates, <math><mi>z</mi></math> is the vertical coordinate. The locus <math><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi></math> is the horizontal plane parallel to the <math><mi>xy</mi></math>-plane.

question.question: Given <math>a+b+c+d+e=8</math> and <math>a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2+e^2=16</math>, find the maximum value of <math>e</math>.
question.explanation: By Cauchy–Schwarz: <math><mn>4</mn><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo><mo>≥</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. With sums this gives <math><mn>4</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo><mo>≥</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>16</mn><mi>e</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>e</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>16</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math>. Equality when <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: The average of Amy’s, Ben’s, and Chris’s ages is 6. Four years ago, Chris was Amy’s current age. In four years, Ben’s age will be <math><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math> of Amy’s age then. How old is Chris now?
question.explanation: Let ages be <math><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></math>. Then <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math>, and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Solve to get <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>.

question.question: If <math><msup><mi>ω</mi><mn>1997</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mi>ω</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, evaluate <math><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>1997</mn></munderover><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: Pair terms: <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mn>1997</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. There are <math><mn>998</mn></math> pairs plus <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mn>1997</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. Sum <math><mo>=</mo><mn>998</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1997</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>49</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>623</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2015</mn></math> and <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Compute the sum of the roots of <math><mi>g</mi></math>.
question.explanation: If roots of <math><mi>f</mi></math> sum to <math><mn>49</mn></math>, the roots of <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math> are each shifted left by <math><mn>5</mn></math>, so new sum <math><mo>=</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>34</mn></math>.

question.question: Compute <math><mn>0.</mn><mover><mn>7</mn><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>−</mo><mn>0.</mn><mover><mn>4</mn><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>0.</mn><mover><mn>2</mn><mo>¯</mo></mover></math>. Express your answer as a common fraction.
question.explanation: Use <math><mn>0.</mn><mover><mi>n</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>n</mi><mn>9</mn></mfrac></math>. Then <math><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: If <math><mi>x</mi></math>, <math><mi>y</mi></math>, and <math><mi>z</mi></math> are positive with <math><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>, <math><mi>x</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>48</mn></math>, and <math><mi>y</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>72</mn></math>, then find <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Multiply to get <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>48</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>72</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>82944</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>288</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>288</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>72</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>288</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>48</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, <math><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>288</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>22</mn></math>.

question.question: What real values of <math><mi>x</mi></math> are not in the domain of <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>|</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>|</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>|</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>|</mo></mrow></mfrac></math>?
question.explanation: Denominator is zero only if both absolute values are zero: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> gives <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></math> or <math><mn>1</mn></math>; <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> gives <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></math> or <math><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. The only common value is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: In the diagram, <math><mi>PT</mi></math> is parallel to <math><mi>QR</mi></math>. What is the measure of <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>PQR</mi></math> (in degrees)?
question.explanation: Parallel lines give <math><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn><mo>°</mo></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Then <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>TPQ</mi></math> and <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>PQR</mi></math> are supplementary, so <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>PQR</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>116</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: The smallest distance from the origin to <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></math> is <math><mi>a</mi></math>. Find <math><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.
question.explanation: Minimize <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. Completing the square gives distance <math><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msqrt><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>68</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></msqrt></math>, minimized at <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>, distance <math><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>17</mn></msqrt></math>, so <math><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn></math>.

question.question: An investment of $24,000 earns 1% interest every two months. After 5 years, how many dollars are in the account (nearest whole number)?
question.explanation: Five years <math><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></math> months <math><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn></math> periods. Amount <math><mo>=</mo><mn>24000</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>1.01</mn><mn>30</mn></msup><mo>≈</mo></math> $32,348.

question.question: A convex polygon has the sum of all but one interior angle equal to 1070°. How many sides does it have?
question.explanation: If <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>, total is <math><mn>1080</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, so the missing angle is <math><mn>10</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, possible. For <math><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>9</mn></math>, the missing angle would exceed <math><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, impossible for convex. Hence <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>10</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>9</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>8</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Find the remainder when <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is divided by <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Write remainder <math><mi>r</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></math>. Since <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn></math> are roots of <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>r</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn></math> and <math><mi>r</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>. Solving gives <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>13</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: Twelve friends order oversized meals: the portions are enough for 18 people. Sharing evenly, how many meals should they have ordered to have just enough for 12 people?
question.explanation: They ordered <math><mn>12</mn></math> meals but needed only <math><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>18</mn></mfrac></math> of that: scale by <math><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>. <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> meals.

question.question: Let <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math> be a quadratic with integer coefficients having <math><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mn>11</mn></msqrt></math> as a root. Compute <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: Conjugate root is <math><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>11</mn></msqrt></math>, so <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>[</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mn>11</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>11</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>]</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>[</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>]</mo></math>. Thus <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>[</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>]</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn><mi>A</mi></math> and <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>]</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>11</mn><mi>A</mi></math>, giving <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>10</mn><mn>11</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Given <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mtable><mtr><mtd><mn>3</mn></mtd><mtd><mn>7</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mtd><mtd><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced></math>, compute <math><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>27</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>31</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>40</mn></msup></math>.
question.explanation: <math><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>I</mi></math>, so <math><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>27</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>9</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>I</mi></math>, <math><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>31</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>10</mn></msup><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>I</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>A</mi></math>, <math><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>40</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>13</mn></msup><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>I</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>A</mi></math>. Sum <math><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>I</mi></math>.

question.question: Find the unique odd integer t with 0<t<23 such that t+2 is the inverse of t modulo 23.
question.explanation: We need <math><mi>t</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>23</mn></math>). Since <math><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, taking negatives gives <math><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>t</mi><mo>≡</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>≡</mo><mn>17</mn></math>.

question.question: Six cars arrive one by one; lanes are Left, Straight, Right. In how many ways do they choose lanes so that all three lanes are occupied?
question.explanation: Total <math><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>729</mn></math>. Subtract assignments leaving some lane empty: <math><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>192</mn></math>; add back cases with two lanes empty: <math><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. So valid <math><mo>=</mo><mn>729</mn><mo>−</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>192</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>540</mn></math>.

question.question: What is the maximum of <math><mn>4</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math> over all real <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Parabola opens downward. Vertex at midpoint between roots <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></math> and <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. Value: <math><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>81</mn></math>.

question.question: Pat selects six cookies from unlimited chocolate chip, oatmeal, and peanut butter (indistinguishable by type). How many different assortments?
question.explanation: Stars and bars: number of nonnegative integer solutions to <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> is <math><mi>C</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>28</mn></math>.

question.question: Identify the curve <math><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>cos</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>θ</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.
question.explanation: <math><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>(</mo><msup><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, a hyperbola.

question.question: Simplify <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>20</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Rewrite as <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>20</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></math>. Cancel: <math><mfrac><mn>20</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>. Product <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>21</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: What is the total surface area, in square inches, of a cube with a volume of 1 cubic foot?
question.explanation: Volume <math><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mtext>ft</mtext><mn>3</mn></msup></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> side <math><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mtext>ft</mtext></math>. Surface area <math><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mtext>ft</mtext><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mtext>ft</mtext><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. Since <math><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mtext>ft</mtext><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>144</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mtext>in</mtext><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, SA <math><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>144</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>864</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mtext>in</mtext><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.

question.question: A bag has blue:yellow marbles in ratio 4:3. After adding 5 blue and removing 3 yellow, the ratio becomes 7:3. How many blue marbles were originally in the bag?
question.explanation: Let <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></math> be original counts with <math><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi></math>. Also <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>21</mn></math>. Solving with <math><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi></math> gives <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>, <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>.

question.question: Compute the product of <math><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></math> and its radical conjugate.
question.explanation: <math><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>22</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Compute <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>ABC</mi></math> in degrees.
question.explanation: <math><mi>AB</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>BC</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></math> and <math><mi>AC</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></math>. By Law of Cosines at <math><mi>B</mi></math>: <math><mi>cos</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>AB</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>BC</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>AC</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>AB</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>BC</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>54</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>54</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>162</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>54</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: In a triangle inscribed in a circle, <math><mi>AB</mi></math> is a diameter and <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. How many degrees are in <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>B</mi></math>?
question.explanation: If <math><mi>AB</mi></math> is a diameter, <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.
