question.question: Given <math><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>211</mn></math>, <math><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>375</mn></math>, <math><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>420</mn></math>, <math><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>523</mn></math>, and <math><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math> for <math><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, compute <math><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>531</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>753</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>975</mn></msub></math>.
question.explanation: From recurrence: <math><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></math>. Hence period <math><mn>10</mn></math> and <math><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>531</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>753</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>975</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>375</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>523</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>898</mn></math>.

question.question: Find all <math><mi>p</mi></math> satisfying both <math><mn>0</mn><mo>≥</mo><mn>54</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>144</mn></math> and <math><mn>0</mn><mo>></mo><mn>12</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>p</mi></math>. Express as interval notation.
question.explanation: First inequality: <math><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>144</mn><mn>54</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>. Second: <math><mi>p</mi><mo>></mo><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>20</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math>. Intersection is <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>]</mo></math>.

question.question: Three consecutive positive integers sum to a <math><mn>3</mn></math>-digit palindrome less than <math><mn>220</mn></math>. What is the largest possible value of the greatest integer?
question.explanation: Sum <math><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>n</mi></math>. Largest palindromic multiple of <math><mn>3</mn></math> below <math><mn>220</mn></math>: <math><mn>171</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>57</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> set <math><mo>{</mo><mn>56</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>57</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>}</mo></math>; largest is <math><mn>58</mn></math>.

question.question: The roots of <math><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> are polygon vertices. The area equals <math><msup><mi>p</mi><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mfrac></msup></math> with prime <math><mi>p</mi></math> and coprime <math><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></math>. Find <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Let <math><mi>w</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi></math>. Roots form a square with <math><mo>|</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></msup></math>, side <math><mo>=</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></msup></math>. Area <math><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></msup></math>. Thus <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> sum <math><mn>11</mn></math>.

question.question: Assume <math><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>r</mi><mo><</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Which equation yields the largest solution <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: For <math><mn>3</mn><msup><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math> with <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo> </mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac></math> is largest when <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is smallest. For <math><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>r</mi><mo><</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, <math><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>10</mn></math> is the smallest among the listed expressions.

question.question: Given <math><mi>a</mi><mo>×</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mi>a</mi><mo>×</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>×</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Compute <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>×</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></math>.
Rectangle with vertices <math><mo>(</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. How many integer-coordinate points lie strictly inside?
question.explanation: Interior lattice <math><mi>x</mi></math>: <math><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>…</mo><mn>4</mn></math> (<math><mn>9</mn></math> values), <math><mi>y</mi></math>: <math><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>…</mo><mn>3</mn></math> (<math><mn>7</mn></math> values). <math><mn>9</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>63</mn></math>.

question.question: Four distinct circles in a plane. What is the maximum number of points where at least two circles intersect?
question.explanation: Each pair intersects in <math><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn></math> points. <math><mi>C</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> pairs <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>, achievable.

question.question: Juan has a collection of stamps from the <math><mn>1970</mn></math>s. He has <math><mn>12</mn></math> stamps from Brazil costing <math><mn>6</mn></math> cents each, <math><mn>12</mn></math> stamps from France costing <math><mn>6</mn></math> cents each, <math><mn>6</mn></math> stamps from Peru costing <math><mn>4</mn></math> cents each, and <math><mn>13</mn></math> stamps from Spain costing <math><mn>5</mn></math> cents each. What is the average price per stamp, in cents? (Round to the nearest tenth.)
question.explanation: Total cost <math><mo>=</mo><mn>0.72</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0.72</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0.24</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0.65</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>$</mo><mn>2.33</mn></math>; count <math><mn>43</mn></math>. <math><mfrac><mn>2.33</mn><mn>43</mn></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.0542</mn></math> <math><mo>→</mo></math> <math><mn>5.4</mn><mo>¢</mo></math>.

question.question: Trapezoid <math><mi>ABCD</mi></math> with <math><mi>AD</mi><mo>∥</mo><mi>BC</mi></math>, <math><mi>AC</mi><mo>⟂</mo><mi>CD</mi></math>, <math><mi>AC</mi></math> bisects <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>BAD</mi></math>, and <math><mtext>area</mtext><mo>[</mo><mi>ABCD</mi><mo>]</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>42</mn></math>. Compute <math><mtext>area</mtext><mo>[</mo><mo>△</mo><mi>ACD</mi><mo>]</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Using angle relations and similar triangles, <math><mo>△</mo><mi>ACD</mi></math> is <math><mn>4</mn></math> times <math><mo>△</mo><mi>CEB</mi></math>; partitioning gives <math><mn>6</mn><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>42</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> area <math><mo>△</mo><mi>ACD</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>28</mn></math>.

question.question: Find the minimum of <math><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> for <math><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Divide: <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>4</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. Equality at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: Solve for <math><mi>x</mi></math>: <math><mfrac><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msqrt><msqrt><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: Square: <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>27</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>19</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>19</mn></mfrac></math> (valid).

question.question: How many quadratics <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> satisfy: whenever <math><mi>c</mi></math> is a root, <math><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math> is also a root?
question.explanation: Analyze cases (double roots, mutual mapping, mixed) <math><mo>→</mo></math> six polynomials: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: What is the range of <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo> </mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>)</mo></math> for <math><mn>0</mn><mo>°</mo><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo></math>?
question.explanation: For <math><mn>0</mn><mo>°</mo><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, <math><mi>sin</mi><mo> </mo><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo></math>; hence <math><msqrt><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo> </mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>∈</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo></math>. <math><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> on <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo></math> gives <math><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mo>∞</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>]</mo></math>.

question.question: A regular tetrahedron ABCD has side length 2. The plane parallel to edges AB and CD and halfway between them cuts the tetrahedron into two pieces. What is the surface area of one piece?
question.explanation: The cross-section is a square of side <math><mn>1</mn></math> (midlines of faces). One piece has half the tetrahedron's total area plus the square: <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: The product of a set of distinct positive integers is 84. What is the least possible sum of these integers?
question.explanation: <math><mn>84</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>7</mn></math>. With distinct factors, combine a pair of <math><mn>2</mn></math>'s as <math><mn>4</mn></math>: <math><mo>{</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>}</mo></math> sum <math><mn>14</mn></math> is minimal.

question.question: For simplified fractions, define the operation <math><mo>⊙</mo></math> as follows: <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>⊙</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mi>q</mi><mi>n</mi></mfrac></math>. Compute <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>30</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>⊙</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>10</mn><mn>21</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Using the definition: <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>30</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>⊙</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>10</mn><mn>21</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>21</mn><mn>30</mn></mfrac></math>. Simplifying: <math><mn>7</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>21</mn><mn>30</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>70</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>490</mn><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>49</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>123</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1234</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>12345</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>123456</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1234567</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>12345678</mn></math>. Compute <math><mi>S</mi><mo> </mo><mtext>mod</mtext><mo> </mo><mn>9</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Sum of digits mod <math><mn>9</mn></math>: <math><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>21</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>28</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>≡</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>≡</mo><mn>3</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>9</mn></math>).

question.question: Solve <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Express the solution set.
question.explanation: <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> is positive only when <math><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>5</mn></math>.

question.question: A unicycle wheel of radius <math><mn>9</mn></math> inches makes <math><mn>2</mn></math> revolutions every <math><mn>3</mn></math> seconds. What is the speed in inches per second?
question.explanation: Circumference <math><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn><mi>π</mi></math> inches. Rate <math><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mtext>rev</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mtext>s</mtext></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mn>18</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>π</mi></math> in/s.

question.question: Reflect <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math> over <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, then reflect the image over <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. What is the resulting point?
question.explanation: <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math> <math><mo>→</mo></math> reflect across <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> <math><mo>→</mo></math> <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Then across <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> <math><mo>→</mo></math> <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: Positive integers <math><mi>a</mi><mo><</mo><mi>b</mi><mo><</mo><mn>2009</mn></math> with <math><mn>2009</mn></math> form a geometric sequence with integer ratio. Find <math><mi>a</mi></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mn>2009</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mn>41</mn></math>. Ratio must be an integer <math><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></math>; only <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math> works: <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>41</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>287</mn></math>, <math><mn>2009</mn></math>.

question.question: Write <math><mn>10</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>24</mn></math> as <math><mo>(</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math> with integers <math><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi></math>. Compute <math><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Factor: <math><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></math> be distinct reals. Find the degree of <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: Each term is quadratic-over-constant <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> degree <math><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. But <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, so <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></math> by polynomial identity. Degree is <math><mn>0</mn></math>.

question.question: Write <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> as a single fraction.
question.explanation: Common denominator <math><mn>20</mn></math>: <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>24</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>20</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>11</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow><mn>20</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: In <math><mo>|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>|</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, what is the product of all possible values of <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: <math><mo>|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math> or <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></math>. Product <math><mn>16</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>128</mn></math>.

question.question: Given <math><mi>sin</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>RPQ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>25</mn></mfrac></math> and <math><mi>S</mi></math> is opposite <math><mi>Q</mi></math> on the line through <math><mi>P</mi></math>, find <math><mi>cos</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>RPS</mi></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mi>cos</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>∠</mo><mi>RPS</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mo>∠</mo><mi>RPQ</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>cos</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>RPQ</mi></math>. With <math><mi>sin</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>25</mn></mfrac></math> (acute), <math><mi>cos</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>24</mn><mn>25</mn></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> answer <math><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>24</mn><mn>25</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: A robot takes <math><mn>2.5</mn></math> hours to travel <math><mn>1</mn></math> km at constant speed. It takes <math><mn>90</mn></math> seconds to traverse a hallway. How many meters long is the hallway?
question.explanation: <math><mn>2.5</mn></math> h <math><mo>=</mo><mn>9000</mn></math> s. <math><mfrac><mn>90</mn><mn>9000</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>100</mn></mfrac></math> of a km <math><mo>=</mo><mn>0.01</mn></math> km <math><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math> m.

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. If <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, find <math><mi>b</mi></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: Four random independent points on a circle are labeled <math><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi></math> uniformly at random. What is <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mtext>segments</mtext><mo> </mo><mi>AB</mi><mo> </mo><mtext>and</mtext><mo> </mo><mi>CD</mi><mo> </mo><mtext>intersect</mtext><mo>)</mo></math>?
question.explanation: With <math><mn>4</mn></math> points forming a convex quadrilateral, choose <math><mi>B</mi></math> among the <math><mn>3</mn></math> other points. Exactly <math><mn>1</mn></math> choice (the opposite vertex) yields intersection <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Two concentric circles with center <math><mi>D</mi></math> have radii <math><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mn>2</mn></math>. The shaded area equals <math><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac></math> of the larger circle's area. Find <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>ADC</mi></math> (in degrees).
question.explanation: Let <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>∠</mo><mi>ADC</mi></math>. Shaded <math><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>360</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>360</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>)</mo></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>360</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>600</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: A cylinder of radius <math><mn>3</mn></math> cm and height <math><mn>8</mn></math> cm is used to fill a sphere of radius <math><mn>6</mn></math> cm. How many full beakers are needed?
question.explanation: <math><msub><mi>V</mi><mtext>cyl</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>72</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. <math><msub><mi>V</mi><mtext>sphere</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>288</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>288</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>72</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: Evaluate <math><mi>sin</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>arcsin</mi><mo> </mo><mn>0.4</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>arcsin</mi><mo> </mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>arcsin</mi><mo> </mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>arcsin</mi><mo> </mo><mn>0.4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Use identity: <math><mi>sin</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo><mi>sin</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mi>sin</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mi>sin</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></math>. With <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>arcsin</mi><mo> </mo><mn>0.5</mn></math>, <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>arcsin</mi><mo> </mo><mn>0.4</mn></math>: <math><mn>0.25</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0.16</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0.09</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>100</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math> be a monic cubic. When divided by <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math> the remainder is <math><mi>R</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math>; when divided by <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math> the remainder is <math><mn>2</mn><mi>R</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math>. Given <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, find <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Let <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and <math><mi>R</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi></math>. Writing <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi></math> and similarly with <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>c</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></math> gives <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi></math>. Comparing <math><mi>x</mi></math>-coefficients gives <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></math> and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>c</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Constant term at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> in first form: <math><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>⌊</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>⌋</mo></math> for <math><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mo>[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>∞</mo><mo>)</mo></math> where <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is real-valued. How many distinct values are in the range of <math><mi>f</mi></math>?
question.explanation: For real <math><mi>x</mi></math>, <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>x</mi></msup></math> is defined only for integer <math><mi>x</mi></math> if we require real values. Values alternate sign and decay to <math><mn>0</mn></math> in magnitude. Floors attained are <math><mn>1</mn></math> (<math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>), <math><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> (<math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>), and <math><mn>0</mn></math> for sufficiently large <math><mi>x</mi></math>. Thus <math><mo>{</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>}</mo></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>3</mn></math> values.

question.question: A bicycle travels at <math><mn>20</mn></math> feet per minute. What is the speed in inches per second?
question.explanation: <math><mn>20</mn></math> ft/min <math><mo>=</mo><mn>240</mn></math> in/min. Divide by <math><mn>60</mn></math>: <math><mfrac><mn>240</mn><mn>60</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> in/s.

question.question: A committee has <math><mn>8</mn></math> Republicans and <math><mn>6</mn></math> Democrats. In how many ways can a <math><mn>5</mn></math>-member subcommittee be formed with at least one from each party?
question.explanation: Total <math><mi>C</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2002</mn></math>. Subtract all-Republican: <math><mi>C</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>56</mn></math> and all-Democrat: <math><mi>C</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>. <math><mn>2002</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>56</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1940</mn></math>.

question.question: Simplify <math><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><mfrac><mn>5</mn><msqrt><mn>80</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>845</mn></msqrt><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>45</mn></msqrt></mrow><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mfrac></msqrt></math>.
question.explanation: Divide each term by <math><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></math>: <math><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mrow><msqrt><mn>80</mn></msqrt><mo>⋅</mo><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><msqrt><mn>400</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>; <math><mfrac><msqrt><mn>845</mn></msqrt><mrow><mn>9</mn><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>169</mn></msqrt><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>13</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></math>; <math><mfrac><msqrt><mn>45</mn></msqrt><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>9</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Sum <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>13</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>169</mn><mn>36</mn></mfrac></math>, square root <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>13</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Given positive reals <math><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi></math> with <math><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, find min of <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Achieved when <math><mi>x</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> with the constraint; e.g., <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: If <math><mroot><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mroot><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mo>…</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfrac></math> with positive integers <math><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo></math>, find <math><mi>b</mi></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> since <math><mn>1</mn><mo><</mo><mroot><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mroot><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Then <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mroot><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mroot><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mroot><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mroot><mo>+</mo><mroot><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mroot><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.587</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1.26</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≈</mo><mn>3.85</mn></math>, so <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>⌊3.85⌋</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: Given <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, compute <math><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Add first two: <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Subtract (<math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></math>): <math><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>; then <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn></math>; product <math><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>120</mn></math>.

question.question: What is the remainder when the 100th Fibonacci number is divided by 4?
question.explanation: Fibonacci mod <math><mn>4</mn></math> has period <math><mn>6</mn></math>: <math><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo></math> Thus <math><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>100</mn></msub><mo>≡</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>≡</mo><mn>3</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>4</mn></math>).

question.question: Compute <math><msup><mn>513</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mn>487</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.
question.explanation: Difference of squares: <math><mo>(</mo><mn>513</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>487</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>513</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>487</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1000</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>26</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>26000</mn></math>.

question.question: The product of three consecutive integers is <math><mn>120</mn></math>. That product divided by the mean of the three integers is <math><mn>24</mn></math>. What is the largest of the three consecutive integers?
question.explanation: Let integers be <math><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>n</mi></math>, <math><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Mean <math><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></math>, product <math><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn></math>, and product/mean <math><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>. Divide: <math><mfrac><mn>120</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, largest is <math><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>.

question.question: What is the base-six equivalent of <math><msub><mn>999</mn><mn>10</mn></msub></math>?
question.explanation: <math><mn>999</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><msub><mn>4343</mn><mn>6</mn></msub></math>.

question.question: A parabola <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math> with vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is reflected about <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></math>, producing <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi></math>. Find <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi></math> in terms of <math><mi>k</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Write <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></math>; reflection gives <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></math>. Summing: <math><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></math> for all <math><mi>x</mi></math>. Plug <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi></math>.

question.question: Vectors <math><mi>a</mi></math> and <math><mi>b</mi></math> have angle <math><mn>29</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. The angle between <math><mi>b</mi></math> and <math><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></math> is <math><mn>84</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Find the angle between <math><mi>a</mi></math> and <math><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi></math>.
question.explanation: In the plane, <math><mtext>angle</mtext><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mtext>angle</mtext><mo>(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>−</mo><mtext>angle</mtext><mo>(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>84</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>29</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>55</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: What is the smallest number which is one less than twice its reciprocal?
question.explanation: Solve <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> or <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Smallest is <math><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: Find the integer <math><mi>x</mi></math> satisfying <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo><</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>7</mn></mfrac><mo><</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: Multiply by <math><mn>7</mn></math>: <math><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>1.75</mn><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>2.333</mn><mo>…</mo></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: How many license plates have <math><mn>2</mn></math> different letters (<math><mi>A</mi><mo>–</mo><mi>Z</mi></math>) followed by <math><mn>2</mn></math> different digits (<math><mn>0</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>9</mn></math>)?
question.explanation: Letters: <math><mn>26</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>25</mn></math>. Digits: <math><mn>10</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. Total <math><mo>=</mo><mn>26</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>58</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>500</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math> for <math><mi>n</mi><mo><</mo><mi>a</mi></math> and <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn></math> for <math><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>a</mi></math>. Find <math><mi>a</mi></math> if <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is continuous.
question.explanation: Match at <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi></math>: <math><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>3</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>.

question.question: If <math><mi>t</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></math>, find <math><mi>t</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>; <math><mi>t</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: Solve for the positive <math><mi>x</mi></math>: <math><mroot><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mroot><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Cube: <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>16</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4096</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>64</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>62</mn></math> or <math><mn>66</mn></math>. Positive solution: <math><mn>66</mn></math>.

question.question: I have a deck of <math><mn>54</mn></math> cards and deal all of them to <math><mi>x</mi></math> players, each getting <math><mi>y</mi></math> cards. If <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mi>y</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, how many possible values of <math><mi>x</mi></math> are there?
question.explanation: We need <math><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>54</mn></math> with <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mi>y</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Factor <math><mn>54</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></math>. Valid <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></math>: <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>27</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Four possibilities.

question.question: Determine the type of the graph: <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Rewrite: <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>, which is an ellipse.

question.question: Given <math><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, and <math><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>, compute <math><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mi>x</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Let <math><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi></math>, <math><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mi>x</mi></math>. Then <math><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>⋅</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math> and <math><msup><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Thus <math><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>24</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>.

question.question: A line has direction vector <math><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo></math>. From the plotted points <math><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math> on the line, find <math><mi>b</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Direction from the two points: <math><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Scale by <math><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> to make <math><mi>x</mi></math>-component <math><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></math>: <math><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></math>. Hence <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: An equilateral triangle is inscribed in <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>y</mi></math> with one vertex at the parabola's vertex. Find its side length.
question.explanation: Let <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></math>. Equilateral gives <math><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mn>64</mn></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>192</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></math>. Side length <math><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></math>.

question.question: Two independent races: Dan vs. Donald for president, Freddie vs. Bernie for VP. Each candidate has 50% to win. What is P(Dan and Freddie both win)?
question.explanation: Independent events: <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Three plus the reciprocal of a number equals 7 divided by that number. What is the number?
question.explanation: <math><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: Each point of <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></math> is reflected through <math><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. The image set satisfies <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Find <math><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Center <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math> reflects to <math><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Same radius <math><mn>5</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>16</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>43</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>43</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.explanation: For each prime <math><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn></math>, exponents split as <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math> or <math><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. <math><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math> ordered splits produce each pair twice (<math><mi>a</mi><mo><</mo><mi>b</mi></math> vs <math><mi>b</mi><mo><</mo><mi>a</mi></math>). Thus <math><mfrac><mn>16</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> values of <math><mi>a</mi></math>.

question.question: Find the remainder mod <math><mn>7</mn></math> of <math><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>197</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>199</mn></math>.

question.explanation: <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> for the <math><mn>4</mn></math> rotational symmetries of the square: <math><mfrac><mn>40320</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>10080</mn></math>.

question.explanation: Same as <math><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>18</mn></msup></math>; powers of <math><mn>2</mn></math> cycle <math><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>18</mn><mtext> mod </mtext><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> units digit <math><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: Triangle <math><mi>ABC</mi></math> is isosceles with <math><mi>AB</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>AC</mi></math> and altitude <math><mi>AM</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></math>. question.explanation: From trig/LoS and right triangles: <math><mi>BD</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>, <math><mi>AB</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>11</mn><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>, <math><mi>BM</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>11</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>, so perimeter <math><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>11</mn></math>.

question.question: You have 6 different books, 2 of which are math. In how many orders can they be placed so the math books are not adjacent?
question.explanation: Arrange <math><mn>4</mn></math> non-math: <math><mn>4</mn><mo>!</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>. question.question: Suppose <math><mi>f</mi></math> has an inverse <math><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, and <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, what is <math><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo></math>?

Thus <math><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: Two sides of a triangle are each 8 units long. If the third side has a whole number length, what is the greatest possible perimeter?
question.explanation: By triangle inequality, third side <math><mo><</mo><mn>16</mn></math>, so max integer is <math><mn>15</mn></math>. Perimeter <math><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>31</mn></math>.

question.question: In the figure, <math><mi>AD</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>BD</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>CD</mi></math> and <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>BCA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Find <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>BAC</mi></math>.

Hence <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>BAC</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: What is the difference between <math><msqrt><mn>64</mn></msqrt></math> and <math><mroot><mn>64</mn><mn>3</mn></mroot></math>?
question.explanation: <math><msqrt><mn>64</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> and <math><mroot><mn>64</mn><mn>3</mn></mroot><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, so difference is <math><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: Let A be the sum of the positive divisors of 500. What is the sum of the distinct prime divisors of A?
question.explanation: <math><mn>500</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>σ</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>500</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>125</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>156</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>13</mn></math>. Distinct primes: <math><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>13</mn></math> sum to <math><mn>25</mn></math>.

question.question: Find the point <math><mi>P</mi></math> on <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></math> such that <math><mi>PA</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>PO</mi></math> where <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mi>O</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: The superfactorial <math><mi>n</mi><mo>$</mo></math> is defined as <math><mi>n</mi><mo>$</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>!</mo></mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>!</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>…</mo><msup><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>!</mo></mrow><mrow></mrow></msup></mrow></msup></mrow></msup></math> with <math><mi>n</mi><mo>!</mo></math> copies of <math><mi>n</mi><mo>!</mo></math> in the power tower. What is the units digit of <math><mn>4</mn><mo>$</mo></math>?
question.explanation: <math><mn>4</mn><mo>!</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>, so <math><mn>4</mn><mo>$</mo></math> is <math><msup><mn>24</mn><mrow><msup><mn>24</mn><mrow><mo>…</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></msup></math> with an even exponent. <math><msup><mn>24</mn><mtext>even</mtext></msup></math> ends in <math><mn>6</mn></math> because any power <math><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></math> of a number ending with <math><mn>4</mn></math> alternates <math><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn></math> and even exponents give <math><mn>6</mn></math>.

question.explanation: Numerator <math><mo>|</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>81</mn><mo>|</mo><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, zero only at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. For the fraction to be <math><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, denominator must be negative: <math><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>36</mn></math>, excluding <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math> where the fraction is <math><mn>0</mn></math>.

question.question: <math><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></math> chosen uniformly from <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. What is the probability that sides <math><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></math> form a triangle?
question.explanation: Triangle inequalities in the <math><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn></math> square give a symmetric shaded region of area <math><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> out of <math><mn>9</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> probability <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: A <math><mn>400</mn></math> m track consists of two straight edges of a rectangle (width <math><mi>w</mi></math>) and two semicircles (radius <math><mi>r</mi></math>). Maximize the rectangle area. What is the largest possible area?
question.explanation: Perimeter <math><mn>2</mn><mi>w</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>400</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>w</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>200</mn></math>. By AM-GM, <math><mi>w</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>10000</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac></math>, so area <math><mn>2</mn><mi>w</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mn>20000</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac></math> with equality at <math><mi>w</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></math>, <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>100</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Solve <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>≤</mo><mn>10</mn></math>. Give interval.
question.explanation: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>7</mn></math>.

question.question: Simplify <math><mn>19</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>81</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Combine like terms: <math><mo>(</mo><mn>19</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>81</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>80</mn></math>.

question.question: Kathy exchanges $150 into pounds at 1.64 USD/£ and $150 into euros at 1.32 USD/€. How many more euros than pounds does she get (nearest whole)?
question.explanation: Pounds: <math><mfrac><mn>150</mn><mn>1.64</mn></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mn>91.46</mn></math>. Euros: <math><mfrac><mn>150</mn><mn>1.32</mn></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mn>113.64</mn></math>. Difference <math><mo>≈</mo><mn>22.18</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>22</mn></math>.

question.question: How many integers satisfy <math><mo>|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>|</mo><mo>≤</mo><mn>5.6</mn></math>?
question.explanation: <math><mo>−</mo><mn>5.6</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>≤</mo><mn>5.6</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mo>−</mo><mn>3.6</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>7.6</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> integers <math><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>11</mn></math> values.

question.question: If <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, what is <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>?

What is the smallest real <math><mi>x</mi></math> in the domain of <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></math>?
question.explanation: Require <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>10</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>55</mn><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mfrac><mn>11</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. Smallest is <math><mfrac><mn>11</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: In right <math><mo>∆</mo><mi>RST</mi></math> with right angle at <math><mi>S</mi></math>, <math><mi>sin</mi><mo> </mo><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math> and <math><mi>RT</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. What is <math><mi>sin</mi><mo> </mo><mi>T</mi></math>?
question.explanation: <math><mi>ST</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mi>RS</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>21</mn></msqrt></math>. So <math><mi>sin</mi><mo> </mo><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>RS</mi><mi>RT</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>21</mn></msqrt><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: For <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, the minimum distance from the origin is <math><mfrac><msqrt><mi>a</mi></msqrt><mi>b</mi></mfrac></math> in lowest radical form. Find <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Minimize <math><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfrac><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt></math>, minimized at <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> distance <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>10</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mtext> if </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>;</mo><mo> </mo><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mtext> if </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>3</mn><mo>}</mo></math>. Compute <math><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> for <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>3</mn></math>: <math><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>; for <math><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>3</mn></math> none. So <math><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. For <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> for <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>3</mn></math>: <math><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></math>; for <math><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>3</mn></math> none. So sum <math><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.

question.question: From a point <math><mi>P</mi></math>, distances to five vertices of a regular octahedron are <math><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn></math>. Find the distance to the sixth vertex.
question.explanation: In an octahedron, opposite-vertex distance squares pair to the same sum. Repeated pair sum: <math><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>11</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>130</mn></math>. Thus missing <math><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>130</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>66</mn></math>.

question.question: Jen (<math><mn>200</mn></math> g ball) and Jack (<math><mn>150</mn></math> g ball) throw with equal force. What is the ratio of Jen's acceleration to Jack's?
question.explanation: <math><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>a</mi></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>a</mi><mo>∝</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>m</mi></mfrac></math> for equal force. <math><mfrac><msub><mi>a</mi><mtext>Jen</mtext></msub><msub><mi>a</mi><mtext>Jack</mtext></msub></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>150</mn><mn>200</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: For <math><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>y</mi></math>, Archimedes picks <math><mi>x</mi></math>, then Brahmagupta picks <math><mi>y</mi></math> to maximize <math><mi>z</mi></math>. Archimedes wants to minimize <math><mi>z</mi></math>. What <math><mi>x</mi></math> should he choose?
question.explanation: For fixed <math><mi>x</mi></math>, <math><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is concave; maximized at <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. Substitution gives <math><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>, minimized at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mn>16</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: If <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>, evaluate <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mroot><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>3</mn></mroot><mo>)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup></math>.
question.explanation: <math><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></math>, <math><mroot><mn>64</mn><mn>3</mn></mroot><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>64</mn><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: Square <math><mi>ABCD</mi></math> has area <math><mn>16</mn></math>. In the tangram, piece <math><mi>e</mi></math> is a square and all triangles are isosceles. What is the area of the gray triangular piece?
question.explanation: The gray piece is an isosceles right triangle with leg <math><mn>2</mn></math>, so area <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: If <math><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn></math>, what is the value of <math><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math>?
question.explanation: <math><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Then <math><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>23</mn></math>.

question.question: Navin makes 160 rupee/hr (32.35 rupee = 1 USD), Luka makes 25 kuna/hr (5.18 kuna = 1 USD), and Ian makes 34 pula/hr (6.95 pula = 1 USD). Who earns the most in USD per hour?
question.explanation: Navin: <math><mfrac><mn>160</mn><mn>32.35</mn></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mn>4.95</mn></math>; Luka: <math><mfrac><mn>25</mn><mn>5.18</mn></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mn>4.83</mn></math>; Ian: <math><mfrac><mn>34</mn><mn>6.95</mn></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mn>4.89</mn></math>. Largest is Navin.

question.question: Add <math><mn>313.9</mn></math> and <math><mn>12.6</mn></math>.

In a circle of radius <math><mn>14</mn></math> with center <math><mi>Q</mi></math>, radii <math><mi>QA</mi></math> and <math><mi>QB</mi></math> are perpendicular. Two tangent semicircles inside have centers <math><mi>C</mi></math> (larger) and <math><mi>D</mi></math> (smaller). What is the radius <math><mi>r</mi></math> of the smaller semicircle?
question.explanation: Using right triangle <math><mi>QCD</mi></math>: <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>196</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>28</mn><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn><mi>r</mi></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>14</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mo>|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Find the maximum value of <math><mo>|</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>|</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>|</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>|</mo></math>.
question.explanation: With <math><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mi>y</mi></math>, expression becomes <math><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mo>|</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>|</mo></math>. Max over <math><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mo>[</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo></math> is <math><mfrac><mn>13</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: A <math><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math> clockwise rotation about <math><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>i</mi></math> is applied to <math><mn>3</mn></math> (as a complex number). What is the image?
question.explanation: Rotate about <math><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>i</mi></math>: <math><mi>z</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>−</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>i</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>[</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>i</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>]</mo></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>z</mi><mo>'</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>i</mi></math>.

question.question: How many digits are common between the base-<math><mn>7</mn></math> and base-<math><mn>8</mn></math> representations of <math><msub><mn>629</mn><mn>10</mn></msub></math>?
question.explanation: <math><msub><mn>629</mn><mn>10</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mn>1556</mn><mn>7</mn></msub></math> and <math><msub><mn>1165</mn><mn>8</mn></msub></math>. Common digits: <math><mo>{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>}</mo></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: Roslyn has 10 boxes: 5 contain pencils, 4 contain pens, and 2 contain both. How many contain neither?
question.explanation: Pencils only: <math><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>; pens only: <math><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>; both: <math><mn>2</mn></math>. So filled <math><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>; neither <math><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: If no one shares an office, in how many ways can 3 people be assigned to 5 distinct offices?
question.explanation: Permutations: <math><mn>5</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></math>.

question.question: What is the remainder when 2004 is divided by 12?
question.explanation: <math><mn>2004</mn></math> is divisible by <math><mn>3</mn></math> (digit sum <math><mn>6</mn></math>) and by <math><mn>4</mn></math> (last two digits <math><mn>04</mn></math>), hence divisible by <math><mn>12</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> remainder <math><mn>0</mn></math>.

question.question: If <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>, what is <math><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></math>?
question.explanation: Solve <math><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>.

question.question: A reflection takes <math><mo>⟨</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>⟩</mo></math> to <math><mo>⟨</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⟩</mo></math>. Which vector does it take <math><mo>⟨</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⟩</mo></math> to?
question.explanation: Reflection line is along <math><mo>⟨</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>⟩</mo></math>. Reflect <math><mi>v</mi></math> via <math><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mtext>proj</mtext><mo>_</mo><mtext>line</mtext><mo>(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>v</mi></math> to get <math><mo>⟨</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>18</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>⟩</mo></math>.

question.question: Asymptotes <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></math>; the hyperbola passes through <math><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. What is the distance between its foci?
question.explanation: Center <math><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></math>; slopes <math><mo>±</mo><mn>2</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>1</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Then <math><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> distance <math><mn>2</mn><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></math>.

question.question: Let N be the units digit of 21420N. Which nonzero N makes the number divisible by 6?
question.explanation: Divisible by <math><mn>6</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> even and sum of digits multiple of <math><mn>3</mn></math>. <math><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>N</mi></math> multiple of <math><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><mi>N</mi></math> even <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>.

question.question: Six witches each shake hands with ten sorcerers; no other handshakes occur. How many handshakes?
question.explanation: Each witch shakes with <math><mn>10</mn></math> sorcerers: <math><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>P</mi></math> be quadratic with real coefficients and <math><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>≤</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> for all <math><mi>x</mi></math>, and <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>181</mn></math>. Find <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mi>P</mi></math> has vertex at <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>: <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. From <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>100</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>181</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math>. Then <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mn>225</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>406</mn></math>.

question.question: Simplify <math><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>40</mn><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>9</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>5</mn></msup></math>.

question.question: Solve for the sum of all <math><mi>a</mi></math>: <math><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>63</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Multiply by <math><mn>3</mn></math>: <math><mn>9</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>189</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>36</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> or <math><mn>8</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> sum <math><mn>10</mn></math>.

question.question: What is the remainder when <math><msup><mn>129</mn><mn>34</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>96</mn><mn>38</mn></msup></math> is divided by <math><mn>11</mn></math>?
question.explanation: <math><mn>129</mn><mo>≡</mo><mn>96</mn><mo>≡</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>11</mn></math>).
