Then <math><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>34</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>38</mn></msup></math> with <math><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mo>≡</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>81</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>27</mn><mo>≡</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>≡</mo><mn>9</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>11</mn></math>).

question.question: Compute <math><msup><mrow><mi>sin</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mn>18</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mi>sin</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mn>18</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Using identities or <math><mi>sin</mi><mo> </mo><mn>18</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> gives <math><msup><mrow><mi>sin</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mn>18</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mi>sin</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mn>18</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. If <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, what is the sum of the coefficients of <math><mi>g</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Sum of coefficients of <math><mi>g</mi></math> is <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: What is the shortest distance from <math><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math> to the line <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math>?
question.explanation: The perpendicular from <math><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math> meets the line at <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>; distance <math><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>20</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></math>.

question.question: Find the vector <math><mi>v</mi></math> of smallest magnitude such that <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Solve cross-product system and minimize <math><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>.

question.question: If <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>, find the projection of <math><mi>a</mi></math> onto <math><mi>b</mi></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mtext>proj</mtext><mo>_</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>49</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>16</mn><mn>49</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>48</mn><mn>49</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>24</mn><mn>49</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: If <math><mi>arccos</mi><mo> </mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>arccos</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>arccos</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></math>, <math><mi>x</mi></math> satisfies <math><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> with integers <math><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></math> (<math><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>). What is the smallest possible value of <math><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>|</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>|</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>|</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>|</mo></math>?
question.explanation: Eliminate radicals to get <math><mn>12</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>14</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> sum of absolute coefficients <math><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>27</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></math> be the distinct roots of <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Determine the unordered set <math><mo>{</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>α</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>}</mo></math>.
question.explanation: The cubic resolvent is <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>; roots are <math><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mn>1</mn><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></math>.

question.question: Find the largest integer <math><mo><</mo><mn>2010</mn></math> with remainders <math><mn>5</mn><mtext> mod </mtext><mn>7</mn></math>, <math><mn>10</mn><mtext> mod </mtext><mn>11</mn></math>, and <math><mn>10</mn><mtext> mod </mtext><mn>13</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Solution to the congruences is <math><mn>439</mn></math> modulo <math><mi>lcm</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1001</mn></math>. Largest <math><mo><</mo><mn>2010</mn></math> is <math><mn>439</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1001</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1440</mn></math>.

question.question: <math><mi>y</mi></math> varies inversely as <math><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></math>. If <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math> when <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>, find <math><mi>x</mi></math> when <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mi>y</mi><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn><msqrt><mn>24</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></math>. For <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>: <math><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>600</mn></math>.

question.question: In <math><mo>∆</mo><mi>ABC</mi></math> with side lengths <math><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></math> and circumradius <math><mi>R</mi></math>, <math><mi>G</mi></math> is the centroid, <math><mi>H</mi></math> the orthocenter, and <math><mi>F</mi></math> the midpoint of <math><mi>GH</mi></math>. Find <math><mi>AF</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>BF</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>CF</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.
question.explanation: With circumcenter at origin, vectors give <math><mi>AF</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>BF</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>CF</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>R</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.

question.question: A square and an equilateral triangle have equal perimeters. If the triangle's area is <math><mn>16</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo> </mo><msup><mtext>cm</mtext><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, what is the length of a diagonal of the square?
question.explanation: Triangle area <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> perimeters equal <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> square side <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> diagonal<math><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></math>.

question.question: Three pencils and a jumbo eraser cost $1.24. Five pencils and a jumbo eraser cost $1.82. In cents, what is the cost of a pencil?
question.explanation: Let <math><mi>p</mi></math> be pencil (cents), <math><mi>e</mi></math> eraser. <math><mn>3</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>124</mn></math> and <math><mn>5</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>182</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> subtract: <math><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>58</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>29</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> with <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Find the minimum of <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>a</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>b</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mi>c</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>16</mn><mi>d</mi></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: By Cauchy-Schwarz: <math><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>a</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>b</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mi>c</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>16</mn><mi>d</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>≥</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></math>. Equality at <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, totaling <math><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: Given positive reals <math><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></math> with <math><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, find the minimum value of <math><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>8</mn></msup></math>.
question.explanation: AM-GM: <math><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>8</mn></msup><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>8</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></math>. Equality when <math><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>8</mn></msup></math> and <math><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>.

question.question: What is <math><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> as a decimal?
question.explanation: <math><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>4.5</mn></math> (or <math><mfrac><mn>45</mn><mn>10</mn></mfrac></math>).

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>arccos</mi><mo> </mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>arcsin</mi><mo> </mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> (radians). Find the range of <math><mi>f</mi></math> on <math><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mo>[</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Let <math><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>arccos</mi><mo> </mo><mi>x</mi></math>, <math><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>arcsin</mi><mo> </mo><mi>x</mi></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. Then <math><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math>. With <math><mi>β</mi><mo>∈</mo><mo>[</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>]</mo></math>, min <math><mfrac><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math>, max <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: The sequence satisfies <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo></math> for <math><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, and <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1986</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Compute <math><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1985</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Summing recurrences from <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> to <math><mn>1985</mn></math> and using <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1986</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> yields <math><mn>3</mn><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>993</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>331</mn></math>.

question.question: Convert <math><mfrac><mn>57</mn><mn>160</mn></mfrac></math> to a terminating decimal.
question.explanation: To convert to a terminating decimal, we need a power of 10 in the denominator. Factor <math><mn>160</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. To get <math><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></math>, we need <math><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></math>, so multiply numerator and denominator by <math><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>625</mn></math>: <math><mfrac><mn>57</mn><mn>160</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>57</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>625</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>160</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>625</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>35625</mn><mn>100000</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0.35625</mn></math>.

question.question: In an isosceles right triangle, the altitude to the hypotenuse is <math><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></math>. What is the area of the triangle?
question.explanation: Altitude to hypotenuse splits into two <math><mn>45</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>90</mn></math> triangles with legs <math><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></math>; hypotenuse <math><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></math>. Area <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mtext>altitude</mtext><mo>⋅</mo><mtext>hypotenuse</mtext><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>⋅</mo><mn>8</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></math>.

question.question: Find the domain of <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msqrt></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: Require denominator <math><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math>: <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn></math> or <math><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: <math><mi>n</mi></math> fair <math><mn>6</mn></math>-sided dice are rolled. The probability exactly two show a number other than <math><mn>1</mn></math> is <math><mfrac><mn>25</mn><mn>216</mn></mfrac></math>. Find <math><mi>n</mi></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>25</mn><mn>216</mn></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>25</mn><mn>216</mn></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>108</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: Symbols <math><mo>△</mo></math>, <math><mo>□</mo></math>, <math><mo>♦</mo></math>, <math><mo>♣</mo></math> are distinct integers <math><mn>1</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. Given <math><mo>△</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>□</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>♣</mo></math>, <math><mo>△</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>△</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>♦</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>♦</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>♦</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>♦</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>♦</mo></math>, and <math><mo>△</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>△</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>♣</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>♦</mo></math>, what is <math><mo>□</mo></math>?
question.explanation: From <math><mn>2</mn><mo>△</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>♦</mo></math> and <math><mn>2</mn><mo>△</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>♣</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>♦</mo></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>5</mn><mo>♦</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>♣</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>♦</mo></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mo>♣</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>♦</mo></math>. Valid <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></math> pair is <math><mo>(</mo><mo>♦</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>♣</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Then <math><mn>2</mn><mo>△</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mo>△</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and <math><mo>□</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>♣</mo><mo>−</mo><mo>△</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: What is the last nonzero digit to the right of the decimal point in <math><mfrac><mn>137</mn><mn>500</mn></mfrac></math>?
question.explanation: <math><mfrac><mn>137</mn><mn>500</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>274</mn><mn>1000</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0.274</mn></math>; last nonzero decimal digit is <math><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: Find the quotient when <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>9</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> is divided by <math><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Use <math><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>9</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>8</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and write <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>9</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>9</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. The quotient part is <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>8</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: Simplify <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>.
question.explanation: Expand the first product: <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Expand the second product: <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>18</mn></math>. Subtracting: <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>u</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></math>.

question.question: Karla drove <math><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></math> miles last year. How many gallons would she have saved using <math><mn>48</mn></math> mpg instead of <math><mn>15</mn></math> mpg?
question.explanation: SUV: <math><mfrac><mn>12000</mn><mn>15</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>800</mn></math> gal. Hybrid: <math><mfrac><mn>12000</mn><mn>48</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>250</mn></math> gal. Saved: <math><mn>800</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>250</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>550</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup></math>. Find <math><msqrt><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></msqrt></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>, <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>16</mn></msup></math>. Square root is <math><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></math>.

question.question: In the arithmetic sequence <math><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></math>, find <math><mi>x</mi></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mi>x</mi></math> is the mean of <math><mn>9</mn></math> and <math><mn>81</mn></math>: <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>81</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>45</mn></math>.

question.question: Rectangle <math><mi>ABCD</mi></math> has center <math><mi>O</mi></math> with <math><mfrac><mi>AB</mi><mi>AD</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></math>. A random interior point is chosen. What is the probability it is closer to <math><mi>O</mi></math> than to any vertex?
question.explanation: Partition into four congruent rectangles about <math><mi>O</mi></math>; symmetry shows the locus closer to <math><mi>O</mi></math> than to <math><mi>A</mi></math> fills half of each such rectangle. Probability <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>, independent of <math><mi>k</mi></math>.

question.question: Circle <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and parabola <math><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi></math> share two common tangents, producing four tangency points. Find the area of the quadrilateral formed by these points.
question.explanation: Tangents are <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Tangency points: <math><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> on circle, <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math> on parabola. Trapezoid with bases <math><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mn>8</mn></math>, height <math><mn>3</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> area <math><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math>.

question.question: The sum of the first <math><mi>n</mi></math> terms of <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>16</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo></math> is <math><mfrac><mn>255</mn><mn>512</mn></mfrac></math>. Find <math><mi>n</mi></math>.
question.explanation: <math><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac></math>. Set equal to <math><mfrac><mn>255</mn><mn>512</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>9</mn></msup></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>.

question.question: Thirty-five students attend a math club meeting. The number of girls is a multiple of 13 and there are more girls than boys. How many boys are at the meeting?
question.explanation: Girls <math><mo>∈</mo><mo>{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>26</mn><mo>}</mo></math>. More girls than boys <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> girls<math><mo>></mo><mn>17.5</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>26</mn></math> girls. Boys <math><mo>=</mo><mn>35</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>26</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>.

question.question: Compute <math><msup><mn>17</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mtext> mod </mtext><mn>83</mn></math> (residue <math><mn>0</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>82</mn></math>).
question.explanation: <math><mn>17</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>≡</mo><mn>2</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>83</mn></math>). Since <math><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>42</mn><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, inverse is <math><mn>5</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>42</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>210</mn><mo>≡</mo><mn>44</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>83</mn></math>).

question.question: A new binary operation <math><mo>★</mo></math> is defined such that for any two numbers <math><mi>a</mi></math> and <math><mi>b</mi></math>, <math><mi>a</mi><mo>★</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>ab</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Using this definition, what is the value of <math><mn>5</mn><mo>★</mo><mn>1</mn></math>?
question.explanation: To find <math><mn>5</mn><mo>★</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, substitute <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> into the definition: <math><mi>a</mi><mo>★</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>ab</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. This gives us <math><mn>5</mn><mo>★</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>−</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>47</mn></math>.

question.question: What is the average of the two smallest positive integer solutions to <math><mn>14</mn><mi>u</mi><mo>≡</mo><mn>46</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>100</mn></math>)?
question.explanation: Divide by <math><mn>2</mn></math>: <math><mn>7</mn><mi>u</mi><mo>≡</mo><mn>23</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>50</mn></math>). Multiply by <math><mn>7</mn></math>: <math><mo>−</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>≡</mo><mn>11</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>50</mn></math>) <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>u</mi><mo>≡</mo><mn>39</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>50</mn></math>). Smallest positives: <math><mn>39</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>89</mn></math>. Average <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>39</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>89</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></math>.

question.question: On a map, <math><mn>3</mn></math> inches represent <math><mn>10</mn></math> miles. If two buildings are <math><mn>53.25</mn></math> miles apart in real life, what is their map distance (in inches), expressed as a fraction?
question.explanation: <math><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mn>53.25</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>10</mn></mfrac></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15.975</mn></math> in <math><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mfrac><mn>39</mn><mn>40</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>639</mn><mn>40</mn></mfrac></math> inches.

question.question: A two-digit number has digits summing to 13; the difference between the number and its reverse is 27. What is the sum of the number and its reverse?
question.explanation: Let digits <math><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></math> with <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></math>. Sum of number and reverse: <math><mn>11</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>143</mn></math> (independent of order).

question.question: Grades 7 and 8 have 520 and 650 students, with 18 total council reps. For fair representation, how many reps should 8th grade have?
question.explanation: Share <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>650</mn><mrow><mn>520</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>650</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>650</mn><mn>1170</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></math>. <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>.

question.question: A linear map <math><mi>M</mi></math> sends <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>→</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>→</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Find the image of the line <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> under <math><mi>M</mi></math> (as <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>mx</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></math>).
question.explanation: From images, <math><mi>M</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mi>M</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Points on line <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math> map to <math><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math>; slope <math><mn>2</mn></math>, intercept <math><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: In how many ways can 5 students be selected from 6?
question.explanation: Combinations: <math><mi>C</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>.

question.question: Find all integer roots of <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
question.explanation: By Rational Root Theorem test divisors of <math><mn>14</mn></math>; only <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> satisfy the equation.

question.question: Determine the remainder of <math><mn>54</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>6</mn></math>).
question.explanation: <math><mn>54</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, so <math><mn>54</mn><mo>≡</mo><mn>0</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>6</mn></math>).

question.question: Between 30 and 50 students attend an archery class. The students cannot be divided into equal-sized groups (with more than 1 student per group). When Betty and Wilma join the class, the total still cannot be divided into equal-sized groups. How many students attended the class?
question.explanation: If the students cannot be divided into equal groups, the class size must be a prime number (only divisible by 1 and itself). After adding 2 people (Betty and Wilma), the total must also be prime. This means we need two consecutive odd primes (twin primes) in the range 30-50. The twin primes in this range are 41 and 43. Since the original class size is the smaller one, <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>41</mn></math>.

question.question: The cost of making gold-painted concrete cubes is proportional to the surface area for paint and proportional to the volume for concrete. A <math><mn>1</mn></math>-inch cube costs <math><mo>$</mo><mn>1.30</mn></math> and a <math><mn>2</mn></math>-inch cube costs <math><mo>$</mo><mn>6.80</mn></math>. What does a <math><mn>3</mn></math>-inch cube cost?
question.explanation: Let <math><mi>x</mi></math> be the cost per square inch of paint and <math><mi>y</mi></math> be the cost per cubic inch of concrete. For a <math><mn>1</mn></math>-inch cube: surface area <math><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> in², volume <math><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> in³, so <math><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.30</mn></math>. For a <math><mn>2</mn></math>-inch cube: surface area <math><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math> in², volume <math><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> in³, so <math><mn>24</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6.80</mn></math>. Solving: <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.40</mn></math>, <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.15</mn></math>. For a <math><mn>3</mn></math>-inch cube: surface area <math><mo>=</mo><mn>54</mn></math> in², volume <math><mo>=</mo><mn>27</mn></math> in³, so cost <math><mo>=</mo><mn>54</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>0.15</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>27</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>0.40</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>$</mo><mn>18.90</mn></math>.

question.question: In a figure with <math><mover><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>∥</mo><mover><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>¯</mo></mover></math>, <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>°</mo></math> and <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>35</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Find <math><mi>m</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>R</mi></math>.
question.explanation: In <math><mo>△</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi><mi>R</mi></math>, <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>35</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. With <math><mover><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>T</mi></mrow><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>∥</mo><mover><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>¯</mo></mover></math>, <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>S</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>R</mi></math> is supplementary to <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>R</mi></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>75</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>⌊</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⌋</mo></math> (floor function) for <math><mi>n</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></math> and <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>⌈</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⌉</mo></math> (ceiling function) for <math><mi>n</mi><mo><</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Compute <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mn>45</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><msup><mn>8</mn><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Evaluate each term: <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></math>: Since <math><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.047</mn><mo><</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, we use the ceiling function: <math><mo>⌈</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>⌉</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mn>45</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo></math>: Since <math><msqrt><mn>45</mn></msqrt><mo>≈</mo><mn>6.708</mn><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, we use the floor function: <math><mo>⌊</mo><msqrt><mn>45</mn></msqrt><mo>⌋</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>. <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><msup><mn>8</mn><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>)</mo></math>: Since <math><msup><mn>8</mn><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, we use the floor function: <math><mo>⌊</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⌋</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Sum: <math><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>.

question.question: Linda has <math><mo>$</mo><mn>27.47</mn></math>, Sherry has <math><mo>$</mo><mn>35.23</mn></math>, June has <math><mo>$</mo><mn>37.37</mn></math>, and Connie has <math><mo>$</mo><mn>26.52</mn></math>. After converting all their coins to bills, how many cents remain in total?
question.explanation: To find the remaining cents after converting coins to bills, we need the total amount modulo <math><mn>100</mn></math> (since bills are multiples of <math><mo>$</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></math> cents). Adding the cents portions: <math><mn>47</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>23</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>37</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>52</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>159</mn></math> cents. Since <math><mn>159</mn><mo>≡</mo><mn>59</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>100</mn></math>), there are <math><mn>59</mn></math> cents remaining.

question.question: For how many values of <math><mi>x</mi></math> is <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> not defined?
question.explanation: Undefined when denominator <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Two values.

question.question: If <math><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><msub><mi>log</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, find <math><mi>x</mi></math>.
question.explanation: From the first equation, using the product rule for logarithms: <math><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo>(</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, so <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math>. From the second equation: <math><msub><mi>log</mi><mi>y</mi></msub><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, so <math><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. Substituting into the first equation: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi></math>, which gives <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Factoring: <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math> or <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Since <math><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> (for the logarithms to be defined), and <math><mi>y</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math>, we must have <math><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Therefore, <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>.

question.question: When listing positive integers with exactly three positive divisors in ascending order, what is the fifth number?
question.explanation: Numbers with exactly three divisors are squares of primes: <math><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mn>11</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>121</mn></math>. Fifth is <math><mn>121</mn></math>.

question.question: If <math><mi>r</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mi>θ</mi></mrow></msup></math> is a root of <math><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>8</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> with <math><mi>r</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></math>, find the sum of all possible <math><mi>θ</mi></math>.
question.explanation: The polynomial can be factored as <math><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>9</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>. The roots satisfy <math><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>9</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> except <math><mi>z</mi><mo>≠</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> (which would make the denominator zero). For <math><msup><mi>z</mi><mn>9</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, we have <math><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>k</mi></mrow><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup></math> for <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn></math>. Excluding <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> (which gives <math><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>), we have 8 roots. The sum of their angles is <math><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mn>8</mn></munderover><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>k</mi></mrow><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>9</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mn>36</mn></mrow><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>π</mi></math>.

question.question: In the diagram, what is the area of the shaded triangle?
question.explanation: Base <math><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mtext>cm</mtext></math> and height <math><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mtext>cm</mtext></math>, so area <math><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mtext>cm</mtext><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.

question.question: The square root of <math><mi>t</mi></math> is greater than <math><mn>2</mn></math> and less than <math><mn>3.5</mn></math>. How many integer values of <math><mi>t</mi></math> satisfy this condition?
question.explanation: <math><mn>2</mn><mo><</mo><msqrt><mi>t</mi></msqrt><mo><</mo><mn>3.5</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mn>4</mn><mo><</mo><mi>t</mi><mo><</mo><mn>12.25</mn></math>. Integer <math><mi>t</mi></math> are <math><mn>5</mn><mo>–</mo><mn>12</mn></math> inclusive: <math><mn>8</mn></math> values.

question.question: Evaluate <math><msup><mrow><mo>⌈</mo><msqrt><mn>20</mn></msqrt><mo>⌉</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.
question.explanation: <math><mn>4</mn><mo><</mo><msqrt><mn>20</mn></msqrt><mo><</mo><mn>5</mn></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mo>⌈</mo><msqrt><mn>20</mn></msqrt><mo>⌉</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, so <math><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> with <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>. Find the maximum of <math><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></math>.
question.explanation: AM-GM on <math><mn>10</mn></math> terms gives <math><mn>10</mn><mo>≥</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><mn>27648</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>10</mn></mfrac></msup></math> <math><mo>⇒</mo></math> <math><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>≤</mo><mn>27648</mn></math>. Equality at <math><mi>a</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>:</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: A class of 30 students took a test. Scores: twenty 80s, eight 90s, and two 100s. What was the class average?
question.explanation: Total <math><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>80</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2520</mn></math>. Average <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2520</mn><mn>30</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>84</mn></math>.

question.question: At 50 mph, how far is a car driven in 2¾ hours? (mixed number)
question.explanation: Distance <math><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2.75</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>137.5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>137</mn><mo> </mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> miles.

question.question: In the 3×3 magic square shown (rows/cols/diagonals equal), what is n?
question.explanation: In a magic square, all rows, columns, and diagonals have the same sum. Row <math><mn>1</mn></math> sum: <math><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Row <math><mn>2</mn></math> sum: <math><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></math>. Setting these equal: <math><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, which gives <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>.

question.question: Compute <math><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mn>5</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>5</mn></msub><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>6</mn></msub><mn>7</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>7</mn></msub><mn>8</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Telescopes via change of base: <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>…</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mn>8</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mn>7</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mn>8</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: An unfair die has <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>F</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mi>n</mi></mfrac></math> (<math><mo>></mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math>), <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mtext>opposite</mtext><mo> </mo><mi>F</mi><mo>)</mo><mo><</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math>, others <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math>. Opposite faces sum to <math><mn>7</mn></math>. With two such dice, <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mtext>sum</mtext><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>47</mn><mn>288</mn></mfrac></math>. Find <math><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Let face <math><mi>F</mi></math> have probability <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>F</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></math> and its opposite face (which sums to <math><mn>7</mn></math> with <math><mi>F</mi></math>) have probability <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></math>. The other four faces each have probability <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math>. For two dice to sum to <math><mn>7</mn></math>, we need pairs that sum to <math><mn>7</mn></math>: <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Four of these pairs involve faces with probability <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math> each, contributing <math><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>36</mn></mfrac></math>. The two pairs involving <math><mi>F</mi></math> and its opposite contribute <math><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>36</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. Total: <math><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mn>36</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>47</mn><mn>288</mn></mfrac></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac></math>. Therefore, <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>F</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac></math> and <math><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>29</mn></math>.

question.question: A 300×400 ft rectangular field: Jim walks the diagonal; Martha walks along two sides. How many feet less does Jim walk?
question.explanation: Diagonal <math><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>300</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>400</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mtext>ft</mtext></math>. Martha: <math><mn>300</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>400</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>700</mn><mo> </mo><mtext>ft</mtext></math>. Difference: <math><mn>700</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>500</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mtext>ft</mtext></math>.

question.question: The two-digit number “B6,” where B is the tens digit, is the square of a positive integer. How many distinct possible values are there for B?
question.explanation: A two-digit number ending in <math><mn>6</mn></math> has the form <math><mn>10</mn><mi>B</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, where <math><mi>B</mi></math> is the tens digit. We need this to be a perfect square. Checking two-digit perfect squares: <math><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>, <math><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math>, <math><msup><mn>14</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>196</mn></math> (three digits). The two-digit squares ending in <math><mn>6</mn></math> are <math><mn>16</mn></math> and <math><mn>36</mn></math>, which give <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> or <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Therefore, there are <math><mn>2</mn></math> distinct possible values for <math><mi>B</mi></math>.

question.question: Find the sum of all complex solutions of <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2010</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Rewriting and clearing denominators yields a degree-<math><mn>8</mn></math> polynomial with leading terms <math><mn>2010</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>8</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mo>…</mo></math> so the sum of roots <math><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>2010</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>1005</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: For how many primes <math><mi>p</mi></math> does <math><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></math> (mod <math><mi>p</mi></math>) have no solution? Find the sum of all such primes.
question.explanation: The equation <math><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>≡</mo><mn>1</mn></math> (mod <math><mi>p</mi></math>) has a solution if and only if <math><mn>8</mn></math> is invertible modulo <math><mi>p</mi></math>, which requires <math><mi>gcd</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Since <math><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></math>, the only prime that shares a factor with <math><mn>8</mn></math> is <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Therefore, there is exactly <math><mn>1</mn></math> prime for which the equation has no solution, and the sum is <math><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>ω</mi></math> be a complex cube root of unity (i.e., <math><msup><mi>ω</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>). Compute <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: Combining over a common denominator: <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ω</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ω</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ω</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac></math>. Since <math><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ω</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> for any non-trivial cube root of unity, we have <math><mi>ω</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, so the numerator becomes <math><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. The denominator also simplifies to <math><mn>1</mn></math>, giving the result <math><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>n</mi></math> be a positive integer. Simplify <math><mfrac><mrow><munderover><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><munderover><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: Factor <math><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>. The product telescopes, with most factors canceling. The result simplifies to <math><mn>8</mn><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: A positive odd integer less than <math><mn>2010</mn></math> is chosen at random. The decimal expansion of its reciprocal terminates with probability <math><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mfrac></math> in lowest terms. Find <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></math>.
question.explanation: A decimal terminates if and only if the denominator (in lowest terms) has no prime factors other than <math><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mn>5</mn></math>. Since we're choosing an odd integer, it has no factor of <math><mn>2</mn></math>, so the reciprocal terminates if and only if the number is a power of <math><mn>5</mn></math>. The odd powers of <math><mn>5</mn></math> less than <math><mn>2010</mn></math> are: <math><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, <math><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></math>, <math><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>125</mn></math>, <math><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>625</mn></math>. There are <math><mn>5</mn></math> such numbers. The number of positive odd integers less than <math><mn>2010</mn></math> is <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>2010</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1005</mn></math>. The probability is <math><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>1005</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>201</mn></mfrac></math>, so <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>201</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>202</mn></math>.

question.question: Triangle <math><mi>ABC</mi></math> has area <math><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, where <math><mi>a</mi></math>, <math><mi>b</mi></math>, <math><mi>c</mi></math> are the sides opposite angles <math><mi>A</mi></math>, <math><mi>B</mi></math>, <math><mi>C</mi></math> respectively. Compute <math><mi>tan</mi><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi></math>.
question.explanation: The area formula gives <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>bc</mi><mo> </mo><mi>sin</mi><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>bc</mi></math>. Using the Law of Cosines, <math><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>bc</mi><mo> </mo><mi>cos</mi><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi></math>, we get <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>bc</mi><mo> </mo><mi>sin</mi><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>bc</mi><mo> </mo><mi>cos</mi><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>bc</mi></math>, which simplifies to <math><mi>sin</mi><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cos</mi><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi></math>. Using <math><msup><mi>sin</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, we get <math><mn>17</mn><msup><mi>cos</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>A</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>32</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, so <math><mi>cos</mi><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>15</mn><mn>17</mn></mfrac></math> and <math><mi>sin</mi><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>17</mn></mfrac></math>. Therefore, <math><mi>tan</mi><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>15</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Solve <math><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msqrt></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Squaring both sides: <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math>, which simplifies to <math><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math>. Isolating the square root and squaring again: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, which gives <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>. Checking: <math><msqrt><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>36</mn></msqrt></mrow></msqrt><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>−</mo><msqrt><mn>36</mn></msqrt></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>16</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>4</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>.

question.question: Four points <math><mi>A</mi></math>, <math><mi>B</mi></math>, <math><mi>C</mi></math>, and <math><mi>D</mi></math> form a square with side length <math><mn>5</mn></math>. Starting at any of these points and visiting the other three exactly once, what is the shortest possible total distance traveled?
question.explanation: To visit all four points, we need to travel along <math><mn>3</mn></math> edges. A distance of <math><mn>12</mn></math> would require three sides of length <math><mn>4</mn></math> each, which is impossible. The shortest path is achieved by routes like <math><mi>A</mi><mo>→</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>→</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>→</mo><mi>C</mi></math> or <math><mi>B</mi><mo>→</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>→</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>→</mo><mi>A</mi></math>, which have total distance <math><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></math> (using two sides and one diagonal).

question.question: A steel sphere of radius <math><mn>3</mn></math> inches fits exactly inside a cube (touching all six faces). What is the cube's volume (in cubic inches)?
question.explanation: If a sphere of radius <math><mn>3</mn></math> fits exactly inside a cube, the sphere's diameter equals the cube's side length. Since the diameter is <math><mn>6</mn></math> inches, the cube has side length <math><mn>6</mn></math> inches. The volume is <math><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>216</mn></math> cubic inches.

question.question: Determine the remainder modulo <math><mn>4</mn></math> of <math><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn></math>.
question.explanation: The sum <math><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>13</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>78</mn></math>. Alternatively, we can compute modulo <math><mn>4</mn></math>: the residues modulo <math><mn>4</mn></math> repeat as <math><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. There are <math><mn>3</mn></math> complete cycles, so <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>≡</mo><mn>2</mn></math> (mod <math><mn>4</mn></math>).

question.question: A shirt is on sale for $14.40, which is 60% off the original price. What was the original price?
question.explanation: If the shirt is <math><mn>60</mn><mo>%</mo></math> off, the sale price is <math><mn>40</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of the original price. Let <math><mi>p</mi></math> be the original price. Then <math><mn>0.40</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14.40</mn></math>, so <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>14.40</mn><mn>0.40</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math>. The original price was <math><mo>$</mo><mn>36</mn></math>.

question.question: For <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>|</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>|</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>|</mo></math> with <math><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mi>p</mi><mo><</mo><mn>15</mn></math>, find the minimum of <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math> over the interval <math><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>15</mn></math>.
question.explanation: On the interval <math><mo>[</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>]</mo></math>, we have <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>p</mi></math>, <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>15</mn></math>, and <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn></math> (since <math><mi>p</mi><mo><</mo><mn>15</mn></math>). Therefore, <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>30</mn></math>. This is a decreasing function, so it is minimized at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math>, giving <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math>.

question.question: A polynomial <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math> has integer coefficients, distinct integer roots, leading coefficient <math><mn>2</mn></math>, and constant term <math><mn>66</mn></math>. What is the least possible value of <math><mo>|</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>|</mo></math>, where <math><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> is the coefficient of the second-highest degree term?
question.explanation: If <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><munderover><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></math> with distinct integer roots <math><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>, then the product of roots is <math><mo>±</mo><mfrac><mn>66</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>33</mn></math>. The coefficient <math><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>. To minimize <math><mo>|</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>|</mo></math>, we need to minimize <math><mo>|</mo><munderover><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>|</mo></math>. The roots must be divisors of <math><mn>66</mn></math> and multiply to <math><mo>±</mo><mn>33</mn></math>. The minimal absolute sum is <math><mn>7</mn></math> (e.g., roots <math><mo>−</mo><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></math>), so <math><mo>|</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></math>.

question.question: Mr. Potato Head can be assembled with the following parts: hair (<math><mn>3</mn></math> options or bald), eyebrows (<math><mn>2</mn></math> options), eyes (<math><mn>1</mn></math> option), ears (<math><mn>2</mn></math> options), lips (<math><mn>2</mn></math> options), and shoes (<math><mn>2</mn></math> options). How many distinct personalities can be created?
question.explanation: By the multiplication principle, the total number of distinct combinations is <math><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></math>.

question.question: All vectors <math><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></math> whose projection onto <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> is zero lie on what line?
question.explanation: The projection of <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></math> onto <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> is zero if and only if <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is orthogonal to <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. This means <math><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, so <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></math>.

question.question: If <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></math>, find <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Expanding <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup></math> using the binomial theorem: <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></math>. Therefore, <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, and <math><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>{</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>∈</mo><msup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>:</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>b</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mtext>has a real root</mtext><mo>}</mo></math>. What is the area of <math><mi>S</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Using the substitution <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></math>, the equation reduces to a condition involving <math><mi>a</mi></math> and <math><mi>b</mi></math>. The condition for a real root is <math><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></math> over the unit square <math><mo>[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo><mo>⋅</mo><mo>[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>]</mo></math>. This defines a triangular region with vertices at <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, and <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, but restricted to the unit square gives a triangle with area <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Find the domain of <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>log</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac></math>, where all logarithms are base <math><mn>10</mn></math>.
question.explanation: We require: (1) <math><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>2</mn></math>, (2) <math><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>log</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> so <math><mi>log</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo><</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, which gives <math><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo><</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>102</mn></math>, and (3) the denominator <math><mi>log</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>log</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, so <math><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>log</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>≠</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, which gives <math><mi>log</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>≠</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>≠</mo><mn>10</mn></math>, meaning <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>12</mn></math>. Therefore, the domain is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>∪</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>102</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi></math> and <math><mi>w</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>. Find <math><mo>|</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>|</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Substituting <math><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi></math>: <math><mn>3</mn><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>i</mi></math> and <math><mn>5</mn><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>i</mi></math>. For complex numbers, <math><mo>|</mo><mfrac><mi>u</mi><mi>v</mi></mfrac><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mo>|</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>|</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>|</mo></mfrac></math>, so <math><mo>|</mo><mi>w</mi><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mo>|</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>i</mi><mo>|</mo><mo>|</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>i</mi><mo>|</mo></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>12</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>13</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: An equiangular octagon has sides of length <math><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> alternating (no two consecutive sides are equal). Find its area.
question.explanation: An equiangular octagon with alternating side lengths can be decomposed into <math><mn>5</mn></math> squares and <math><mn>4</mn></math> half-squares, each with side length <math><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. The area of each square is <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>, and each half-square has area <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>. Total area: <math><mn>5</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: A sequence is defined by <math><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></math> for <math><mi>i</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. If <math><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>, compute <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>9</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>9</mn></msup></math>.
question.explanation: If <math><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>, then the sequence has period <math><mn>2</mn></math> (or period dividing <math><mn>2</mn></math>). From <math><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></math> and <math><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>, we get <math><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></mfrac></math>, which simplifies to <math><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Therefore, <math><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Since <math><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>9</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> (by periodicity), we have <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mn>9</mn></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>9</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: In △ABC, altitudes AD and BE meet at H. If ∠BAC=54° and ∠ABC=52°, find ∠AHB.
question.explanation: In triangle <math><mo>△</mo><mi>ABC</mi></math>, <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>ACB</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>54</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>52</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>74</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Since <math><mi>AD</mi></math> and <math><mi>BE</mi></math> are altitudes, they are perpendicular to <math><mi>BC</mi></math> and <math><mi>AC</mi></math> respectively. In quadrilateral <math><mi>ABEH</mi></math>, the angles at <math><mi>A</mi></math> and <math><mi>B</mi></math> are <math><mn>54</mn><mo>°</mo></math> and <math><mn>52</mn><mo>°</mo></math> respectively.
