question.question: In circle <math><mi>O</mi></math>, the measures of three central angles are <math><mn>110</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, <math><mn>95</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, and <math><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is the measure of the remaining central angle that completes the circle?
question.explanation: All central angles around the center sum to <math><mn>360</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. So the missing angle is <math><mn>360</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>-</mo><mrow><mn>110</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>95</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>360</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>265</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>95</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. But note we subtracted incorrectly if we choose that; compute carefully: <math><mn>110</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>95</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>265</mn></math>, and <math><mn>360</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>265</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>95</mn></math>, so the remaining angle is <math><mn>95</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: A circle has radius <math><mn>10</mn></math> cm and a chord of length <math><mn>12</mn></math> cm. What is the perpendicular distance from the center to the chord?
question.explanation: A perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects the chord. Half the chord is <math><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>. Using the right triangle with hypotenuse <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>, distance <math><mi>d</mi></math> satisfies <math><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></math>, so <math><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>.

question.question: In circle <math><mi>O</mi></math>, arc <math><mover><mi>XY</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math> measures <math><mn>144</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is the measure of the central angle <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>XOY</mi></math> that intercepts arc <math><mover><mi>XY</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math>?
question.explanation: A central angle has the same degree measure as its intercepted arc. Therefore <math><mi>m</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>XOY</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi><mover><mi>XY</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>144</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: A circle has circumference <math><mn>36</mn><mi>π</mi></math> cm. What is the radius of the circle?
question.explanation: Circumference is <math><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi></math>. Set <math><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn><mi>π</mi></math>, then divide by <math><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></math> to get <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn></math>. But note the equation: <math><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn><mi>π</mi></math> gives <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>36</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn></math>, so the correct choice is <math><mn>18</mn></math>.

question.question: In a circle, a chord has length <math><mn>16</mn></math> and the perpendicular distance from the center to the chord is <math><mn>6</mn></math>. What is the radius of the circle?
question.explanation: A perpendicular from the center bisects the chord, so half the chord is <math><mfrac><mn>16</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>. In the right triangle, the radius is the hypotenuse, so <math><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn></math>, hence <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>.

question.question: A circle has radius <math><mn>15</mn></math> cm. A central angle measures <math><mn>24</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is the length of the intercepted arc?
question.explanation: Use <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi></math>. With <math><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math> and <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math>, <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>24</mn><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>15</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>30</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. So the arc length is <math><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></math> cm.

question.question: A circle has radius <math><mn>8</mn></math> meters. An arc has length <math><mn>12</mn></math> meters. What is the measure of the corresponding central angle in degrees? (Use <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>θ</mi></math> with <math><mi>θ</mi></math> in radians, then convert to degrees.)
question.explanation: First find the angle in radians: <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>θ</mi></math> so <math><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>s</mi><mi>r</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> radians. Convert to degrees: <math><mi>θ</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>°</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mn>180</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>270</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac></math>. Since <math><mi>π</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>3.1416</mn></math>, <math><mfrac><mn>270</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mfrac><mn>270</mn><mn>3.1416</mn></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mn>86</mn></math> degrees.

question.question: Which statement is always true for a diameter of a circle?
choices: <math><mtext>A diameter is any segment with endpoints on the circle.</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>A diameter is the longest chord of the circle.</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>A diameter is tangent to the circle at exactly one point.</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>A diameter has length equal to the radius.</mtext></math>
question.explanation: A diameter is a chord that passes through the center, and it is the longest chord in the circle. Also <math><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>r</mi></math>, so it is not equal to the radius.

question.question: In circle <math><mi>O</mi></math>, chord <math><mi>AB</mi></math> is longer than chord <math><mi>CD</mi></math>. Which comparison must be true about the intercepted minor arcs?
choices: <math><mtext>There is no relationship between chord length and arc measure.</mtext></math>
question.explanation: In the same circle, longer chords intercept larger arcs. Since <math><mi>AB</mi></math> is longer than <math><mi>CD</mi></math>, the intercepted minor arc satisfies <math><mi>m</mi><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover><mo>></mo><mi>m</mi><mover><mi>CD</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math>.

question.question: In circle <math><mi>O</mi></math>, a chord <math><mi>MN</mi></math> has length <math><mn>14</mn></math>. The radius of the circle is <math><mn>25</mn></math>. What is the perpendicular distance from the center to chord <math><mi>MN</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Half the chord is <math><mfrac><mn>14</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>. Using <math><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><msup><mrow><mfrac><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></msqrt></math>, we get <math><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><msup><mn>25</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>625</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>49</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>576</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>.

question.question: A radius is drawn from the center of a circle perpendicular to a chord. Which result must be true?
choices: <math><mtext>The radius is parallel to the chord.</mtext></math>
question.explanation: A radius (or diameter) drawn perpendicular to a chord bisects the chord. This creates two congruent right triangles, so the chord is cut into two equal parts.

question.question: Two central angles in the same circle intercept arcs with measures <math><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn></math> degrees and <math><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>30</mn></math> degrees. If the arcs are congruent, what is the value of <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Congruent arcs have equal measures, so set <math><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>30</mn></math>. Then <math><mn>40</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math>.

question.question: From an external point <math><mi>P</mi></math>, two tangents <math><mover><mi>PA</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> and <math><mover><mi>PB</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> touch a circle at points <math><mi>A</mi></math> and <math><mi>B</mi></math>. If <math><mi>PA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mi>PB</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, what is <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Tangent segments from the same external point are congruent, so <math><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></math>. Then <math><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: A line <math><mi>l</mi></math> is tangent to circle <math><mi>O</mi></math> at point <math><mi>T</mi></math>. Which angle measure must be true for the radius <math><mover><mi>OT</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> and the tangent line at <math><mi>T</mi></math>?
question.explanation: By the Tangent–Radius Theorem, a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so the angle is <math><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: From an external point <math><mi>P</mi></math>, a tangent touches circle <math><mi>O</mi></math> at <math><mi>T</mi></math>. If <math><mi>OP</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math> and the radius <math><mi>OT</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, what is the tangent length <math><mi>PT</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Since <math><mover><mi>OT</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> is perpendicular to the tangent at <math><mi>T</mi></math>, triangle <math><mi>OPT</mi></math> is right at <math><mi>T</mi></math>. Use Pythagorean Theorem: <math><msup><mi>OP</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>OT</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>PT</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. Then <math><msup><mi>PT</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>^</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>^</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></math>, so <math><mi>PT</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>.

question.question: From an external point <math><mi>P</mi></math>, a tangent <math><mover><mi>PT</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> and a secant passing through the circle at <math><mi>E</mi></math> and <math><mi>F</mi></math> are drawn. If <math><mi>PT</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math> and <math><mi>PE</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>, what is the total secant length <math><mi>PF</mi></math>?
question.explanation: By the Tangent–Secant Theorem, <math><msup><mi>PT</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>PE</mi><mo>·</mo><mi>PF</mi></math>. So <math><mn>12</mn><mo>^</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>PF</mi></math>, giving <math><mn>144</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>PF</mi></math>, hence <math><mi>PF</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>.

question.question: Two secants are drawn from the same external point <math><mi>P</mi></math>. On the first secant, <math><mi>PA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> and <math><mi>PB</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math>. On the second secant, <math><mi>PC</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. What is <math><mi>PD</mi></math>?
question.explanation: By the Secant–Secant Theorem, <math><mi>PA</mi><mo>·</mo><mi>PB</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>PC</mi><mo>·</mo><mi>PD</mi></math>. So <math><mn>4</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>PD</mi></math>, giving <math><mn>80</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>PD</mi></math> and <math><mi>PD</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>.

question.question: From an external point <math><mi>P</mi></math>, a tangent <math><mover><mi>PT</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> and a secant through the circle at <math><mi>E</mi></math> and <math><mi>F</mi></math> are drawn. If <math><mi>PT</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mi>PE</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, and <math><mi>PF</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn></math>, what is the value of <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Use the Tangent–Secant Theorem: <math><msup><mi>PT</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>PE</mi><mo>·</mo><mi>PF</mi></math>. So <math><msup><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Expand: <math><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>60</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>56</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, which factors as <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. The positive solution is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>.

question.question: Two secants are drawn from external point <math><mi>P</mi></math>. On one secant, <math><mi>PA</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></math> and <math><mi>PB</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn></math>. On the other secant, <math><mi>PC</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> and <math><mi>PD</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>. What is <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Apply the Secant–Secant Theorem: <math><mi>PA</mi><mo>·</mo><mi>PB</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>PC</mi><mo>·</mo><mi>PD</mi></math>. So <math><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>144</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>x</mi><mo>^</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>144</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Factoring gives <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. The positive solution is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>.

question.question: From an external point <math><mi>P</mi></math>, two tangents <math><mover><mi>PA</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> and <math><mover><mi>PB</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> are drawn to a circle. If <math><mi>PA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math>, what is <math><mi>PB</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Tangent segments from the same external point are congruent, so <math><mi>PA</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>PB</mi></math>. Therefore <math><mi>PB</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math>.

question.question: From an external point <math><mi>P</mi></math>, two tangents are drawn to a circle at <math><mi>A</mi></math> and <math><mi>B</mi></math>. If <math><mi>PA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and <math><mi>PB</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>17</mn></math>, what is <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Tangent segments from the same external point are equal, so <math><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>17</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>.

question.question: A tangent <math><mover><mi>PT</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> and a chord <math><mover><mi>TA</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> form an angle at point <math><mi>T</mi></math> on a circle. If the intercepted arc <math><mover><mi>AT</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math> measures <math><mn>110</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, what is the measure of the angle formed by the tangent and the chord?
question.explanation: The angle formed by a tangent and a chord equals half the measure of the intercepted arc. So the angle is <math><mfrac><mn>110</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>55</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: A tangent <math><mover><mi>PT</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> and a chord <math><mover><mi>TR</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> form an angle of <math><mn>35</mn><mo>°</mo></math> at point <math><mi>T</mi></math> on the circle. What is the measure of the intercepted arc <math><mover><mi>TR</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math>?
question.explanation: For a tangent–chord angle, <math><mi>m</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>PTR</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>m</mi><mover><mi>TR</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math>. Thus <math><mi>m</mi><mover><mi>TR</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>35</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>70</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: From an external point <math><mi>P</mi></math>, a tangent touches circle <math><mi>O</mi></math> at <math><mi>T</mi></math>. If <math><mi>OP</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></math> and the radius <math><mi>OT</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>, what is <math><mi>PT</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at <math><mi>T</mi></math>, triangle <math><mi>OPT</mi></math> is right at <math><mi>T</mi></math>. Then <math><msup><mi>PT</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>OP</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><msup><mi>OT</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>^</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>^</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>625</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>576</mn></math>, so <math><mi>PT</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>576</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>.

question.question: From an external point <math><mi>P</mi></math>, a secant intersects the circle at <math><mi>E</mi></math> and <math><mi>F</mi></math>. If the external part is <math><mi>PE</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> and the portion inside the circle is <math><mi>EF</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>, what is the tangent length <math><mi>PT</mi></math> drawn from the same point <math><mi>P</mi></math>?
question.explanation: First find the whole secant length: <math><mi>PF</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>PE</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>EF</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>. Then apply the Tangent–Secant Theorem: <math><msup><mi>PT</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>PE</mi><mo>·</mo><mi>PF</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math>. So <math><mi>PT</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>.

question.question: Two secants are drawn from external point <math><mi>P</mi></math>. On the first secant, the external segment is <math><mi>PA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></math> and the inside segment is <math><mi>AB</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>. On the second secant, the external segment is <math><mi>PC</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math> and the inside segment is <math><mi>CD</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>. What is <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Whole lengths are <math><mi>PB</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>PA</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>AB</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></math> and <math><mi>PD</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>PC</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>CD</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. Secant–secant gives <math><mi>PA</mi><mo>·</mo><mi>PB</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>PC</mi><mo>·</mo><mi>PD</mi></math>. So <math><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>. Expanding gives <math><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>27</mn></math>, so <math><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>27</mn></math> and <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: Two secants are drawn from an external point <math><mi>P</mi></math>. On one secant, <math><mi>PA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and <math><mi>PB</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math>. On the other secant, <math><mi>PC</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. What is <math><mi>PD</mi></math>?
question.explanation: By the Secant–Secant Theorem, <math><mi>PA</mi><mo>·</mo><mi>PB</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>PC</mi><mo>·</mo><mi>PD</mi></math>. So <math><mn>5</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>PD</mi></math>. Then <math><mn>75</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>PD</mi></math>, giving <math><mi>PD</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></math>.

question.question: In circle <math><mi>O</mi></math>, minor arc <math><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math> measures <math><mn>92</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Point <math><mi>P</mi></math> lies on the circle, and <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi></math> is an inscribed angle intercepting arc <math><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math>. What is <math><mi>m</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi></math>?
question.explanation: By the Inscribed Angle Theorem, an inscribed angle equals half its intercepted arc. So <math><mi>m</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>92</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>46</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: An inscribed angle in a circle measures <math><mn>37</mn><mo>°</mo></math> and intercepts arc <math><mover><mi>CD</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math>. What is the measure of arc <math><mover><mi>CD</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math>?
question.explanation: The intercepted arc is twice the inscribed angle. So <math><mi>m</mi><mover><mi>CD</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>37</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>74</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: Points <math><mi>A</mi></math> and <math><mi>B</mi></math> are endpoints of a diameter of a circle. Point <math><mi>P</mi></math> lies on the circle, forming inscribed angle <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi></math>. What is <math><mi>m</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi></math>?
question.explanation: An inscribed angle that intercepts a semicircle (a diameter) is a right angle. Therefore <math><mi>m</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: In circle <math><mi>O</mi></math>, central angle <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>AOB</mi></math> measures <math><mn>120</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. An inscribed angle <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi></math> intercepts the same arc <math><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math>. What is <math><mi>m</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi></math>?
question.explanation: The central angle equals the arc measure, so arc <math><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math> is <math><mn>120</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. An inscribed angle intercepting that arc is half: <math><mfrac><mn>120</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: Tangent <math><mi>PT</mi></math> touches a circle at <math><mi>T</mi></math>, and chord <math><mover><mi>TR</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> forms angle <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>PTR</mi></math> at <math><mi>T</mi></math>. If the intercepted arc <math><mover><mi>TR</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math> measures <math><mn>146</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, what is <math><mi>m</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>PTR</mi></math>?
question.explanation: By the Tangent–Chord Theorem, the angle formed by a tangent and a chord equals half its intercepted arc. So <math><mi>m</mi><mo>∠</mo><mi>PTR</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>146</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>73</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: A circle has radius <math><mn>9</mn></math> cm. The minor arc <math><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math> has measure <math><mn>40</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is the length of arc <math><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math>?
question.explanation: Use <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi></math>. With <math><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></math> and <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>, <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>40</mn><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>18</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></math> cm.

question.question: A circle has radius <math><mn>12</mn></math> meters, and a sector has central angle <math><mn>150</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is the area of the sector?
question.explanation: Sector area is <math><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. With <math><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>150</mn></math> and <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>, <math><mi>Area</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>150</mn><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>144</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>144</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. But <math><mn>60</mn><mi>π</mi></math> is not listed; check the fraction: <math><mfrac><mn>150</mn><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac></math>, and <math><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>144</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></math>. Therefore the sector area is <math><mn>60</mn><mi>π</mi></math> square meters.

question.question: Quadrilateral <math><mi>ABCD</mi></math> is inscribed in a circle. If <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>°</mo></math> and <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, what is <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary: <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mo>∠</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. So <math><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>180</mn></math>. Then <math><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>180</mn></math>, so <math><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>200</mn></math> and <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></math>. (Thus the correct choice is <math><mn>25</mn></math>.)

question.question: Two inscribed angles intercept the same arc <math><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math> in the same circle. If one inscribed angle measures <math><mn>58</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, what is the measure of the other inscribed angle?
question.explanation: Inscribed angles that intercept the same arc are congruent, so the other inscribed angle also measures <math><mn>58</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: An inscribed angle <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi></math> measures <math><mn>48</mn><mo>°</mo></math> in a circle of radius <math><mn>10</mn></math> cm. Find the length of the intercepted minor arc <math><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math>.
question.explanation: The intercepted arc measure is twice the inscribed angle: <math><mi>m</mi><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>48</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>96</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Arc length is <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>96</mn><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo></math> = <math><mfrac><mn>96</mn><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>π</mi></math> = <math><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>30</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>π</mi></math> = <math><mfrac><mn>160</mn><mn>30</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi></math> = <math><mfrac><mn>16</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi></math>. (Thus the correct choice is <math><mfrac><mn>16</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi></math>.)

question.question: A circle has radius <math><mn>6</mn></math> inches. A sector is formed by a central angle of <math><mn>75</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is the length of the arc of the sector?
question.explanation: Arc length is <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>m</mi><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi></math>. With <math><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>75</mn></math> and <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>75</mn><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>60</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi></math> inches.

question.question: In circle <math><mi>O</mi></math>, inscribed angle <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi></math> measures <math><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, and the corresponding central angle <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>AOB</mi></math> measures <math><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Both intercept arc <math><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>⌢</mo></mover></math>. What is <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: For the same arc, the central angle equals the arc measure, and the inscribed angle is half the arc. Thus <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>AOB</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>·</mo><mo>∠</mo><mi>APB</mi></math>. So <math><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Then <math><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn></math>, giving <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math>. Since <math><mn>20</mn></math> is not listed, the correct option set does not match; however solving the relationship gives <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math>.

question.question: A circle has radius <math><mn>14</mn></math> cm. A sector has area <math><mn>49</mn><mi>π</mi></math> cm<math><msup><mtext>2</mtext><mn> </mn></msup>. What is the measure of the central angle of the sector in degrees?
question.explanation: Circle area is <math><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>^</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>196</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. The sector fraction is <math><mfrac><mn>49</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac><mo>/</mo><mrow><mn>196</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>. So the central angle is <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>360</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. (Thus the correct choice is <math><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.)

question.question: Quadrilateral <math><mi>ABCD</mi></math> is inscribed in a circle. If <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>112</mn><mo>°</mo></math> and <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, and <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>28</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, what is <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary. Here <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>B</mi></math> and <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>D</mi></math> are opposite, so <math><mo>∠</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>+</mo><mo>∠</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Then <math><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>28</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>180</mn></math>, so <math><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>180</mn></math>, hence <math><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>144</mn></math> and <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>. Since <math><mn>24</mn></math> is not listed, the choice set does not match; the correct solution is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>.

question.question: A circle has radius <math><mn>5</mn></math> units. An arc has length <math><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></math> units. What is the measure of the central angle in radians?
question.explanation: Using <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>θ</mi></math>, we get <math><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>s</mi><mi>r</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></mfrac><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi></math> radians.

question.question: Euclid’s Parallel Postulate states that through a point not on a line, exactly one line can be drawn parallel to the given line. Which alternative postulate describes hyperbolic geometry?
choices: Through a point not on a line, exactly one parallel line can be drawn.
Through a point not on a line, infinitely many parallel lines can be drawn.
Through a point not on a line, no parallel lines can be drawn.
Any two lines in a plane are parallel and never intersect.
question.explanation: Hyperbolic geometry replaces Euclid’s Parallel Postulate with the statement that through a point not on a line, there are infinitely many distinct lines that do not meet the given line (infinitely many parallels).

question.question: In spherical geometry, “lines” are modeled by great circles. Which statement about great circles is correct?
choices: Two different great circles can be parallel and never intersect.
Any two different great circles intersect in exactly two opposite points on the sphere.
Two different great circles intersect in exactly one point.
Great circles are finite and always have endpoints.
question.explanation: A great circle is the intersection of a sphere with a plane through the center. Two distinct such planes intersect in a line through the center, which meets the sphere in two opposite points, so two distinct great circles intersect in two antipodal points.

question.question: A spherical triangle on Earth is formed by the equator and two meridians that are <math><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math> apart; the third vertex is the North Pole. Each corner angle is <math><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is the sum of the triangle’s angles?
question.explanation: The angles are <math><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, <math><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, and <math><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Their sum is <math><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>270</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, which is greater than <math><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo></math> as expected in spherical geometry.

question.question: On a unit sphere (radius <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>), a spherical triangle has angles <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>70</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, and <math><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is the area of the spherical triangle?
question.explanation: The spherical excess is <math><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>70</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. On a sphere, area <math><mo>=</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mi>pi</mi><mn>180</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. With <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, area <math><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mi>pi</mi><mn>180</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>pi</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Two points on Earth subtend a central angle of <math><mi>Δ</mi><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.5</mn></math> radians at Earth's center. Using <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6371</mn></math> km, what is the surface distance between the points along a great-circle route?
question.explanation: Great-circle surface distance is <math><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>Δ</mi><mi>σ</mi></math>. Substituting gives <math><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6371</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3185.5</mn></math> km.

question.question: When using formulas like <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>θ</mi></math>, angles must be in radians. What is <math><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math> in radians?
question.explanation: Convert degrees to radians using <math><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>°</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>180</mn></mfrac></math>. Thus <math><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>180</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: In Euclidean geometry, two triangles can be similar without being congruent. In spherical geometry (using great circles as sides), what is true about similar triangles?
choices: Similar triangles never exist on a sphere.
Two spherical triangles can be similar without being congruent, just like in the plane.
All similar spherical triangles are congruent.
Spherical triangles are congruent only when their angle sum is <math><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.
question.explanation: On a sphere, the angles determine the area via spherical excess, and scaling does not work the same way as in the plane. As a result, if two spherical triangles have the same angles (similarity), they must have the same side lengths as well, making them congruent.

question.question: A pilot wants the shortest route between two far-apart cities on Earth. Ignoring wind and obstacles, which path best models the shortest travel distance on Earth’s surface?
choices: A straight line drawn on a flat map, because maps preserve distance perfectly.
An arc of a great circle passing through the two cities.
A path that keeps the plane at constant latitude (a parallel).
A path made of two perpendicular segments, like a right angle turn.
question.explanation: On a sphere, geodesics (shortest paths on the surface) are great-circle arcs. Routes that look “curved” on many maps are often great-circle routes.

question.question: A spherical triangle has side lengths (measured as central angles) <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math> and <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, and the included angle is <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Using the spherical law of cosines <math><mi>cos</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>cos</mi><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>sin</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>sin</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>cos</mi><mi>A</mi></math>, what is <math><mi>a</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Compute: <math><mi>cos</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>cos</mi><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo><mi>cos</mi><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo><mi>cos</mi><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Since <math><mi>cos</mi><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mi>sin</mi><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, this becomes <math><mi>cos</mi><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. Therefore <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: A spherical triangle on a sphere of radius <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> has angle sum <math><mn>185</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is its area?
question.explanation: Spherical excess <math><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>185</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Area <math><mo>=</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mi>pi</mi><mn>180</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> becomes <math><mn>5</mn><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mi>pi</mi><mn>180</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>20</mn><mi>pi</mi><mn>180</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>pi</mi><mn>9</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Which geometry is characterized by the statement “Through a point not on a given line, there are no lines parallel to the given line,” a situation that matches great circles on a sphere?
question.explanation: Elliptic (spherical) geometry has no parallel lines: great circles always intersect, so a “parallel” great circle does not exist.

question.question: In the Poincaré disk model of hyperbolic geometry, what do “lines” look like inside the disk?
choices: Only straight Euclidean line segments, and they can touch the boundary anywhere.
Circular arcs (or diameters) that meet the boundary circle at right angles.
Spirals that wrap infinitely many times around the center.
Any curve drawn inside the disk is considered a line.
question.explanation: In the Poincaré disk model, hyperbolic lines are represented by Euclidean circular arcs (or diameters) that intersect the boundary circle orthogonally (at right angles).

question.question: Cartographers make flat maps of Earth (approximately spherical). Which statement best explains why distortion is unavoidable?
choices: A sphere can be flattened to a plane while preserving all distances and angles everywhere.
A sphere can be flattened to a plane while preserving all areas and distances everywhere.
Any flat map of a sphere must distort at least one of: distances, angles, or areas.
Distortion occurs only because maps are drawn with imperfect tools, not because of geometry.
question.explanation: A curved surface cannot be laid flat without changing some geometric measurements. In practice, projections can preserve certain properties (like angles or areas) but must distort others, so at least one of distances, angles, or areas is distorted somewhere on the map.

question.question: A triangle in a certain geometry has angle sum <math><mn>150</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Compared with Euclidean triangles, what does this suggest about the geometry’s curvature?
choices: It suggests positive curvature, like spherical geometry.
It suggests negative curvature, like hyperbolic geometry.
It suggests the geometry must be Euclidean because the sum is close to <math><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.
It suggests curvature is impossible to determine from angle sums.
question.explanation: In hyperbolic geometry (negative curvature), triangle angle sums are less than <math><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. In spherical geometry (positive curvature), they exceed <math><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: Two cities lie at latitude <math><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo><mi>N</mi></math> and their longitudes differ by <math><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Using the approximation <math><mi>Δ</mi><mi>σ</mi><mo>≈</mo><mi>Δ</mi><mi>λ</mi><mo>cos</mo><mi>φ</mi></math> (with degrees converted consistently) and Earth radius <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6371</mn></math> km, what is the approximate great-circle distance?
question.explanation: Compute <math><mi>Δ</mi><mi>σ</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>·</mo><mo>cos</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>90</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>·</mo><mn>0.866</mn><mo>≈</mo><mn>77.94</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Convert to radians: <math><mn>77.94</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>180</mn></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.36</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>Δ</mi><mi>σ</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>6371</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>1.36</mn><mo>≈</mo><mn>8667</mn></math> km, closest to <math><mn>8700</mn></math> km.

question.question: A triangle has base <math><mn>14</mn></math> units and height <math><mn>9</mn></math> units (the height is perpendicular to the base). What is the area of the triangle?
question.explanation: Use <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>b</mi><mi>h</mi></math>. Substitute <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></math> and <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>: <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>63</mn></math>.

question.question: A parallelogram has base <math><mn>12</mn></math> cm and perpendicular height <math><mn>7</mn></math> cm. What is its area?
question.explanation: For a parallelogram, <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>h</mi></math>. So <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>84</mn></math>.

question.question: A trapezoid has bases <math><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> m and <math><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></math> m, and height <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> m. What is the area of the trapezoid?
question.explanation: Use <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>)</mo><mi>h</mi></math>. Then <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mn>22</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>66</mn></math>.

question.question: A circle has diameter <math><mn>10</mn></math> inches. What is the area of the circle in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: The radius is half the diameter: <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Area is <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn><mi>π</mi></math>.

question.question: A sector of a circle has radius <math><mn>12</mn></math> cm and central angle <math><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is the area of the sector in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Use <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>θ</mi><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. With <math><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></math> and <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>: <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>60</mn><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>144</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>144</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn><mi>π</mi></math>.

question.question: A rectangle measures <math><mn>20</mn></math> units by <math><mn>10</mn></math> units. A semicircle with diameter <math><mn>10</mn></math> units is removed from one side of the rectangle. What is the area of the remaining region in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Rectangle area is <math><mn>20</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>200</mn></math>. The semicircle has radius <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, so its area is <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>25</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi></math>. Subtract: <math><mn>200</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>25</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi></math>.

question.question: A regular pentagon has side length <math><mn>8</mn></math> units and apothem <math><mn>5.5</mn></math> units. What is the area of the pentagon?
question.explanation: Perimeter is <math><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></math>. Regular polygon area: <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>P</mi></math>. So <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mn>5.5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>110</mn></math>.

question.question: A regular hexagon has side length <math><mn>10</mn></math> units. Using <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>÷</mo><mi>tan</mi><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>180</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></math> with <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, what is the apothem of the hexagon in exact form?
question.explanation: For a regular hexagon, <math><mfrac><mn>180</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>180</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Then <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>10</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>÷</mo><mi>tan</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>÷</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></math>.

question.question: If the radius of a circle is doubled, by what factor does the area of the circle change?
question.explanation: Circle area is <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. Doubling <math><mi>r</mi></math> gives <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><msup><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, so the area becomes 4 times as large.

question.question: A circle has area <math><mn>49</mn><mi>π</mi></math> square units. What is the radius of the circle?
question.explanation: Using <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, set <math><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>49</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. Divide by <math><mi>π</mi></math>: <math><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>49</mn></math>, so <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>.

question.question: A square has perimeter <math><mn>36</mn></math> cm. What is the area of the square?
question.explanation: For a square, <math><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>s</mi></math>. So <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>36</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>9</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>81</mn></math>.

question.question: A shaded region is an annulus (a ring) formed by two concentric circles with radii <math><mn>8</mn></math> and <math><mn>5</mn></math>. What is the area of the shaded region in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Area of the annulus is outer circle minus inner circle: <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>39</mn><mi>π</mi></math>.

question.question: A composite figure is made by attaching a semicircle (diameter <math><mn>8</mn></math> units) to the hypotenuse-free side of a right triangle with legs <math><mn>6</mn></math> and <math><mn>8</mn></math>. What is the total area of the composite figure in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Triangle area: <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>. Semicircle has radius <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, so its area is <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>16</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. Total: <math><mn>24</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>π</mi></math>.

question.question: A sector has radius <math><mn>10</mn></math> cm and arc length <math><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></math> cm. Using the relationship <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></math> for sector area (where <math><mi>s</mi></math> is arc length), what is the area of the sector in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Use <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>r</mi><mi>s</mi></math>. Substitute <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math> and <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi></math>: <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn><mi>π</mi></math>.

question.question: A regular hexagon has side length <math><mn>6</mn></math> units. What is the exact area of the hexagon?
question.explanation: A regular hexagon can be decomposed into 6 equilateral triangles of side <math><mn>6</mn></math>. Each equilateral triangle has area <math><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>4</mn></mfrac><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></math>. Multiply by 6: <math><mn>6</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>9</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>54</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></math>.

question.question: A right rectangular prism has length <math><mn>8</mn></math> cm, width <math><mn>5</mn></math> cm, and height <math><mn>3</mn></math> cm. What is the total surface area of the prism?
question.explanation: Use <math><mtext>SA = 2(lw + lh + wh)</mtext></math>. Compute <math><mi>lw</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></math>, <math><mi>lh</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>, <math><mi>wh</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math>. Sum is <math><mn>79</mn></math>; multiply by 2 gives <math><mn>158</mn></math> square centimeters.

question.question: A right prism has a triangular base with area <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn></math> square units and base perimeter <math><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math> units. The prism’s height is <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math> units. What is the total surface area of the prism?
question.explanation: For a prism, <math><mtext>SA = 2B + Ph</mtext></math>. Substitute: <math><mn>2</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>150</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>186</mn></math>.

question.question: A cylinder has radius <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> in and height <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math> in. What is its total surface area in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Cylinder surface area: <math><mtext>SA = 2πr² + 2πrh</mtext></math>. Compute <math><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn><mi>π</mi></math> and <math><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. Total is <math><mn>112</mn><mi>π</mi></math>.

question.question: A cone has radius <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> cm and slant height <math><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> cm. What is the total surface area of the cone in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Cone surface area: <math><mtext>SA = πr² + πrl</mtext></math>. Compute <math><mi>π</mi><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>π</mi></math> and <math><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. Total is <math><mn>24</mn><mi>π</mi></math>.

question.question: A sphere has radius <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math> cm. What is its surface area in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Sphere surface area: <math><mtext>SA = 4πr²</mtext></math>. With <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>, <math><mi>SA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><msup><mn>7</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>196</mn><mi>π</mi></math>.

question.question: A square pyramid has base side length <math><mn>6</mn></math> m and slant height <math><mn>5</mn></math> m. What is the total surface area of the pyramid?
question.explanation: Base area is <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math>. Perimeter is <math><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>24</mn></math>. Lateral area is <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>P</mi><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mn>24</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></math>. Total: <math><mn>36</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>96</mn></math>.

question.question: A right prism has base area <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn></math> square units, base perimeter <math><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>22</mn></math> units, and height <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math> units. What is the lateral area of the prism?
question.explanation: For a prism, lateral area is <math><mi>LA</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>h</mi></math>. So <math><mi>LA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>22</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>198</mn></math>.

question.question: A cylinder has total surface area <math><mn>150</mn><mi>π</mi></math> square units and radius <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> units. What is the height <math><mi>h</mi></math> of the cylinder?
question.explanation: Use <math><mtext>SA = 2πr² + 2πrh</mtext></math>. Substitute <math><mi>SA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>150</mn><mi>π</mi></math> and <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>: <math><mn>150</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>h</mi></math>. Subtract: <math><mn>100</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>h</mi></math>, so <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>. (Correct choice is C.)

question.question: A cone has radius <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> cm and vertical height <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> cm. The slant height is <math><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msqrt></math>. What is the total surface area of the cone in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Compute slant height: <math><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>36</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>64</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>100</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>. Cone SA is <math><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>60</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. (Correct choice is B.)

question.question: A composite solid is formed by placing a hemisphere of radius <math><mn>4</mn></math> on top of a cylinder with the same radius <math><mn>4</mn></math> and height <math><mn>9</mn></math>. The circular face where they join is not exposed. What is the total exposed surface area in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Exposed area includes: cylinder lateral area <math><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>72</mn><mi>π</mi></math>, cylinder bottom base <math><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mi>π</mi></math>, and hemisphere curved area (half of sphere) <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. Total <math><mo>=</mo><mn>72</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>32</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. None match exactly; rewriting: <math><mn>120</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>72</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>48</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. The closest listed intended decomposition is choice B, but the correct exposed area is <math><mn>120</mn><mi>π</mi></math>.

question.question: A paint can is shaped like a cylinder with radius <math><mn>6</mn></math> cm and height <math><mn>20</mn></math> cm. Only the lateral surface (not the top or bottom) will be painted. What is the lateral area in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Cylinder lateral area is <math><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>h</mi></math>. Substitute: <math><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>240</mn><mi>π</mi></math>, which corresponds to choice B. (Correct choice is B.)

question.question: A triangular prism has a right-triangle base with legs <math><mn>5</mn></math> cm and <math><mn>12</mn></math> cm. The prism height (length) is <math><mn>9</mn></math> cm. What is the total surface area of the prism?
question.explanation: Base area: <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn></math>. Hypotenuse is <math><msqrt><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>12</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>169</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></math>, so perimeter <math><mi>P</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn></math>. Lateral area <math><mi>LA</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>270</mn></math>. Total <math><mi>SA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>B</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>LA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>270</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>330</mn></math>. The computed value is <math><mn>330</mn></math>, which is not listed; the correct surface area should be <math><mn>330</mn></math> square centimeters.

question.question: A sphere has diameter <math><mn>12</mn></math> inches. What is its surface area in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Diameter <math><mn>12</mn></math> means radius <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>. Surface area is <math><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>144</mn><mi>π</mi></math>, which is choice A. (Correct choice is A.)

question.question: A cone has total surface area <math><mn>96</mn><mi>π</mi></math> square units and radius <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> units. What is the slant height <math><mi>l</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Cone SA is <math><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi><mi>l</mi></math>. Substitute: <math><mn>96</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mi>l</mi></math>. Divide by <math><mi>π</mi></math>: <math><mn>96</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>l</mi></math>. Then <math><mn>60</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>l</mi></math>, so <math><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>, which is choice D. (Correct choice is D.)

question.question: A shipping box is a cube with side length <math><mn>0.5</mn></math> m. What is the total surface area of the cube in square centimeters?
question.explanation: Cube surface area is <math><mn>6</mn><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. Convert <math><mn>0.5</mn></math> m to cm: <math><mn>0.5</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></math> cm. Then <math><mi>SA</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>·</mo><msup><mn>50</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>2500</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>15000</mn></math> square centimeters.

question.question: A right rectangular prism has length <math><mn>8</mn></math> cm, width <math><mn>5</mn></math> cm, and height <math><mn>6</mn></math> cm. What is the volume of the prism?
question.explanation: For a prism, <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>h</mi></math>. Here the base is a rectangle with area <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></math>. Multiply by height <math><mn>6</mn></math>: <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>240</mn></math> cm<math><msup><mtext>3</mtext><mn> </mn></msup>.

question.question: A right circular cylinder has radius <math><mn>4</mn></math> in and height <math><mn>9</mn></math> in. What is the volume of the cylinder in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Cylinder volume is <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>h</mi></math>. With <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> and <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>, <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>·</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>·</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>144</mn><mi>π</mi></math> in<math><msup><mtext>3</mtext><mn> </mn></msup>.

question.question: A square pyramid has a square base with side length <math><mn>12</mn></math> m and perpendicular height <math><mn>9</mn></math> m. What is the volume of the pyramid?
question.explanation: Pyramid volume is <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>B</mi><mi>h</mi></math>. Base area <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>12</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>144</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>144</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1296</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>432</mn></math> m<math><msup><mtext>3</mtext><mn> </mn></msup>.

question.question: A right cone has radius <math><mn>6</mn></math> cm and perpendicular height <math><mn>10</mn></math> cm. What is the volume of the cone in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Cone volume is <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>h</mi></math>. With <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math> and <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>, <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>360</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn><mi>π</mi></math> cm<math><msup><mtext>3</mtext><mn> </mn></msup>.

question.question: A sphere has radius <math><mn>3</mn></math> ft. What is the volume of the sphere in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Sphere volume is <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math>. With <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>27</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn><mi>π</mi></math> ft<math><msup><mtext>3</mtext><mn> </mn></msup>.

question.question: A triangular prism has a triangular base with base length <math><mn>10</mn></math> cm and height <math><mn>6</mn></math> cm. The prism height (distance between the triangular bases) is <math><mn>12</mn></math> cm. What is the volume of the prism?
question.explanation: Volume of a prism is <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>h</mi></math>. The base area is a triangle: <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn></math>. Multiply by prism height <math><mn>12</mn></math>: <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>360</mn></math> cm<math><msup><mtext>3</mtext><mn> </mn></msup>.

question.question: A cylinder has volume <math><mn>480</mn><mi>π</mi></math> cubic centimeters and radius <math><mn>8</mn></math> cm. What is the height of the cylinder?
question.explanation: Cylinder volume is <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>h</mi></math>. Substitute <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>480</mn><mi>π</mi></math> and <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>: <math><mn>480</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>64</mn><mo>·</mo><mi>h</mi></math>. Cancel <math><mi>π</mi></math>: <math><mn>480</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn><mi>h</mi></math>, so <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>480</mn><mn>64</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>7.5</mn></math>.

question.question: A cone and a cylinder have the same base radius <math><mn>5</mn></math> cm and the same height <math><mn>12</mn></math> cm. What is the volume of the cone?
question.explanation: Cone volume is <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>h</mi></math>. With <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>, <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>300</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn><mi>π</mi></math> cm<math><msup><mtext>3</mtext><mn> </mn></msup>.

question.question: A hemisphere has radius <math><mn>6</mn></math> inches. What is the volume of the hemisphere in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: A hemisphere is half a sphere. Sphere volume is <math><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math>. With <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, sphere volume is <math><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>216</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>288</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. Half of that is <math><mn>144</mn><mi>π</mi></math> in<math><msup><mtext>3</mtext><mn> </mn></msup>.

question.question: A sphere has volume <math><mn>3</mn><mn>6</mn><mi>π</mi></math> cubic units. What is the radius of the sphere?
question.explanation: Use <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math>. Set <math><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. Cancel <math><mi>π</mi></math>: <math><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math>. Multiply by <math><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>: <math><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>27</mn></math>, so <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: A right prism has a base area of <math><mn>3</mn><mn>0</mn></math> square units and height <math><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></math> units. What is the volume of the prism?
question.explanation: For a prism, <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>h</mi></math>. With <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn></math> and <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></math>, <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>420</mn></math> cubic units.

question.question: A composite solid is made by placing a right circular cone on top of a right circular cylinder. Both have radius <math><mn>3</mn></math> cm. The cylinder height is <math><mn>8</mn></math> cm and the cone height is <math><mn>6</mn></math> cm. What is the total volume in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Cylinder volume: <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>72</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. Cone volume: <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. Total volume <math><mo>=</mo><mn>72</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>90</mn><mi>π</mi></math>.

question.question: A cylindrical hole of radius <math><mn>2</mn></math> cm is drilled straight through the center of a solid cylinder of radius <math><mn>6</mn></math> cm and height <math><mn>10</mn></math> cm. What is the volume of the remaining solid in terms of <math><mi>π</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Remaining volume = (large cylinder) − (hole cylinder). Large: <math><mi>π</mi><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>·</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>360</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. Hole: <math><mi>π</mi><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>·</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>π</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn><mi>π</mi></math>. Difference: <math><mn>360</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>40</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>320</mn><mi>π</mi></math>.

question.question: A cone has volume <math><mn>96</mn><mi>π</mi></math> cubic centimeters and radius <math><mn>4</mn></math> cm. What is the height of the cone?
question.explanation: Cone volume: <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>h</mi></math>. Substitute <math><mn>96</mn><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>π</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>·</mo><mi>h</mi></math>. Cancel <math><mi>π</mi></math>: <math><mn>96</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>16</mn><mi>h</mi></mfrac><mn>3</mn></math>. Multiply by <math><mn>3</mn></math>: <math><mn>288</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mi>h</mi></math>, so <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn></math>. (Thus the correct choice is <math><mn>18</mn></math>.)

question.question: A square pyramid has volume <math><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></math> cubic units and height <math><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></math> units. What is the area of its square base?
question.explanation: For a pyramid, <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mi>B</mi><mi>h</mi></math>. So <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mi>V</mi></mfrac><mi>h</mi></math>. With <math><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></math> and <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>, <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>256</mn></mfrac><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>768</mn></mfrac><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></math>. (Thus base area is <math><mn>64</mn></math>.)

question.question: Point <math><mi>P</mi></math> has coordinates <math><mo>(</mo><mn>-4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. In which quadrant is point <math><mi>P</mi></math> located?
question.explanation: Quadrant II contains points with <math><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mi>y</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Since <math><mo>(</mo><mn>-4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></math> has negative <math><mi>x</mi></math> and positive <math><mi>y</mi></math>, it lies in Quadrant II.

question.question: Point <math><mi>A</mi></math> is at <math><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. If you start at the origin and plot <math><mi>A</mi></math>, how many units do you move left or right, and then up or down?
question.explanation: For <math><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, move right <math><mn>6</mn></math> units (positive <math><mi>x</mi></math>) and down <math><mn>3</mn></math> units (negative <math><mi>y</mi></math>).

question.question: Find the distance between <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mi>Q</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: The points have the same <math><mi>x</mi></math>-coordinate, so the segment is vertical. Distance is <math><mo>|</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>-</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>|</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>.

question.question: Find the distance between <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mi>B</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: The points have the same <math><mi>y</mi></math>-coordinate, so the segment is horizontal. Distance is <math><mo>|</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>−3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>|</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>.

question.question: Use the distance formula to find the length of segment <math><mover><mi>CD</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> where <math><mi>C</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-2</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mi>D</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Compute <math><mi>Δx</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>-</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and <math><mi>Δy</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>-</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>-2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>12</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>25</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>144</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>169</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></math>.

question.question: Find the midpoint of segment <math><mover><mi>EF</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> with endpoints <math><mi>E</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>-6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mi>F</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Midpoint is <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>-6</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>-4</mn></mfrac><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>-2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. (Thus the correct choice is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>-2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.)

question.question: Point <math><mi>M</mi></math> is the midpoint of <math><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math>. If <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>-8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mi>M</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>-2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, what are the coordinates of <math><mi>B</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Midpoint formula: <math><mn>-2</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>-8</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> gives <math><mn>-4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>-8</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Also <math><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> gives <math><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi></math>, so <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. Thus <math><mi>B</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: Triangle <math><mi>ABC</mi></math> has vertices <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mi>B</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, and <math><mi>C</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Which statement is true based on distances?
question.explanation: Compute <math><mi>AC</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and <math><mi>BC</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, so <math><mi>AC</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>BC</mi></math>.

question.question: A circle has center <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and passes through the point <math><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. What is the radius of the circle?
question.explanation: Radius is the distance between center and the point. <math><mi>Δx</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><mi>Δy</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. So <math><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>16</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>25</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. (Thus the correct choice is <math><mn>5</mn></math>.)

question.question: Determine whether segment <math><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> has length <math><mn>10</mn></math> when <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>−2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mi>B</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Compute <math><mi>Δ</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>−2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> and <math><mi>Δ</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>. Distance <math><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>64</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>36</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>100</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>, so the length is <math><mn>10</mn></math>.

question.question: Points <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mi>B</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, <math><mi>C</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, and <math><mi>D</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math> form quadrilateral <math><mi>ABCD</mi></math>. Which statement best describes <math><mi>ABCD</mi></math> using coordinate distances?
choices: <math><mtext>It is a kite because two adjacent sides are equal.</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>It is a rectangle because opposite sides are equal and adjacent sides are perpendicular (one horizontal and one vertical).</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>It is a rhombus because all sides are the same length.</mtext></math>
question.explanation: Segment <math><mover><mi>AB</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> is horizontal (same <math><mi>y</mi></math>) and <math><mover><mi>BC</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></math> is vertical (same <math><mi>x</mi></math>), so they are perpendicular.
