So <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mfrac><mi>sin</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>sin</mi><mi>A</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mfrac><mi>sin</mi><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mfrac><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></math>.

question.question: In <math><mo>△</mo><mi>ABC</mi></math>, suppose <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>, and <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Use the Law of Cosines to find <math><mi>a</mi></math> (to the nearest tenth).
question.explanation: Law of Cosines: <math><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>cos</mi><mi>A</mi></math>. So <math><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>81</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo><mi>cos</mi><mn>50</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, giving <math><mi>a</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>7.0</mn></math>.

question.question: In <math><mo>△</mo><mi>ABC</mi></math>, sides are <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn></math>, and <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>. Find <math><mi>B</mi></math> (the angle opposite side <math><mi>b</mi></math>) to the nearest tenth.
question.explanation: Use Law of Cosines for angle <math><mi>B</mi></math>: <math><mi>cos</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>. Substituting gives <math><mi>B</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>93.6</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: In <math><mo>△</mo><mi>ABC</mi></math>, suppose <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>38</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>, and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math> (an <math><mi>SSA</mi></math> situation). Which set lists all possible values of <math><mi>B</mi></math> (to the nearest tenth) that could work?
question.explanation: Law of Sines gives <math><mi>sin</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>b</mi><mi>sin</mi><mi>A</mi></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>a</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mi>sin</mi><mn>38</mn><mo>°</mo></mfrac><mn>10</mn></math>, so <math><mi>B</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>47.6</mn><mo>°</mo></math> or <math><mi>B</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>47.6</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>132.4</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Both keep <math><mi>A</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi><mo><</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, so both are possible.

question.question: In <math><mo>△</mo><mi>ABC</mi></math>, suppose <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></math> (an <math><mi>SSA</mi></math> situation). How many triangles satisfy these measurements?
question.explanation: Using Law of Sines, <math><mi>sin</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>b</mi><mi>sin</mi><mi>A</mi></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>a</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>13</mn><mi>sin</mi><mn>25</mn><mo>°</mo></mfrac><mn>5</mn></math>, which is greater than <math><mn>1</mn></math>. Since <math><mi>sin</mi><mi>B</mi></math> cannot exceed <math><mn>1</mn></math>, no triangle exists.

question.question: In <math><mo>△</mo><mi>ABC</mi></math>, suppose <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, <math><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, and <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>. What is side <math><mi>c</mi></math> in exact form?
question.explanation: First find <math><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>180</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>105</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. By Law of Sines, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mfrac><mi>sin</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>sin</mi><mi>A</mi></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mfrac><mi>sin</mi><mn>105</mn><mo>°</mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>sin</mi><mn>105</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Since <math><mi>sin</mi><mn>105</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>, then <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>·</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: A triangle has side lengths <math><mn>9</mn></math>, <math><mn>10</mn></math>, and <math><mn>17</mn></math>. What is the area of the triangle?
question.explanation: Use Heron’s Formula. The semiperimeter is <math><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>17</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn></math>. Area <math><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mi>s</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>17</mn><mo>)</mo></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>18</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>1</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>1296</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math>.

question.question: In <math><mo>△</mo><mi>ABC</mi></math>, suppose <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>, and the included angle <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>71</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is the area of the triangle (to the nearest tenth)?
question.explanation: Use <math><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi><mo>sin</mo><mi>A</mi></math>. Then <math><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mn>13</mn><mo>)(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>sin</mo><mn>71</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>61.5</mn></math>.

question.question: In a triangle, the sides have lengths <math><mn>9</mn></math>, <math><mn>11</mn></math>, and <math><mn>13</mn></math>. Let <math><mi>C</mi></math> be the angle opposite the side of length <math><mn>13</mn></math>. What is <math><mi>C</mi></math> (to the nearest tenth)?
question.explanation: Use Law of Cosines with <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn></math>, <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>11</mn></math>: <math><mi>cos</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>81</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>121</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>169</mn><mn>198</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></math>. Thus <math><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>80.4</mn><mo>°</mo></math>.

question.question: From a lighthouse, Ship 1 is <math><mn>10</mn></math> km away at a bearing of <math><mn>030</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, and Ship 2 is <math><mn>12</mn></math> km away at a bearing of <math><mn>110</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Approximately how far apart are the two ships?
question.explanation: The included angle between the routes is <math><mn>110</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. By Law of Cosines, <math><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>12</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>cos</mo><mn>80</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, so <math><mi>d</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>14.2</mn></math> km.

question.question: A surveyor measures two sides of a triangular plot as <math><mn>50</mn><mtext> m</mtext></math> and <math><mn>70</mn><mtext> m</mtext></math> with an included angle of <math><mn>40</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is the length of the third side (to the nearest tenth)?
question.explanation: This is an <math><mi>SAS</mi></math> case, so use Law of Cosines: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>50</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>70</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>)(</mo><mn>70</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>cos</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Solving gives <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>45.1</mn></math> m.

question.question: In <math><mo>△</mo><mi>ABC</mi></math>, two sides have lengths <math><mn>15</mn></math> and <math><mn>20</mn></math> with included angle <math><mn>35</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is the length of the third side (to the nearest tenth)?
question.explanation: Use Law of Cosines: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>15</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>20</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>)(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>)</mo><mi>cos</mi><mn>35</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Then <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>11.6</mn></math>.

question.question: In <math><mo>△</mo><mi>ABC</mi></math>, suppose <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo></math>, <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>, and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math> (an <math><mi>SSA</mi></math> situation). How many different triangles are possible?
question.explanation: Compute the altitude to side <math><mi>b</mi></math>: <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>sin</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>sin</mi><mn>30</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>. Since <math><mi>h</mi><mo><</mo><mi>a</mi><mo><</mo><mi>b</mi></math> (because <math><mn>6</mn><mo><</mo><mn>8</mn><mo><</mo><mn>12</mn></math>), the ambiguous case produces <math><mn>2</mn></math> possible triangles.

question.question: A triangle has side lengths <math><mn>6</mn></math> and <math><mn>10</mn></math> with included angle <math><mn>120</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. What is the area in exact form?
question.explanation: Use <math><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mi>sin</mi><mi>C</mi></math>. Then <math><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo><mi>sin</mi><mn>120</mn><mo>°</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>·</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></math>.

question.question: Consider the quadratic function <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Which statement correctly describes its vertex and translation from the parent function <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>?
choices: Vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>; shifted right 4 units and up 1 unit
Vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>-4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>; shifted left 4 units and up 1 unit
Vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>; shifted right 4 units and down 1 unit
Vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>-4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>; shifted left 4 units and down 1 unit
question.explanation: In vertex form <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></math>, the vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></math>. Here <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> and <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, so the vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, meaning the graph shifts right 4 and up 1 from <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.

question.question: Start with the parent function <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. After shifting the graph left 5 units and down 2 units (with no stretch or reflection), what is the new equation in vertex form?
question.explanation: A left shift by 5 changes <math><mi>x</mi></math> to <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. A downward shift by 2 subtracts 2. So the equation is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: For the function <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, which statement is true about its transformations compared with <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>?
choices: It shifts left 1 unit, down 4 units, and becomes narrower
It shifts right 1 unit, up 4 units, and becomes wider
It shifts right 4 units, up 1 unit, and becomes wider
It shifts left 4 units, down 1 unit, and becomes narrower
question.explanation: Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>, <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, and <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. So the graph shifts right 1 and up 4. Because <math><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>|</mo><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, the parabola is vertically compressed and appears wider.

question.question: A parabola is obtained from <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> by reflecting across the x-axis, stretching vertically by a factor of 4, shifting right 2 units, and shifting down 1 unit. What is the equation of the transformed function?
question.explanation: Reflection across the x-axis makes <math><mi>a</mi></math> negative, and a vertical stretch by 4 gives <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Shifting right 2 gives <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, and shifting down 1 subtracts 1. So <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: A quadratic function has vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, opens downward, and passes through the point <math><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-5</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. What is its equation in vertex form?
question.explanation: With vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, write <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Substitute <math><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-5</mn><mo>)</mo></math>: <math><mn>-5</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math> so <math><mn>-5</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, giving <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-2</mn></math>. Thus the equation is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: Which parabola is wider than the parent function <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>?
question.explanation: A parabola is wider than <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> when <math><mn>0</mn><mo><</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>|</mo><mo><</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Only choice B has <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math>, which makes the parabola wider (a vertical compression).

question.question: Reflect the graph of <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> across the x-axis and then shift it up 6 units. What is the resulting equation?
question.explanation: Reflecting across the x-axis multiplies the function by <math><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, giving <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. Shifting up 6 units adds 6: <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></math>.

question.question: Rewrite <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math> in vertex form and identify its vertex. Which option gives the correct vertex form?
question.explanation: Factor and complete the square: <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Then <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. So <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. The vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: Two functions are <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. What is the main difference between their graphs?
choices: <math><mi>g</mi></math> is reflected across the x-axis compared to <math><mi>f</mi></math>
question.explanation: Both have the same <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> term and <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, so there is no stretch or reflection. The constant term changes from <math><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> to <math><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, which is a net change of <math><mn>-5</mn></math>. Therefore <math><mi>g</mi></math> is shifted down 5 units from <math><mi>f</mi></math>.

question.question: The function <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></math> represents a parabola. What is the maximum value of <math><mi>y</mi></math> for this function?
question.explanation: Because <math><mi>a</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, the parabola opens downward, so the vertex gives the maximum value. The vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, so the maximum <math><mi>y</mi></math>-value is <math><mn>7</mn></math>.

question.question: A parabola has vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and passes through the origin <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. What is the equation in vertex form?
question.explanation: With vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, write <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Substitute <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math>: <math><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Thus <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>, giving <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: Which equation represents a parabola with vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, opening upward, and vertically stretched by a factor of 3?
question.explanation: Vertex form is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></math>. For vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, we need <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> and <math><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Opening upward and stretched by 3 means <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. So choice A is correct.

question.question: The function <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn></math> is in vertex form. What is the axis of symmetry of this parabola?
question.explanation: In <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></math>, the axis of symmetry is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi></math>. Here <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></math> means <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-4</mn></math>, so the axis is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-4</mn></math>.

question.question: A parabola has equation <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and passes through <math><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>28</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. What is the value of <math><mi>a</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Substitute <math><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>28</mn><mo>)</mo></math> into <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>: <math><mn>28</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Then <math><mn>27</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>a</mi></math>, so <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: Which change will move the graph of <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> down 6 units without changing its shape or orientation?
question.explanation: A vertical translation down by 6 subtracts 6 from the output, giving <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></math>. This does not change the parabola’s width or opening direction.

question.question: A student claims that in <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, the graph shifts left 3 units because of <math><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Which statement correctly addresses the claim?
choices: The student is correct; <math><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math> always shifts left
The student is incorrect; <math><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math> shifts right 3 units
The student is correct; <math><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math> shifts down 3 units
The student is incorrect; <math><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math> causes a reflection
question.explanation: In vertex form <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></math>, the graph shifts right when <math><mi>h</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Since <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, the parabola shifts right 3 units (the sign inside is opposite the direction).

question.question: The parabola <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math> passes through the point <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. What is the value of <math><mi>a</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Substitute <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-6</mn><mo>)</mo></math> into <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math>: <math><mn>-6</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Then <math><mn>-8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi></math>, so <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-2</mn></math>.

question.question: Consider the quadratic function in vertex form <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Which choice correctly gives the vertex and the axis of symmetry?
question.explanation: In vertex form <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></math>, the vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></math> and the axis is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi></math>. Here <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, so the vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and the axis is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: A quadratic function is given in standard form: <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. What is the equation of the axis of symmetry?
question.explanation: For <math><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math>, the axis of symmetry is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: The quadratic function <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> opens in which direction, and what does that mean about its vertex?
choices: <math><mtext>Opens up; the vertex is a minimum.</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>Opens down; the vertex is a maximum.</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>Opens up; the vertex is a maximum.</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>Opens down; the vertex is a minimum.</mtext></math>
question.explanation: The leading coefficient is <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, which is negative, so the parabola opens down. When a parabola opens down, its vertex is the highest point, so it represents a maximum.

question.question: A quadratic function is <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></math>. What is the y-intercept of the graph?
question.explanation: The y-intercept occurs when <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Compute <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>. So the y-intercept is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: Find the x-intercepts (zeros) of <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Set <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Factor the difference of squares: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. So <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> or <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: For <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, what does the discriminant tell you about the number of real x-intercepts?
question.explanation: Compute the discriminant <math><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></math> for <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>31</mn></math>. Since <math><mi>D</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, there are no real zeros, so the graph has no real x-intercepts.

question.question: A quadratic function has vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and opens upward. Which of the following is the correct range?
question.explanation: If a parabola opens upward, its vertex gives the minimum value. With vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, the smallest <math><mi>y</mi></math>-value is <math><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, so the range is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>≥</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: Rewrite <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn></math> in vertex form and identify the vertex.
question.explanation: Complete the square: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn></math>. Then <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, so <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></math>. The vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: For <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, what is the average rate of change from <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> to <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>?
question.explanation: Average rate of change from <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> to <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> is <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>-</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>. Compute <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Then <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.

question.paragraph: A rectangular garden is being designed next to a wall. Only three sides need fencing. If <math><mi>x</mi></math> is the length (in meters) of each side perpendicular to the wall, and the side parallel to the wall is <math><mn>20</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></math>, then the area is <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.question: Based on the quadratic model <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math>, what value of <math><mi>x</mi></math> gives the maximum area?
question.explanation: First expand: <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, so <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math>. The maximum occurs at the vertex, where <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>.

question.question: A quadratic function has vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and passes through the point <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Which equation matches the function?
question.explanation: Use vertex form: <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></math>. With vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, we have <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, so <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Substitute point <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>: <math><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn></math>, so <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Thus the equation is <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: Which statement best describes how the value of <math><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>|</mo></math> affects the graph of <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>?
choices: <math><mtext>The value of </mtext><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>|</mo><mtext> only changes the vertex location.</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>The value of </mtext><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>|</mo><mtext> changes the axis of symmetry.</mtext></math>
question.explanation: In <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, increasing <math><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>|</mo></math> stretches the graph vertically, which makes the parabola appear narrower. Decreasing <math><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>|</mo></math> compresses it vertically, making it wider.

question.question: A quadratic function is <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. What is the maximum value of the function?
question.explanation: Since <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, the parabola opens down and has a maximum at the vertex. The vertex x-value is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Wait carefully: <math><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>, and <math><mn>9</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, so the maximum value is <math><mn>4</mn></math>. Therefore the correct choice is <math><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: For what value of <math><mi>k</mi></math> does the quadratic equation <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> have exactly one real solution?
question.explanation: A quadratic has exactly one real solution when the discriminant is zero: <math><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></math>, so <math><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>k</mi></math>. Set equal to zero: <math><mn>16</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> gives <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: Which quadratic function is a horizontal shift of <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> left by 2 units and a vertical shift up by 7 units?
question.explanation: A left shift by 2 replaces <math><mi>x</mi></math> with <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math>: <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. A vertical shift up by 7 adds <math><mn>7</mn></math>. So the function is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></math>.

question.question: A quadratic function is <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. Which statement is true about its x-intercepts?
choices: <math><mtext>It has exactly one real x-intercept (the parabola is tangent to the x-axis).</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>The number of x-intercepts depends on the domain.</mtext></math>
question.explanation: Use the discriminant with <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>144</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math>. Wait: <math><mn>144</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math> which is positive, suggesting two real zeros. However, notice the function can be factored: <math><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, so it actually has two distinct intercepts. Therefore the correct statement should be choice A, not B. The correct selection is: two distinct real x-intercepts.

question.question: A quadratic function in vertex form is <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. If the graph passes through <math><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, what is <math><mi>a</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Substitute the point into the function: <math><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Then <math><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, so <math><mi>a</mi><mo>·</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> and <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: The axis of symmetry of a quadratic function is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Which statement must be true?
choices: <math><mtext>The function has exactly two real zeros.</mtext></math>
question.explanation: The axis of symmetry is the vertical line passing through the vertex. If the axis is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, then the vertex must have x-coordinate <math><mn>5</mn></math>.

question.question: Consider the quadratic function in vertex form <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Which choice correctly gives the vertex and the axis of symmetry?
question.explanation: In vertex form <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></math>, the vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></math> and the axis is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi></math>. Here <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, so the vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and the axis is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: A quadratic function is given in standard form: <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. What is the equation of the axis of symmetry?
question.explanation: For <math><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math>, the axis of symmetry is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: The quadratic function <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> opens in which direction, and what does that mean about its vertex?
choices: <math><mtext>Opens up; the vertex is a minimum.</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>Opens down; the vertex is a maximum.</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>Opens up; the vertex is a maximum.</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>Opens down; the vertex is a minimum.</mtext></math>
question.explanation: The leading coefficient is <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, which is negative, so the parabola opens down. When a parabola opens down, its vertex is the highest point, so it represents a maximum.

question.question: A quadratic function is <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></math>. What is the y-intercept of the graph?
question.explanation: The y-intercept occurs when <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Compute <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>. So the y-intercept is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: Find the x-intercepts (zeros) of <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Set <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Factor the difference of squares: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. So <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> or <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: For <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, what does the discriminant tell you about the number of real x-intercepts?
question.explanation: Compute the discriminant <math><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></math> for <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>31</mn></math>. Since <math><mi>D</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, there are no real zeros, so the graph has no real x-intercepts.

question.question: A quadratic function has vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and opens upward. Which of the following is the correct range?
question.explanation: If a parabola opens upward, its vertex gives the minimum value. With vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, the smallest <math><mi>y</mi></math>-value is <math><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, so the range is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>≥</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: Rewrite <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn></math> in vertex form and identify the vertex.
question.explanation: Complete the square: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn></math>. Then <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, so <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></math>. The vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: For <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, what is the average rate of change from <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> to <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>?
question.explanation: Average rate of change from <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> to <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> is <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>-</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>. Compute <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Then <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.

question.paragraph: A rectangular garden is being designed next to a wall. Only three sides need fencing. If <math><mi>x</mi></math> is the length (in meters) of each side perpendicular to the wall, and the side parallel to the wall is <math><mn>20</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></math>, then the area is <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.question: Based on the quadratic model <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math>, what value of <math><mi>x</mi></math> gives the maximum area?
question.explanation: First expand: <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, so <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math>. The maximum occurs at the vertex, where <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>.

question.question: A quadratic function has vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and passes through the point <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Which equation matches the function?
question.explanation: Use vertex form: <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></math>. With vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, we have <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, so <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Substitute point <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>: <math><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn></math>, so <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Thus the equation is <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: Which statement best describes how the value of <math><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>|</mo></math> affects the graph of <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>?
choices: <math><mtext>The value of </mtext><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>|</mo><mtext> only changes the vertex location.</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>The value of </mtext><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>|</mo><mtext> changes the axis of symmetry.</mtext></math>
question.explanation: In <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, increasing <math><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>|</mo></math> stretches the graph vertically, which makes the parabola appear narrower. Decreasing <math><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>|</mo></math> compresses it vertically, making it wider.

question.question: A quadratic function is <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. What is the maximum value of the function?
question.explanation: Since <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, the parabola opens down and has a maximum at the vertex. The vertex x-value is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Wait carefully: <math><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>, and <math><mn>9</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, so the maximum value is <math><mn>4</mn></math>. Therefore the correct choice is <math><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: For what value of <math><mi>k</mi></math> does the quadratic equation <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> have exactly one real solution?
question.explanation: A quadratic has exactly one real solution when the discriminant is zero: <math><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></math>, so <math><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>k</mi></math>. Set equal to zero: <math><mn>16</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> gives <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: Which quadratic function is a horizontal shift of <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> left by 2 units and a vertical shift up by 7 units?
question.explanation: A left shift by 2 replaces <math><mi>x</mi></math> with <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math>: <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. A vertical shift up by 7 adds <math><mn>7</mn></math>. So the function is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></math>.

question.question: A quadratic function is <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. Which statement is true about its x-intercepts?
choices: <math><mtext>It has exactly one real x-intercept (the parabola is tangent to the x-axis).</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>The number of x-intercepts depends on the domain.</mtext></math>
question.explanation: Use the discriminant with <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>144</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math>. Wait: <math><mn>144</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>108</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn></math> which is positive, suggesting two real zeros. However, notice the function can be factored: <math><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, so it actually has two distinct intercepts. Therefore the correct statement should be choice A, not B. The correct selection is: two distinct real x-intercepts.

question.question: A quadratic function in vertex form is <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. If the graph passes through <math><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, what is <math><mi>a</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Substitute the point into the function: <math><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Then <math><mn>9</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, so <math><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> and <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: The axis of symmetry of a quadratic function is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Which statement must be true?
choices: <math><mtext>The function has exactly two real zeros.</mtext></math>
question.explanation: The axis of symmetry is the vertical line passing through the vertex. If the axis is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, then the vertex must have x-coordinate <math><mn>5</mn></math>.

question.question: A parabola is given by <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>. What is the value of <math><mi>p</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Compare <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> with <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>. Here <math><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math>, so <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: For the parabola <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>-12</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>, what is its vertex?
question.explanation: In <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>, the vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></math>. Here <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, so the vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: A parabola has vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and focus <math><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. What is its directrix?
question.explanation: For a vertical parabola, <math><mi>p</mi></math> is the directed distance from vertex to focus. Here <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. The directrix is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>p</mi></math>, so <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>-1</mn></math>. However the focus is above the vertex, so the directrix must be equally far below: <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>-1</mn></math>. (This corresponds to choice A.) The correct directrix is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-1</mn></math>.

question.question: The parabola <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math> is in vertex form. What are the focus and directrix?
question.explanation: Here the vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>-2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. For <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></math>, <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>. With <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>, <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Focus is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>-2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Directrix is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>-2</mn></math>.

question.question: A parabola is given by <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>. What is the focus?
question.explanation: This is horizontal form <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>. Here <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-1</mn></math>, <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, and <math><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math> so <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Focus is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: Which directrix corresponds to the parabola <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>y</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Write <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>y</mi></math> as <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>. Then <math><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></math>, so <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Directrix is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>-3</mn></math>.

question.question: A parabola has vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-2</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and directrix <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-6</mn></math>. What is its focus?
question.explanation: For a vertical parabola, directrix is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>p</mi></math>. With <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-2</mn></math> and directrix <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-6</mn></math>, we solve <math><mn>-6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>-2</mn><mo>-</mo><mi>p</mi></math>, giving <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Focus is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Therefore the correct focus is choice B. (Focus must be 4 units above the vertex because the directrix is 4 units below.)

question.question: Find the equation of the parabola with vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and focus <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Assume it opens vertically. Which equation is correct?
question.explanation: Vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Since focus is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, the directed distance is <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. For vertical form, <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>, so <math><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></math> and <math><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Thus <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>.

question.question: For the parabola <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>-20</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>, which statement is true?
choices: It opens to the right because <math><mi>p</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math>
It opens to the left because <math><mi>p</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math>
question.explanation: This is horizontal form <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>. Since <math><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-20</mn></math>, <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-5</mn></math>. A negative <math><mi>p</mi></math> in the horizontal form means the parabola opens to the left.

question.question: A parabola has focus <math><mo>(</mo><mn>-2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and directrix <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-3</mn></math>. What is its vertex?
question.explanation: The vertex is halfway between the focus and directrix along the axis of symmetry. Since the directrix is horizontal (<math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-3</mn></math>), the parabola opens vertically and has axis <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-2</mn></math>. The vertex y-coordinate is the midpoint between <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> (focus) and <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-3</mn></math> (directrix): <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>-3</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>-2</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>-1</mn></math>. So the vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>-2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: For the parabola <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, what is the value of <math><mi>p</mi></math> and the directrix?
question.explanation: Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac></math>, so <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>12</mn></mfrac></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. The vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, so the directrix is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>-1</mn></math>.

question.question: Which equation represents a parabola with vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and focus <math><mo>(</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>?
question.explanation: Vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. The focus has the same y-coordinate, so it opens horizontally. For a horizontal parabola, focus is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></math>. Since focus is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, we have <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>-3</mn></math>. Then <math><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>-12</mn></math>, so the equation is <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>-12</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>. Since <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-1</mn></math>, <math><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, matching choice B.

question.question: Which line is the axis of symmetry of the parabola <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>?
question.explanation: The equation is in vertical focus–directrix form, so the axis of symmetry is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi></math>. Since <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>-7</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, we have <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-7</mn></math>. Thus the axis is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-7</mn></math>.

question.question: A point <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math> lies on a parabola whose focus is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and whose directrix is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-1</mn></math>. Which statement best explains why <math><mi>P</mi></math> is on the parabola?
choices: Because <math><mi>P</mi></math> is closer to the focus than to the directrix
Because <math><mi>P</mi></math> is equidistant from the focus and the directrix
Because <math><mi>P</mi></math> is on the axis of symmetry
Because <math><mi>P</mi></math> is the vertex of the parabola
question.explanation: By definition, a parabola is the set of all points equidistant from a fixed point (focus) and a fixed line (directrix). For <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, distance to the focus is <math><mo>|</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> (same x-value). Distance to the line <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-1</mn></math> is <math><mo>|</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>-1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>|</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. The distances match, so <math><mi>P</mi></math> lies on the parabola.

question.question: For the parabola <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>, what are the focus and directrix?
question.explanation: This is vertical form with vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Since <math><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Focus is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Directrix is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>.

question.question: A horizontal parabola has vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and directrix <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-7</mn></math>. Which equation matches this parabola?
question.explanation: For a horizontal parabola, directrix is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>p</mi></math>. With vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and directrix <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-7</mn></math>, solve <math><mn>-7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>-</mo><mi>p</mi></math> to get <math><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Then <math><mn>4</mn><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math> and the equation is <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>-3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>.

question.paragraph: The height (in meters) of a ball thrown upward is modeled by <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, where <math><mi>t</mi></math> is time in seconds.
question.question: What is the maximum height of the ball?
question.explanation: The maximum occurs at the vertex. For <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math>, the vertex time is <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math>, so <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>23</mn></math>.

question.paragraph: The height (in meters) of a ball is modeled by <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.
question.question: At what time does the ball hit the ground (when <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>)? Choose the positive solution.
question.explanation: Solve <math><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Multiply by <math><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and divide by <math><mn>5</mn></math>: <math><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Using the quadratic formula gives <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mn>16</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>12</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mfrac><mn>92</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. This simplifies to <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mn>115</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math>. The positive time is <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>115</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.paragraph: A projectile’s height is modeled by <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></math> (meters).
question.question: In this model, what does the constant term <math><mn>3</mn></math> represent?
choices: <math><mtext>The time when the ball reaches its maximum height</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>The initial height of the ball at </mtext><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>
<math><mtext>The upward speed of the ball at release</mtext></math>
question.explanation: In a quadratic model <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math>, the value <math><mi>c</mi></math> equals <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Here <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, so the ball starts 3 meters above the ground.

question.paragraph: A rectangular pen is built against a wall, so only three sides need fencing. Suppose the total fencing available is <math><mn>60</mn></math> meters. Let <math><mi>x</mi></math> be the length (in meters) of each side perpendicular to the wall, so the third fenced side is <math><mn>60</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></math>.
question.question: Which quadratic function models the area <math><mi>A</mi></math> of the pen in terms of <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Area is <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math>. Expanding gives <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.

question.paragraph: A rectangular pen is built against a wall with <math><mn>60</mn></math> meters of fencing for three sides, so <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.question: What value of <math><mi>x</mi></math> gives the maximum area?
question.explanation: Expand: <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, a downward-opening parabola with <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></math>. The maximum occurs at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math>.

question.paragraph: A pen against a wall uses <math><mn>60</mn></math> meters of fencing for three sides, so <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.question: What is the maximum possible area of the pen?
question.explanation: The maximum occurs at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn></math>. Then the third side is <math><mn>60</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn></math>. So <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>450</mn></math> square meters.

question.paragraph: A rectangular pen is modeled by <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>60</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math>, where <math><mi>x</mi></math> is a length in meters.
question.question: Which set of values is a reasonable domain for <math><mi>x</mi></math> in this context?
question.explanation: Lengths must be nonnegative, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Also the third side is <math><mn>60</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></math>, which must be nonnegative: <math><mn>60</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></math> so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>30</mn></math>. Therefore <math><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>30</mn></math> is reasonable.

question.paragraph: A company models revenue (in dollars) by <math><mi>R</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>120</mn><mi>x</mi></math>, where <math><mi>x</mi></math> is the number of items sold in hundreds.
question.question: How many items (not hundreds) should be sold to maximize revenue?
question.explanation: The maximum occurs at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>120</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>120</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math>. Since <math><mi>x</mi></math> is in hundreds, that is <math><mn>20</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2000</mn></math> items.

question.paragraph: A company models profit (in thousands of dollars) by <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>40</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>100</mn></math>, where <math><mi>x</mi></math> is the number of items sold in thousands.
question.question: How many thousand items should be sold to achieve the maximum profit?
question.explanation: The profit is maximized at the vertex: <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math> thousand items.
