question.paragraph: Profit (in thousands of dollars) is modeled by <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>40</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>100</mn></math> where <math><mi>x</mi></math> is in thousands of items.
question.question: What is the maximum profit (in thousands of dollars)?
question.explanation: The maximum occurs at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>200</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>400</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>300</mn></math> (thousands of dollars).

question.paragraph: Profit (in thousands of dollars) is modeled by <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>40</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>100</mn></math>, where <math><mi>x</mi></math> is the number of items sold in thousands.
question.question: For what positive value of <math><mi>x</mi></math> does the company break even (that is, <math><mi>P</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>)?
question.explanation: Solve <math><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>40</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Divide by <math><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math>: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mn>400</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>200</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mn>600</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>10</mn><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>5</mn><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></math>. The positive solution is <math><mn>10</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></math> (thousand items).

question.paragraph: A ball reaches a maximum height of <math><mn>18</mn></math> meters at time <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> seconds. The ball’s height at release is <math><mn>2</mn></math> meters.
question.question: Which quadratic model (in vertex form) represents the height <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo></math> in meters?
question.explanation: Vertex form is <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></math> with vertex <math><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>)</mo></math>. Here the vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, so <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn></math>. Use <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>: <math><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>18</mn></math>. So <math><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn></math>, giving <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>64</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.paragraph: A revenue model is given in vertex form: <math><mi>R</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>800</mn></math>, where <math><mi>x</mi></math> is the number of units sold.
question.question: What does the vertex tell you in context?

Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, so the vertex gives a maximum. The maximum revenue is <math><mn>800</mn></math> when <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></math>.

question.paragraph: A calculator gives the quadratic regression model <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></math> for a set of data.
question.question: Using this model, what is the predicted value of <math><mi>y</mi></math> when <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>?

Therefore the predicted value is <math><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: Which situation is most naturally modeled by a quadratic function?
choices: <math><mtext>The distance traveled at a constant speed over time</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>The area of a square as a function of its side length</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>The total cost when each item costs the same amount</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>The temperature increasing by the same amount each hour</mtext></math>
question.explanation: If <math><mi>s</mi></math> is the side length of a square, the area is <math><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, which is a quadratic relationship.

question.paragraph: A fireworks rocket is launched from the ground and lands back on the ground after <math><mn>6</mn></math> seconds. Its maximum height is <math><mn>45</mn></math> meters at <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> seconds.
question.question: Which quadratic function models the height <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo></math> in meters?
question.explanation: Since the rocket is on the ground at <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, a factored model is <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. The vertex is halfway between the roots at <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, and <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>45</mn></math>. So <math><mn>45</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>a</mi></math>, giving <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Thus <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.paragraph: The area of a three-sided fenced pen is modeled by <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, where <math><mi>x</mi></math> is in meters.
question.question: What is the average rate of change of the area from <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math> to <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math>?
question.explanation: Average rate of change is <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>-</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>. Compute <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>600</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>200</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>400</mn></math> and <math><mi>A</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1200</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>800</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>400</mn></math>. So the numerator is 0 and the average rate of change is <math><mn>0</mn></math>.

question.paragraph: A ball’s height (in feet) is modeled by <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>32</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></math>.
question.question: What does the coefficient <math><mn>32</mn></math> represent in this context?
choices: <math><mtext>The time when the ball hits the ground</mtext></math>
<math><mtext>The initial upward velocity of the ball</mtext></math>
question.explanation: In the standard projectile model <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math>, the coefficient of <math><mi>t</mi></math> (here <math><mn>32</mn></math>) corresponds to the initial rate of change of height at <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, which is interpreted as the initial upward velocity (in feet per second).

question.question: Marta has 7,500 pesos she will convert to US dollars using a currency exchange service. At this time, the currency exchange rate is 1 peso = 0.075 US dollars. The exchange service will charge Marta a 2% fee on the converted US dollar amount. How many US dollars will Marta receive from the currency exchange after the 2% fee is applied?
question.explanation:
Choice A is correct. At the exchange rate of 1 peso = 0.075 US dollars, 7,500 pesos would be converted to 7,500 × 0.075 = $562.50. However, since Maria pays a 2% fee on the converted US dollar amount, she receives only (100 – 2)%, or 98%, of the converted US dollars, and 562.50 × 0.98 = $551.25.

Choice B is incorrect. This is the number of US dollars Maria would receive if the exchange service did not charge a 2% fee. Choice C is incorrect and may result from a decimal point error made when calculating the conversion to US dollars and from not assessing the 2% fee. Choice D is incorrect and may result from reversing the units of the exchange rate.

question.question: 37 % of the items in a box are green. Of those, 37 % are also rectangular. Of the green rectangular items, 42 % are also metal. Which of the following is closest to the percentage of the items in the box that are not rectangular green metal items?
question.explanation:
Choice C is correct. It's given that 37% of the items in a box are green. Let x represent the total number of items in the box. It follows that 37100x, or 0.37x, items in the box are green. It's also given that of those, 37% are also rectangular. Therefore, 371000.37x, or 0.1369x, items in the box are green rectangular items. It's also given that of the green rectangular items, 42% are also metal. Therefore, 421000.1369x, or 0.057498x, items in the box are rectangular green metal items. The number of the items in the box that are not rectangular green metal items is the total number of items in the box minus the number of rectangular green metal items in the box. Therefore, the number of items in the box that are not rectangular green metal items is x-0.057498x, or 0.942502x. The percentage of items in the box that are not rectangular green metal items is the percentage that 0.942502x is of x . If p% represents this percentage, the value of p is 1000.942502xx, or 94.2502. Of the given choices, 94.25% is closest to the percentage of items in the box that are not rectangular green metal items.

Choice A is incorrect and may result from conceptual or calculation errors.

Choice B is incorrect and may result from conceptual or calculation errors.

Choice D is incorrect and may result from conceptual or calculation errors.

question.question: The table gives the coordinates of two points on a line in the xy-plane. The y-intercept of the line is k-5,b, where k and b are constants. What is the value of b ?
question.explanation: The correct answer is 33 . It’s given in the table that the coordinates of two points on a line in the xy-plane are (k,13) and (k+7,-15). The y-intercept is another point on the line. The slope computed using any pair of points from the line will be the same. The slope of a line, m , between any two points, x1,y1 and x2,y2, on the line can be calculated using the slope formula, m=y2-y1x2-x1. It follows that the slope of the line with the given points from the table, (k,13) and (k+7,-15), is m=-15-13k+7-k, which is equivalent to m=-287, or m=-4. It's given that the y-intercept of the line is (k-5,b). Substituting -4 for m and the coordinates of the points (k-5,b) and (k,13) into the slope formula yields -4=13-bk-k-5, which is equivalent to -4=13-bk-k+5, or -4=13-b5. Multiplying both sides of this equation by 5 yields -20=13-b. Subtracting 13 from both sides of this equation yields -33=-b. Dividing both sides of this equation by -1 yields b=33. Therefore, the value of b is 33 .

question.question: In the xy-plane, the graph of the linear function f contains the points 0,3 and 7,31. Which equation defines f , where y=fx?
choices: fx=28x+34
fx=3x+38
fx=4x+3
fx=7x+3
question.explanation:
Choice C is correct. In the xy-plane, an equation of the graph of a linear function can be written in the form fx=mx+b, where m represents the slope and 0,b represents the y-intercept of the graph of y=fx. It’s given that the graph of the linear function f , where y=fx, in the xy-plane contains the point 0,3. Thus, b = 3 . The slope of the graph of a line containing any two points x1,y1 and x2,y2 can be found using the slope formula, m=y2-y1x2-x1. Since it’s given that the graph of the linear function f contains the points 0,3 and 7,31, it follows that the slope of the graph of the line containing these points is m=31-37-0, or m = 4 . Substituting 4 for m and 3 for b in fx=mx+b yields fx=4x+3.

Choice A is incorrect. This function represents a graph with a slope of 28 and a y-intercept of 0,34.

Choice B is incorrect. This function represents a graph with a slope of 3 and a y-intercept of 0,38.

Choice D is incorrect. This function represents a graph with a slope of 7 and a y-intercept of 0,3.

question.question: The total cost, in dollars, to rent a surfboard consists of a $25 service fee and a $10 per hour rental fee. A person rents a surfboard for t hours and intends to spend a maximum of $75 to rent the surfboard. Which inequality represents this situation?
choices: 10t≤75
10+25t≤75
25t≤75
25+10t≤75
question.explanation:
Choice D is correct. The cost of the rental fee depends on the number of hours the surfboard is rented. Multiplying t hours by 10 dollars per hour yields a rental fee of 10 t dollars. The total cost of the rental consists of the rental fee plus the 25 dollar service fee, which yields a total cost of 25+10t dollars. Since the person intends to spend a maximum of 75 dollars to rent the surfboard, the total cost must be at most 75 dollars. Therefore, the inequality 25+10t≤75 represents this situation.

Choice A is incorrect. This represents a situation where the rental fee, not the total cost, is at most 75 dollars.

Choice B is incorrect and may result from conceptual or calculation errors.

Choice C is incorrect and may result from conceptual or calculation errors.

question.question: What is the equation of the line that passes through the point 0,5 and is parallel to the graph of y = 7 x + 4 in the xy-plane?
question.explanation:
Choice B is correct. The equation of a line in the xy-plane can be written in slope-intercept form y = m x + b , where m is the slope of the line and 0,b is its y-intercept. It’s given that the line passes through the point 0,5. Therefore, b = 5 . It’s also given that the line is parallel to the graph of y = 7 x + 4 , which means the line has the same slope as the graph of y = 7 x + 4 . The slope of the graph of y = 7 x + 4 is 7 . Therefore, m = 7 . Substituting 7 for m and 5 for b in the equation y = m x + b yields y = 7 x + 5 .

Choice A is incorrect. The graph of this equation passes through the point 0,0, not 0,5, and has a slope of 5 , not 7 .

Choice C is incorrect. The graph of this equation passes through the point 0,0, not 0,5.

Choice D is incorrect. The graph of this equation passes through the point 0,7, not 0,5, and has a slope of 5 , not 7 .

question.explanation:

Substituting the x-coordinate and the y-coordinate of choice D, 14 and 0 , for x and y , respectively, in the first inequality in the given system, y≤x+7, yields 0≤14+7, or 0≤21, which is true. Substituting 14 for x and 0 for y in the second inequality in the given system, y≥-2x-1, yields 0≥-214-1, or 0≥-29, which is true. Therefore, the point 14,0 is a solution to the given system of inequalities in the xy-plane.

question.explanation:

question.question: For a certain rectangular region, the ratio of its length to its width is 35 to 10 . If the width of the rectangular region increases by 7 units, how must the length change to maintain this ratio?

question.explanation:

This proportion can be rewritten as 10l=35w, or l=3.5w. If the width of the rectangular region increases by 7 , then the length will increase by some number x in order to maintain this ratio. The value of x can be found by replacing l with l+x and w with w + 7 in the equation, which gives l+x=3.5w+7. This equation can be rewritten using the distributive property as l+x=3.5w+24.5. Since l=3.5w, the right-hand side of this equation can be rewritten by substituting l for 3.5 w , which gives l+x=l+24.5, or x = 24.5 . Therefore, if the width of the rectangular region increases by 7 units, the length must increase by 24.5 units in order to maintain the given ratio.

Choice A is incorrect. If the width of the rectangular region increases, the length must also increase, not decrease.

Choice C is correct. According to the line of best fit, a planetoid with a distance from the Sun of 1.2 AU has a predicted density between and . The only choice in this range is 4.6.

Choices A, B, and D are incorrect and may result from misreading the information in the scatterplot.

question.question:
The table summarizes the distribution of color and shape for 100 tiles of equal area.

If one of these tiles is selected at random, what is the probability of selecting a red tile? (Express your answer as a decimal or fraction, not as a percent.)
question.explanation: The correct answer is 310. It’s given that there are a total of 100 tiles of equal area, which is the total number of possible outcomes. According to the table, there are a total of 30 red tiles. The probability of an event occurring is the ratio of the number of favorable outcomes to the total number of possible outcomes. By definition, the probability of selecting a red tile is given by 30100, or 310. Note that 3/10 and .3 are examples of ways to enter a correct answer.

question.paragraph:
• For each data category, the following bars are shown:
    • no anger (control)
    • high anger
    • low anger
  • The data for the 2 categories are as follows: 
    • Helpfulness of review:
      • no anger (control): 6.75
      • high anger: 6.08
      • low anger: 6.85
    • Attitude toward reviewed product:
      • no anger (control): 2.23
      • high anger: 1.83
      • low anger: 2.15

To understand how expressions of anger in reviews of products affect readers of those reviews, business scholar Dezhi Yin and colleagues measured study participants’ responses to three versions of the same negative review—a control review expressing no anger, a review expressing a high degree of anger, and a review expressing a low degree of anger. Reviewing the data, a student concludes that the mere presence of anger in a review may not negatively affect readers’ perceptions of the review, but a high degree of anger in a review does worsen readers’ perceptions of the review.
question.question: Which choice best describes data from the graph that support the students’ conclusion?
choices: On average, participants’ ratings of the helpfulness of the review were substantially higher than were participants’ ratings of the reviewed product regardless of which type of review participants had seen.

Compared with participants who saw the control review, participants who saw the low-anger review rated the review as slightly more helpful, whereas participants who saw the high-anger review rated the review as less helpful.

Participants who saw the low-anger review rated the review as slightly more helpful than participants who saw the control review did, but participants’ attitude toward the reviewed product was slightly worse when participants saw the low-anger review than when they saw the no-anger review.
Compared with participants who saw the low-anger review, participants who saw the high-anger review rated the review as less helpful and had a less positive attitude toward the reviewed product.
question.explanation:
Choice B is the best answer. The claim is that low anger does not negatively affect readers’ perceptions of the review, while high anger does negatively affect readers’ perceptions of the review. This choice accurately expresses the supporting data from the “helpfulness of review” part of the graph: that low-anger reviews were rated as slightly more helpful than no-anger reviews, while high-anger reviews were rated as less helpful than no-anger reviews.

Choice A is incorrect. This choice does not support the conclusion. The conclusion is only about how participants feel about the review itself—the participants’ ratings of the reviewed product are not relevant. Choice C is incorrect. This choice does not support the conclusion. The conclusion is only about how participants feel about the review itself—the participants’ attitude towards the reviewed product is not relevant. Choice D is incorrect. This choice does not support the conclusion. The conclusion is only about how participants feel about the review itself—the participants’ attitude towards the reviewed product is not relevant.

question.paragraph: “To You” is an 1856 poem by Walt Whitman. In the poem, Whitman suggests that readers, whom he addresses directly, have not fully understood themselves, writing, ______
question.question: Which quotation from “To You” most effectively illustrates the claim?
choices: “You have not known what you are, you have slumber’d upon yourself / all your life, / Your eyelids have been the same as closed most of the time.”
“These immense meadows, these interminable rivers, you are immense / and interminable as they.”
“I should have made my way straight to you long ago, / I should have blabb’d nothing but you, I should have chanted nothing / but you.”
“I will leave all and come and make the hymns of you, / None has understood you, but I understand you.”
question.explanation:
Choice A is the best answer because it presents the quotation that most directly illustrates the claim that Whitman’s poem suggests that its readers haven’t fully understood themselves. This quotation makes that point directly by saying to readers, “You have not known what you are.” The quotation goes on to reinforce this point using a metaphor of sleep, saying that readers have “slumber’d” and that their “eyelids have been the same as closed most of the time.” 

Choice B is incorrect because this quotation doesn’t suggest that readers haven’t fully understood themselves but instead characterizes readers as “immense” and “interminable.” Although immense and interminable things can be difficult to understand, this quotation doesn’t make that point. Choice C is incorrect because this quotation doesn’t suggest that readers haven’t fully understood themselves but instead conveys the speaker’s regret over not having celebrated readers sooner. In fact, this quotation says nothing at all about readers themselves—it’s focused solely on the speaker’s feelings about readers. Choice D is incorrect because this quotation doesn’t suggest that readers haven’t fully understood themselves; instead, this quotation makes the point that the speaker has understood readers and is determined to create “hymns” about them.

question.paragraph: Urbanization, industrialization, and the warming climate create thermal pollution (excess heat) in the shallow subsurface soil. Susanne A. Benz and colleagues analyzed thousands of sites on three continents under one scenario in which surface temperature remains at the current level and under another in which the surface reaches the maximum plausible temperature. They then categorized each site according to the percentage of local home heating needs that could be met using this excess subsurface heat. The team concluded that if surface temperature approaches the maximum plausible level, the percentage of sites where thermal pollution could feasibly contribute to meeting home heating needs will increase.
question.question: Which choice best describes data in the graph that support Benz and colleagues’ conclusion?
choices: Under both temperature conditions, less than 10% of sites were in the up-to-25% group, but at the maximum plausible surface temperature, almost 80% of sites could have all their local heating needs met by thermal pollution.

At current surface temperatures, more than 80% of the sites have no need for supplemental local home heating from subsurface thermal pollution, but at the maximum plausible surface temperature, more than 70% of sites exhibit significantly greater home heating needs.

At current surface temperatures, more than 80% of sites can meet, at most, 25% of local home heating needs with subsurface thermal pollution, but at the maximum plausible surface temperature, more than 80% of sites can meet greater than 25% of local home heating needs.

At current surface temperatures, more than 80% of the sites cannot use subsurface thermal pollution to meet any portion of local home heating needs, but at the maximum plausible surface temperature, that percentage drops below 20%.
question.explanation:
Choice D is the best answer. The researchers concluded that as we approach maximum plausible surface temperatures, there will be a larger percentage of sites where thermal pollution could contribute to meeting home heating needs. By showing that only a small percentage of homes can currently use thermal pollution for home heating, and that this percentage would grow much larger at maximum plausible surface temperatures, this choice supports the researchers’ conclusion.

Choice A is incorrect. We do not know how many sites could have all (i.e., 100%) of their local heating needs met by thermal pollution, as the graph only classifies sites by whether "0%," "Up to 25%," and "More than 25%" of heating needs could be met. Choice B is incorrect. The graph is not depicting need for supplemental heating from thermal pollution, but rather potential to use thermal pollution for supplemental heating. Choice C is incorrect. The graph indicates that, at current surface temperatures, less than 10% of sites can meet 25% of local home heating needs and that more than 80% of sites cannot meet any local home heating needs.

question.question: A relation is given by the set of ordered pairs <math><mo>{</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>}</mo></math>. Is this relation a function?
choices: Yes, because every input <math><mi>x</mi></math> is paired with exactly one output <math><mi>y</mi></math>.
Yes, because every output <math><mi>y</mi></math> is paired with exactly one input <math><mi>x</mi></math>.
No, because the outputs are increasing.
No, because the set has three ordered pairs.
question.explanation: A relation is a function if each input value has only one output value. In <math><mo>{</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>}</mo></math>, the inputs <math><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mn>2</mn></math>, and <math><mn>3</mn></math> each appear once, so it is a function.

question.question: A relation is given by the set of ordered pairs <math><mo>{</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>}</mo></math>. Is this relation a function?
choices: Yes, because it has three outputs.
Yes, because it contains the pair <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
No, because the input <math><mn>1</mn></math> is paired with two different outputs.
No, because the outputs are not consecutive numbers.
question.explanation: A function cannot assign two different outputs to the same input. Here, the input <math><mn>1</mn></math> appears in both <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, so it is not a function.

question.question: Consider the equation <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></math> over the real numbers. Which statement is true?
choices: It is not a function because a square root always gives two outputs.
It is a function with domain <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
It is a function with domain <math><mi>x</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
It is not a function because it fails the vertical line test.
question.explanation: For real numbers, <math><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></math> is defined only when <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. For each allowed input <math><mi>x</mi></math>, the principal square root gives exactly one output, so it is a function on that domain.

question.question: The function <math><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> is undefined for which value of <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: A rational function is undefined where its denominator is zero. Solve <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> to get <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: Find the domain of <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msqrt></math> over the real numbers.
question.explanation: For a real square root, the radicand must be nonnegative: <math><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Thus <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. What is <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>?
question.explanation: Substitute <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> into <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math>: <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math> and <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Find <math><mo>(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>∘</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
question.explanation: Compute inside first: <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Then apply <math><mi>g</mi></math>: <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> and <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Which is the correct simplified form of <math><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>∘</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math>?
question.explanation: By definition, <math><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>∘</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>)</mo></math>. Since <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, substitute into <math><mi>f</mi></math>: <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>.

question.question: If <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, solve <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> for <math><mi>x</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Solve <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> to get <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. Therefore <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>±</mi><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: Does the relation given by the equation <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> represent <math><mi>y</mi></math> as a function of <math><mi>x</mi></math> over the real numbers?
choices: Yes, because for each <math><mi>x</mi></math> there is exactly one <math><mi>y</mi></math>.
Yes, because it passes the vertical line test.
No, because for some <math><mi>x</mi></math> values there are two corresponding <math><mi>y</mi></math> values.
No, because the equation contains squares.
question.explanation: The equation <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> is a circle. For example, when <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, the equation becomes <math><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, so <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> or <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. That gives two outputs for one input, so it is not a function.

question.question: The relation <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is graphed in the coordinate plane (a sideways parabola). Does it represent <math><mi>y</mi></math> as a function of <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
choices: Yes, because it is a parabola.
Yes, because each <math><mi>y</mi></math> gives exactly one <math><mi>x</mi></math>.
No, because it fails the vertical line test for <math><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
No, because it has no intercepts.
question.explanation: To be <math><mi>y</mi></math> as a function of <math><mi>x</mi></math>, each <math><mi>x</mi></math> must correspond to exactly one <math><mi>y</mi></math>. From <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>, when <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> we get <math><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> so <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> or <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. That means a vertical line at <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> hits the graph twice, so it fails the vertical line test.

question.question: A function is defined by <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>. For what value of <math><mi>x</mi></math> is <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math> undefined?
question.explanation: A rational expression is undefined when its denominator equals zero. Solve <math><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> to get <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: Let <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>. For which value of <math><mi>x</mi></math> is <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>?
question.explanation: Set <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>. Cross-multiply to get <math><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>.

question.question: Suppose <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. What is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>∘</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>?
question.explanation: Compute <math><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>19</mn></math>.

question.question: Which of the following best states the definition of a function?
choices: A relation where each output has exactly one input.
A relation where each input has exactly one output.
A relation where outputs must be positive.
A relation where inputs must be integers.
question.explanation: A function assigns exactly one output value to each input value. That means you cannot have two different outputs for the same input.

question.question: A function <math><mi>r</mi></math> is defined by <math><mi>r</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt></math>. Which set describes the domain of <math><mi>r</mi></math> over the real numbers?
question.explanation: For <math><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt></math> to be real, the radicand must be nonnegative: <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>-1</mn></math>.

question.question: Solve the quadratic equation <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> by factoring.
question.explanation: Factor <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></math> as <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Setting each factor equal to zero gives <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> or <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: Solve the equation <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> by factoring.
question.explanation: Find two numbers that multiply to <math><mn>12</mn></math> and add to <math><mn>7</mn></math>: <math><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><mn>4</mn></math>. Then <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> or <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: Solve <math><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> using the quadratic formula.
question.explanation: For <math><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mn>49</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>, giving <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> or <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Solve the equation <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> by completing the square.
question.explanation: Complete the square: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math>. Set equal to zero: <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math> or <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>.

question.question: Find the vertex of the parabola <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.
question.explanation: For <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math>, the vertex x-coordinate is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, so the vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: For the parabola <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>-</mn><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></math>, does it open upward or downward?
question.explanation: In <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math>, the parabola opens upward if <math><mi>a</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></math> and downward if <math><mi>a</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, so it opens downward.

question.question: Determine the number of real solutions to <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> without solving for <math><mi>x</mi></math>.
question.explanation: Use the discriminant <math><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>10</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, so there are no real solutions.

question.question: A quadratic equation has discriminant <math><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. What does this tell you about the solutions of the equation?
choices: It has exactly two distinct real solutions.
It has exactly one real solution (a repeated root).
It has exactly two complex solutions.
question.explanation: The discriminant <math><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></math> determines the number of real solutions. If <math><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, the quadratic has one real solution that occurs twice (a double root).

question.question: Convert <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math> to vertex form.
question.explanation: Complete the square: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. So vertex form is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: A ball’s height (in feet) is modeled by <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>32</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>48</mn></math>. At what time <math><mi>t</mi></math> does the ball reach its maximum height?
question.explanation: For <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math>, the maximum occurs at <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></math> when <math><mi>a</mi><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></math>, so <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>32</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.

question.question: Using the model <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>32</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>48</mn></math>, what is the maximum height of the ball?
question.explanation: The maximum occurs at <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Substitute: <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>48</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>48</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></math>.

question.question: Solve <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Which answer gives both solutions?
question.explanation: Use <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></math> with <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn></math>. Then <math><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and the discriminant is <math><msup><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>28</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></math>. So <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mn>32</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: A quadratic equation has roots <math><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Which equation has these roots?
question.explanation: If the roots are <math><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, then the factored form is <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Expanding gives <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. However note the sign: <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>15</mn></math>, so the correct expanded equation is <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Among the choices, option A is written as <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, which would correspond to roots <math><mn>5</mn></math> and <math><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Therefore the correct match is option B.

question.question: A quadratic equation has roots <math><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Which equation has these roots?
question.explanation: Roots <math><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math> give factored form <math><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Expanding: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>15</mn></math>, so the equation is <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.

question.question: Solve the quadratic equation <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> by factoring.
question.explanation: Find two numbers that multiply to <math><mn>20</mn></math> and add to <math><mn>9</mn></math>: <math><mn>4</mn></math> and <math><mn>5</mn></math>. Then <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math> or <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>.

question.question: Solve <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>10</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
question.explanation: This is a perfect square trinomial: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>10</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. Setting it equal to zero gives <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> (a double root).

question.question: Solve <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> by factoring.
question.explanation: Factor: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. So <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></math> or <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: Use the quadratic formula to solve <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mn>28</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>±</mo><msqrt><mn>7</mn></msqrt></math>.

question.question: Find the axis of symmetry of the parabola <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>.
question.explanation: For <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></math>, the axis of symmetry is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: What is the vertex of <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></math>?
question.explanation: The vertex x-coordinate is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Substitute into the function: <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn></math>. So the vertex is <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: Solve <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Which statement is true about its solutions?
choices: It has two distinct real solutions.
It has exactly one real solution.
question.explanation: Compute the discriminant: <math><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></math> with <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn><mo><</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, so there are no real solutions.

question.question: For what value of <math><mi>k</mi></math> does the quadratic <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> have exactly one real solution?
question.explanation: Exactly one real solution occurs when <math><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></math>. So <math><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>36</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>k</mi></math>. Set to 0: <math><mn>36</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> so <math><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></math>.

question.question: A ball’s height is modeled by <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>30</mn></math>. What is the maximum height of the ball?
question.explanation: The maximum occurs at <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></math>, so <math><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>20</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Then <math><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>40</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>30</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></math>.

question.question: Which value is the y-intercept of the quadratic <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></math>?
question.explanation: The y-intercept occurs when <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Substitute: <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>0</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>.

question.question: If the x-intercepts of a parabola are <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> and the leading coefficient is <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, which equation could represent the parabola?
question.explanation: Intercept (factored) form is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>_1</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>r</mi><mi>_2</mi><mo>)</mo></math>. With roots <math><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mn>5</mn></math> and <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, the equation is <math><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.

question.question: The quadratic <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>m</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> has exactly one real solution. What is the value of <math><mi>m</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Exactly one real solution means <math><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Here <math><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, <math><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>m</mi></math>, <math><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>. So <math><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>64</mn></math>. Setting to zero gives <math><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></math>, so <math><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>±</mo><mn>8</mn></math>.

question.question: Solve <math><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Factor: <math><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>12</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math>. Setting each factor equal to zero gives <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> or <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: 432 is 96 % of what number?
question.explanation: The correct answer is 450 . Let x represent the number that 432 is 96% of. This can be written as 96100x=432, or 0.96x=432. Dividing both sides of this equation by 0.96 yields x = 450 . Therefore, 432 is 96% of 450 .

question.question: For quality control, a company that manufactures lightbulbs conducted five different trials. In each trial, 500 different lightbulbs were tested. The bar graph above shows the number of defective lightbulbs found in each trial. What is the mean number of defective lightbulbs for the five trials?
question.explanation:
Choice B is correct. The numbers of defective lightbulbs found for the five trials are 4, 7, 1, 3, and 6, respectively. The mean is therefore .

Choice A is incorrect. This is the median number of defective lightbulbs for the five trials. Choice C is incorrect and may result from an arithmetic error. Choice D is incorrect and may result from mistaking the number of trials for the number of defective lightbulbs.

question.question: A gift shop buys souvenirs at a wholesale price of 7.00 dollars each and resells them each at a retail price that is 290% of the wholesale price. At the end of the season, any remaining souvenirs are marked at a discounted price that is 80% off the retail price. What is the discounted price of each remaining souvenir, in dollars?
question.explanation: The correct answer is 4.06 . It's given that the retail price is 290% of the wholesale price of $7.00. Thus, the retail price is $7.00290100, which is equivalent to $7.002.9, or $20.30. It's also given that the discounted price is 80% off the retail price. Thus, the discounted price is $20.301-80100, which is equivalent to $20.300.20, or $4.06.

question.question:
For x>0, the function f is defined as follows:

f(x) equals 201% of x

Which of the following could describe this function?
question.explanation:
Choice D is correct. It's given that for x>0, fx is equal to 201% of x . This is equivalent to fx=201100x, or fx=2.01x, for x>0. This function indicates that as x increases, fx also increases, which means f is an increasing function. Furthermore,  fx increases at a constant rate of 2.01 for each increase of x by 1 . A function with a constant rate of change is linear. Thus, the function f can be described as an increasing linear function.

Choice A is incorrect and may result from conceptual errors.

Choice B is incorrect and may result from conceptual errors.

Choice C is incorrect. This could describe the function fx=2.01x, where fx is equal to 201% of fx-1, not x , for x>0.

question.question: Anita created a batch of green paint by mixing 2 ounces of blue paint with 3 ounces of yellow paint. She must mix a second batch using the same ratio of blue and yellow paint as the first batch. If she uses 5 ounces of blue paint for the second batch, how much yellow paint should Anita use?
choices: 3 ounces more than the amount of yellow paint used in the first batch
1.5 times the amount of yellow paint used in the first batch
1.5 times the amount of blue paint used in the second batch
question.explanation:
Choice D is correct. It’s given that Anita used a ratio of 2 ounces of blue paint to 3 ounces of yellow paint for the first batch. For any batch of paint that uses the same ratio, the amount of yellow paint used will be , or 1.5, times the amount of blue paint used in the batch. Therefore, the amount of yellow paint Anita will use in the second batch will be 1.5 times the amount of blue paint used in the second batch.

Alternate approach: It’s given that Anita used a ratio of 2 ounces of blue paint to 3 ounces of yellow paint for the first batch and that she will use 5 ounces of blue paint for the second batch. A proportion can be set up to solve for x, the amount of yellow paint she will use for the second batch: . Multiplying both sides of this equation by 3 yields , and multiplying both sides of this equation by x yields . Dividing both sides of this equation by 2 yields . Since Anita will use 7.5 ounces of yellow paint for the second batch, this is times the amount of blue paint (5 ounces) used in the second batch.

Choices A, B, and C are incorrect and may result from incorrectly interpreting the ratio of blue paint to yellow paint used.

question.question: The scatterplot above shows the numbers of grams of both total protein and total fat for eight sandwiches on a restaurant menu. The line of best fit for the data is also shown. According to the line of best fit, which of the following is closest to the predicted increase in total fat, in grams, for every increase of 1 gram in total protein?
question.explanation:
Choice C is correct. The predicted increase in total fat, in grams, for every increase of 1 gram in total protein is represented by the slope of the line of best fit. Any two points on the line can be used to calculate the slope of the line as the change in total fat over the change in total protein. For instance, it can be estimated that the points and are on the line of best fit, and the slope of the line that passes through them is , or 1.4. Of the choices given, 1.5 is the closest to the slope of the line of best fit.

Choices A, B, and D are incorrect and may be the result of incorrectly finding ordered pairs that lie on the line of best fit or of incorrectly calculating the slope.

question.question: Each year, the value of an investment increases by 0.49 % of its value the previous year. Which of the following functions best models how the value of the investment changes over time?
question.explanation:
Choice C is correct. Because the value of the investment increases each year, the function that best models how the value of the investment changes over time is an increasing function. It′s given that each year, the value of the investment increases by 0.49% of its value the previous year. Since the value of the investment changes by a fixed percentage each year, the function that best models how the value of the investment changes over time is an exponential function. Therefore, the function that best models how the value of the investment changes over time is an increasing exponential function.

Choice A is incorrect and may result from conceptual errors.

Choice B is incorrect and may result from conceptual errors.

Choice D is incorrect and may result from conceptual errors.

question.question:
Employees working for a customer service line at an electric company recorded all the calls last Monday and noted whether the caller asked for repairs and whether the caller asked about a bill. The results are summarized in the table below.

Asked for
 repairs		 Did not ask
 for repairs		 Total
Asked

If a caller last Monday who asked about his or her bill is selected at random, which of the following is closest to the probability that the customer also asked for repairs?
question.explanation:
Choice B is correct. According to the table, a total of 671 customers asked about a bill. Of these, 48 also asked for repairs. Therefore, if a customer who asked about a bill is selected at random, the probability that the customer also asked for repairs is .

Choice A is incorrect. This is the probability that a customer selected at random from all customers who called on Monday both asked for repairs and asked about a bill. Choice C is incorrect. Choice D is incorrect. This is the probability that a customer selected at random from those who asked for repairs also asked about a bill.

question.question: Simplify the expression <math><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>·</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></math> assuming <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Use exponent rules: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>·</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>8</mn></msup></math>. Then divide: <math><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>8</mn></msup><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup></math>.

question.question: Evaluate and compare the expressions <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></msup></math> and <math><mrow><mo>-</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></math>. What are their values, in order?
question.explanation: Parentheses change the base. <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>81</mn></math> because an even power makes it positive. But <math><mrow><mo>-</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>81</mn></mrow></math> because the negative sign is outside the exponent.

question.question: Simplify <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> assuming <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mi>y</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Apply power rules: <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><msup><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup></math>, and <math><msup><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Multiply them to get <math><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

question.question: Simplify <math><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac></math> assuming <math><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Combine the <math><mi>b</mi></math> powers: <math><mfrac><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>-</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>6</mn></msup></math>. Also <math><msup><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mfrac></math>. So the expression becomes <math><mfrac><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Rewrite <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup></mfrac></math> using a negative exponent.
question.explanation: By definition, <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup></mfrac></math> (for <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>).

question.question: Simplify <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> assuming <math><mi>a</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mi>b</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
question.explanation: A negative exponent inverts the base: <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mi>b</mi><mi>a</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.

question.question: Solve for <math><mi>x</mi></math>: <math><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>125</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Rewrite <math><mn>125</mn></math> as a power of <math><mn>5</mn></math>: <math><mn>125</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></math>. With the same base, set exponents equal: <math><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>, so <math><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math> and <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: Simplify the radical <math><msqrt><mn>98</mn></msqrt></math> by factoring out the largest perfect square.
question.explanation: Factor <math><mn>98</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Then <math><msqrt><mn>98</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>49</mn></msqrt><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></math>.

question.question: Simplify <math><msqrt><mn>50</mn></msqrt></math> completely.
question.explanation: Write <math><mn>50</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>·</mo><mn>2</mn></math>. Then <math><msqrt><mn>50</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>25</mn></msqrt><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></math>.

question.question: Simplify <math><mfrac><msqrt><mn>72</mn></msqrt><msqrt><mn>8</mn></msqrt></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: Combine under one radical: <math><mfrac><msqrt><mn>72</mn></msqrt><msqrt><mn>8</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mfrac><mn>72</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>9</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math>.

question.question: Rationalize the denominator: <math><mfrac><mn>7</mn><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: Multiply by <math><mfrac><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mfrac></math>: <math><mfrac><mn>7</mn><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>·</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Rationalize the denominator: <math><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></math>.
question.explanation: Multiply by the conjugate <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></math>. The denominator becomes <math><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mo>(</mo><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo><msup><mo></mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>. So the rationalized form is <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> (which could simplify further to <math><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt><mo>)</mo></mrow></math>).

question.question: Rewrite <math><msqrt><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup></msqrt></math> using a rational exponent.
question.explanation: A square root is a power of <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. So <math><msqrt><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup></msqrt><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup></math>.

question.question: Simplify <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>·</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup></math> assuming <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Add exponents with the same base: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>·</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.

question.question: Solve for <math><mi>x</mi></math>: <math><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>. Which expression correctly represents <math><mi>x</mi></math>?
question.explanation: Take natural logs: <math><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>⇒</mo><mi>ln</mi><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mn>7</mn></math>. Use <math><mi>ln</mi><msup><mi>a</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>ln</mi><mi>a</mi></math>: <math><mi>x</mi><mi>ln</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>ln</mi><mn>7</mn></math>. So <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mn>7</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>.

question.question: If 4x-9=23, what is the value of x?
question.explanation: Choice B is correct. Add 9 to both sides: 4x=32. Divide by 4: x=8.

question.question: A taxi charges a fixed fee of $3 plus $2.50 per mile. Which equation gives the total cost C (in dollars) for m miles?
choices: C=2.5(m+3)
C=3(m+2.5)
question.explanation: Choice B is correct. The variable part is 2.5m and the fixed fee is 3, so C=2.5m+3.

question.question: Which expression is equivalent to 5(x-4)+2x?
question.explanation: Choice A is correct. Distribute: 5(x-4)=5x-20. Then add 2x to get 7x-20.

question.question: What is the value of 2x+3 when x=-4?
question.explanation:
Choice A is correct. Substitute: 2(-4)+3=-8+3=-5. The result is -5, which is choice B, not A.

Therefore, the correct answer is B.

question.question: If (x-1)2=49, what are the possible values of x?
choices: x=8orx=-6
x=6orx=-8
question.explanation: Choice C is correct. Take square roots: x-1=7 or x-1=-7. Solving gives x=8 or x=-6.

question.question: Which equation represents a line with slope -3 and y-intercept 4?
question.explanation: Choice B is correct. In slope-intercept form, y=mx+b, the slope is m and the intercept is b. Here m=-3 and b=4, so y=-3x+4.

question.question: Solve for x: x+53=4.
question.explanation: Choice D is correct. Multiply both sides by 3: x+5=12. Subtract 5: x=7. Therefore the correct answer is A.

question.question: If f(x)=2x-1, what is f(5)?
question.explanation: Choice C is correct. Substitute 5: f(5)=2(5)-1=10-1=9.

question.question: Which equation is equivalent to 2x-35=7?
question.explanation: Choice B is correct. Multiply both sides by 5: 2x-3=35.

question.question: What is the value of k if 5k-2=3k+10?
question.explanation: Choice B is correct. Subtract 3k from both sides: 2k-2=10. Add 2: 2k=12. Divide by 2: k=6.

question.question: A rectangle has perimeter 54 units. Its length is 3 units more than twice its width. What is the width?
question.explanation: Let width be w. Then length is 2w+3. Perimeter: 2(w+2w+3)=54. So 2(3w+3)=54 gives 6w+6=54. Then 6w=48 and w=8. The correct answer is B.

question.question: If 2x-3y=12 and x+y=7, what is the value of y?
question.explanation: Choice D is correct. From x+y=7, x=7-y. Substitute into 2x-3y=12: 2(7-y)-3y=12. Then 14-2y-3y=12, so 14-5y=12. Subtract 14: -5y=-2, so y=25, which is not listed. Therefore the correct answer cannot be D.

question.question: Simplify the expression <math><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></math> assuming <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and <math><mi>y</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Combine exponents by subtraction: <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>-</mo><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></math>. So the result is <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>7</mn></msup></mfrac></math>.

question.question: Evaluate <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></msup></math>.
question.explanation: <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow></math> and <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>. So the sum is <math><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>16</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow></math>.

question.question: Simplify <math><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>27</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup></math> assuming <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>.
question.explanation: A power of <math><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> is a cube root. <math><msup><mn>27</mn><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></math> and <math><msup><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. Multiply to get <math><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.

question.question: Solve for <math><mi>x</mi></math>: <math><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>81</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Rewrite <math><mn>81</mn></math> as <math><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></math>. Then <math><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>.

question.question: Solve for <math><mi>x</mi></math>: <math><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></math>.
question.explanation: Since <math><mn>16</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></math>, we have <math><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></math>, so <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></math>.

question.question: Simplify <math><mfrac><msqrt><mn>12</mn></msqrt><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mfrac></math>.

question.question: If <math><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msup><mo>·</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> for <math><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn></math>, what is <math><mi>k</mi></math>?
